[synonyms: regulation of glycogen breakdown; regulation of glycogen catabolism; regulation of glycogen degradation; regulation of glycogenolysis] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of glycogen catabolic process

intent: starch metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving starch, the most important reserve polysaccharide in plants. It is a glucan consisting of two components, amylose and amylopectin, which are both glucose homopolymers. Starch is synthesized as a temporary storage form of carbon and can be catabolized to produce sucrose. [synonyms: starch metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: starch metabolic process

intent: starch catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of starch, the most important reserve polysaccharide in plants. [synonyms: starch breakdown; starch catabolism; starch degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: starch catabolic process

intent: disaccharide metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving any disaccharide, sugars composed of two monosaccharide units. [synonyms: disaccharide metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: disaccharide metabolic process

intent: sucrose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving sucrose, the disaccharide fructofuranosyl-glucopyranoside. [synonyms: sucrose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: sucrose metabolic process

intent: sucrose biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of sucrose, the disaccharide fructofuranosyl-glucopyranoside. [synonyms: sucrose anabolism; sucrose biosynthesis; sucrose formation; sucrose synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: sucrose biosynthetic process

intent: sucrose catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of sucrose, the disaccharide fructofuranosyl-glucopyranoside. [synonyms: sucrose breakdown; sucrose catabolism; sucrose degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: sucrose catabolic process

intent: lactose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving lactose, the disaccharide galactopyranosyl-glucose. [synonyms: lactose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: lactose metabolic process

intent: lactose biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lactose, the disaccharide galactopyranosyl-glucose. [synonyms: lactose anabolism; lactose biosynthesis; lactose formation; lactose synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: lactose biosynthetic process

intent: lactose catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of lactose, the disaccharide galactopyranosyl-glucose. [synonyms: lactose breakdown; lactose catabolism; lactose degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: lactose catabolic process

intent: trehalose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving trehalose, a disaccharide that consists of two molecules of glucose and is isomeric with sucrose. [synonyms: mycose metabolic process; mycose metabolism; mykose metabolic process; mykose metabolism; trehalose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: trehalose metabolic process

intent: trehalose biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of trehalose, a disaccharide that consists of two molecules of glucose and is isomeric with sucrose. [synonyms: mycose biosynthesis; mycose biosynthetic process; mykose biosynthesis; mykose biosynthetic process; trehalose anabolism; trehalose biosynthesis; trehalose formation; trehalose synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: trehalose biosynthetic process

intent: trehalose catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of trehalose, a disaccharide that consists of two molecules of glucose and is isomeric with sucrose. [synonyms: mycose catabolic process; mycose catabolism; mykose catabolic process; mykose catabolism; trehalose breakdown; trehalose catabolism; trehalose degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: trehalose catabolic process

intent: melibiose catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of melibiose, the disaccharide 6-O-alpha-D-galactopyranosyl-D-glucose. [synonyms: melibiose breakdown; melibiose catabolism; melibiose degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: melibiose catabolic process

intent: monosaccharide metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving monosaccharides, the simplest carbohydrates. They are polyhydric alcohols containing either an aldehyde or a keto group and between three to ten or more carbon atoms. They form the constitutional repeating units of oligo- and polysaccharides. [synonyms: monosaccharide metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: monosaccharide metabolic process

intent: xylulose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving xylulose, the ketopentose threo-2-pentulose. [synonyms: xylulose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: xylulose metabolic process

intent: xylulose catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of xylulose, the ketopentose threo-2-pentulose. [synonyms: xylulose breakdown; xylulose catabolism; xylulose degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: xylulose catabolic process

intent: xylulose biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of xylulose, the ketopentose threo-2-pentulose. [synonyms: xylulose anabolism; xylulose biosynthesis; xylulose formation; xylulose synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: xylulose biosynthetic process

intent: fructose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving fructose, the ketohexose arabino-2-hexulose. Fructose exists in a open chain form or as a ring compound. D-fructose is the sweetest of the sugars and is found free in a large number of fruits and honey. [synonyms: fructose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: fructose metabolic process

intent: fructose catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of fructose, the ketohexose arabino-2-hexulose. [synonyms: fructose breakdown; fructose catabolism; fructose degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: fructose catabolic process

intent: fructose 6-phosphate metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving fructose 6-phosphate, also known as F6P. The D-enantiomer is an important intermediate in glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, and fructose metabolism. [synonyms: fructose 6-phosphate metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: fructose 6-phosphate metabolic process

intent: fructose 2,6-bisphosphate metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving fructose 2,6-bisphosphate. The D enantiomer is an important regulator of the glycolytic and gluconeogenic pathways. It inhibits fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase and activates phosphofructokinase. [synonyms: fructose 2,6-bisphosphate metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: fructose 2,6-bisphosphate metabolic process

intent: fucose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving fucose, or 6-deoxygalactose, which has two enantiomers, D-fucose and L-fucose. [synonyms: fucose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: fucose metabolic process

intent: L-fucose biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of L-fucose (6-deoxy-L-galactose). [synonyms: L-fucose anabolism; L-fucose biosynthesis; L-fucose formation; L-fucose synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: L-fucose biosynthetic process

intent: glucose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving glucose, the aldohexose gluco-hexose. D-glucose is dextrorotatory and is sometimes known as dextrose; it is an important source of energy for living organisms and is found free as well as combined in homo- and hetero-oligosaccharides and polysaccharides. [synonyms: cellular glucose metabolic process; glucose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: glucose metabolic process

intent: glucose catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of glucose, the aldohexose gluco-hexose. [synonyms: glucose breakdown; glucose catabolism; glucose degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: glucose catabolic process

intent: glucose 1-phosphate phosphorylation - The process of introducing a phosphate group into glucose 1-phosphate to produce glucose bisphosphate. (GO biological_process)
name: glucose 1-phosphate phosphorylation

intent: UDP-alpha-D-glucose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving UDP-alpha-D-glucose, a substance composed of alpha-D-glucose in glycosidic linkage with uridine diphosphate. [synonyms: UDP-glucose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: UDP-alpha-D-glucose metabolic process

intent: galactose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving galactose, the aldohexose galacto-hexose. D-galactose is widely distributed in combined form in plants, animals and microorganisms as a constituent of oligo- and polysaccharides; it also occurs in galactolipids and as its glucoside in lactose and melibiose. [synonyms: galactose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: galactose metabolic process

intent: mannose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving mannose, the aldohexose manno-hexose, the C-2 epimer of glucose. The D-(+)-form is widely distributed in mannans and hemicelluloses and is of major importance in the core oligosaccharide of N-linked oligosaccharides of glycoproteins. [synonyms: mannose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: mannose metabolic process

intent: D-ribose metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving D-ribose (ribo-pentose). As beta-D-ribofuranose, D-ribose forms the glycose group of all ribonucleosides, ribonucleotides and ribonucleic acids, and also of ribose phosphates, various glycosides, some coenzymes and some forms of vitamin B12. [synonyms: D-ribose metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: D-ribose metabolic process

intent: 5-phosphoribose 1-diphosphate biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of 5-phosphoribose 1-diphosphate, also known as 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate. [synonyms: 5-phosphoribose 1-diphosphate anabolism; 5-phosphoribose 1-diphosphate biosynthesis; 5-phosphoribose 1-diphosphate formation; 5-phosphoribose 1-diphosphate synthesis; 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate biosynthesis; 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate biosynthetic process; PRPP biosynthetic process] (GO biological_process)
name: 5-phosphoribose 1-diphosphate biosynthetic process

intent: 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate, the phosphorylated sugar 1-phospho-2-deoxyribose. [synonyms: 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate anabolism; 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate biosynthesis; 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate formation; 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate biosynthetic process

intent: 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of deoxyribose 1-phosphate, the phosphorylated sugar 1-phospho-2-deoxyribose. [synonyms: 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate breakdown; 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate catabolism; 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate degradation; deoxyribose 1-phosphate catabolic process] (GO biological_process)
name: 2-deoxyribose 1-phosphate catabolic process

intent: inositol metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving inositol, 1,2,3,4,5,6-cyclohexanehexol, a growth factor for animals and microorganisms. [synonyms: inositol metabolism; vitamin Bh metabolic process; vitamin Bh metabolism; myo-inositol metabolic process; myo-inositol metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: inositol metabolic process

intent: inositol biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of inositol, 1,2,3,4,5,6-cyclohexanehexol, a growth factor for animals and microorganisms. [synonyms: inositol anabolism; inositol biosynthesis; inositol formation; inositol synthesis; vitamin Bh biosynthesis; vitamin Bh biosynthetic process; myo-inositol biosynthesis; myo-inositol biosynthetic process] (GO biological_process)
name: inositol biosynthetic process

intent: aminoglycan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving aminoglycans, any polymer containing amino groups that consists of more than about 10 monosaccharide residues joined to each other by glycosidic linkages. [synonyms: aminoglycan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: aminoglycan metabolic process

intent: aminoglycan biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of aminoglycans, any polymer containing amino groups that consists of more than about 10 monosaccharide residues joined to each other by glycosidic linkages. [synonyms: aminoglycan anabolism; aminoglycan biosynthesis; aminoglycan formation; aminoglycan synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: aminoglycan biosynthetic process

intent: glycosaminoglycan biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glycosaminoglycans, any one of a group of linear polysaccharides composed of repeating disaccharide units. intent: DNA metabolic process - Any cellular metabolic process involving deoxyribonucleic acid. This is one of the two main types of nucleic acid, consisting of a long, unbranched macromolecule formed from one, or more commonly, two, strands of linked deoxyribonucleotides. [synonyms: cellular DNA metabolism; DNA metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: DNA metabolic process

intent: DNA replication - The cellular metabolic process in which a cell duplicates one or more molecules of DNA. DNA replication begins when specific sequences, known as origins of replication, are recognized and bound by the origin recognition complex, and ends when the original DNA molecule has been completely duplicated and the copies topologically separated. The unit of replication usually corresponds to the genome of the cell, an organelle, or a virus. The template for replication can either be an existing DNA molecule or RNA. (GO biological_process)
name: DNA replication

intent: DNA-templated DNA replication - A DNA replication process that uses parental DNA as a template for the DNA-dependent DNA polymerases that synthesize the new strands. [synonyms: DNA-dependent DNA replication] (GO biological_process)
name: DNA-templated DNA replication

intent: mitochondrial DNA replication - The process in which new strands of DNA are synthesized in the mitochondrion. [synonyms: mtDNA replication; replication of mitochondrial DNA; mitochondrial DNA synthesis; mtDNA synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: mitochondrial DNA replication

intent: DNA topological change - The process in which a transformation is induced in the topological structure of a double-stranded DNA helix, resulting in a change in linking number. [synonyms: DNA underwinding] (GO biological_process)
name: DNA topological change

intent: pre-replicative complex assembly involved in nuclear cell cycle DNA replication - The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form the nuclear pre-replicative complex, a protein-DNA complex that forms at the eukaryotic DNA replication origin and is required for replication initiation. [synonyms: nuclear pre-replicative complex assembly; pre-RC complex assembly; pre-replicative complex assembly; pre-replicative complex formation] (GO biological_process)
name: pre-replicative complex assembly involved in nuclear cell cycle DNA replication

intent: DNA replication, synthesis of primer - The synthesis of a short nucleotide polymer using one strand of unwound DNA as a template. The product is usually a RNA molecule between 4-15 nucleotides long that provides a free 3'-OH that can be extended by DNA-directed DNA polymerases. In certain conditions, for example in response to DNA damage, some primases synthesize a DNA primer. [synonyms: DNA priming; DNA replication, synthesis of DNA primer; DNA replication, synthesis of RNA primer; replication priming] (GO biological_process)
name: DNA replication, synthesis of primer

intent: DNA replication initiation - The process in which DNA-dependent DNA replication is started; it begins when specific sequences, known as origins of replication, are recognized and bound by the origin recognition complex, followed by DNA unwinding. [synonyms: DNA-dependent DNA replication initiation; DNA endoreduplication initiation; DNA re-replication initiation] (GO biological_process)
name: DNA replication initiation

intent: DNA strand elongation involved in DNA replication - The process in which an existing DNA strand is extended by activities including the addition of nucleotides to the 3' end of the strand, complementary to an existing template, as part of DNA replication. [synonyms: DNA replication elongation; DNA strand elongation during DNA replication] (GO biological_process)
name: DNA strand elongation involved in DNA replication

intent: leading strand elongation - The process in which an existing DNA strand is extended continuously in a 5' to 3' direction by activities including the addition of nucleotides to the 3' end of the strand, complementary to an existing template, as part of DNA replication. Leading strand elongation proceeds in the same direction as the replication fork. (GO biological_process)
name: leading strand elongation

intent: lagging strand elongation - The process in which an existing DNA strand is extended in a net 3' to 5' direction by activities including the addition of nucleotides to the 3' end of the strand, complementary to an existing template, as part of DNA replication. Lagging strand DNA elongation proceeds by discontinuous synthesis of short stretches of DNA, known as Okazaki fragments, from RNA primers; these fragments are then joined by DNA ligase. Although each segment of nascent DNA is synthesized in the 5' to 3' direction, the overall direction of lagging strand synthesis is 3' to 5', mirroring the progress of the replication fork. (GO biological_process)
name: lagging strand elongation

intent: DNA replication termination - The process in which DNA replication at a replication fork ceases; occurs when the replication fork reaches a specific termination site or when two replication forks meet. (GO biological_process)
name: DNA replication termination

intent: regulation of DNA replication - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of DNA replication. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of DNA replication

intent: plasmid maintenance - The maintenance of the integrity of extrachromosomal plasmid DNA; includes processes that ensure plasmids are retained in the daughter cells after cell division. (GO biological_process)
name: plasmid maintenance

intent: DNA amplification - The process in which the number of copies of a gene is increased in certain cells as extra copies of DNA are made in response to certain signals of cell development or of stress from the environment. (GO biological_process)
name: DNA amplification

intent: RNA-templated DNA biosynthetic process - A DNA biosynthetic process that uses RNA as a template for RNA-dependent DNA polymerases (e.g. reverse transcriptase) that synthesize the new strand. [synonyms: RNA-dependent DNA biosynthetic process] (GO biological_process)
name: RNA-templated DNA biosynthetic process

intent: premeiotic DNA replication - The replication of DNA that precedes meiotic cell division. [synonyms: DNA replication involved in S phase involved in meiotic cell cycle; DNA replication involved in S-phase involved in meiotic cell cycle; meiotic cell cycle DNA replication; meiotic nuclear cell cycle DNA replication; nuclear cell cycle DNA replication involved in meiotic cell cycle; DNA replication during S phase involved in meiotic cell cycle; meiotic DNA replication; meiotic DNA synthesis; premeiotic DNA synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: premeiotic DNA replication

intent: DNA repair - The process of restoring DNA after damage. Genomes are subject to damage by chemical and physical agents in the environment (e.g. UV and ionizing radiations, chemical mutagens, fungal and bacterial toxins, etc.) and by free radicals or alkylating agents endogenously generated in metabolism. DNA is also damaged because of errors during its replication. A variety of different DNA repair pathways have been reported that include direct reversal, base excision repair, nucleotide excision repair, photoreactivation, bypass, double-strand break repair pathway, and mismatch repair pathway. (GO biological_process)
name: DNA repair

intent: regulation of DNA repair - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of DNA repair. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of DNA repair

intent: transcription-coupled nucleotide-excision repair - The nucleotide-excision repair process that carries out preferential repair of DNA lesions on the actively transcribed strand of the DNA duplex. In addition, the transcription-coupled nucleotide-excision repair pathway is required for the recognition and repair of a small subset of lesions that are not recognized by the global genome nucleotide excision repair pathway. [synonyms: TC-NER; transcription-coupled NER; transcription-coupled repair; TCR] (GO biological_process)
name: transcription-coupled nucleotide-excision repair

intent: base-excision repair - In base excision repair, an altered base is removed by a DNA glycosylase enzyme, followed by excision of the resulting sugar phosphate. The small gap left in the DNA helix is filled in by the sequential action of DNA polymerase and DNA ligase. [synonyms: BER] (GO biological_process)
name: base-excision repair

intent: base-excision repair, AP site formation - The formation of an AP site, a deoxyribose sugar with a missing base, by DNA glycosylase which recognizes an altered base in DNA and catalyzes its hydrolytic removal. (GO biological_process)
name: base-excision repair, AP site formation

intent: base-excision repair, gap-filling - Repair of the damaged strand by the combined action of an apurinic endouclease that degrades a few bases on the damaged strand and a polymerase that synthesizes a 'patch' in the 5' to 3' direction, using the undamaged strand as a template. (GO biological_process)
name: base-excision repair, gap-filling

intent: nucleotide-excision repair - A DNA repair process in which a small region of the strand surrounding the damage is removed from the DNA helix as an oligonucleotide. [synonyms: NER; pyrimidine-dimer repair, DNA damage excision; intrastrand cross-link repair] (GO biological_process)
name: nucleotide-excision repair

intent: pyrimidine dimer repair - The repair of UV-induced T-T, C-T and C-C dimers. (GO biological_process)
name: pyrimidine dimer repair

intent: nucleotide-excision repair, preincision complex stabilization - The stabilization of the multiprotein complex involved in damage recognition, DNA helix unwinding, and endonucleolytic cleavage at the site of DNA damage as well as the unwound DNA. (GO biological_process)
name: nucleotide-excision repair, preincision complex stabilization

intent: nucleotide-excision repair, preincision complex assembly - The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of proteins on DNA to form the multiprotein complex involved in damage recognition, DNA helix unwinding, and endonucleolytic cleavage at the site of DNA damage. [synonyms: nucleotide-excision repair, preincision complex formation] (GO biological_process)
name: nucleotide-excision repair, preincision complex assembly

intent: nucleotide-excision repair, DNA gap filling - Repair of the gap in the DNA helix by DNA polymerase and DNA ligase after the portion of the strand containing the lesion has been removed by pyrimidine-dimer repair enzymes. (GO biological_process)
name: nucleotide-excision repair, DNA gap filling

intent: mismatch repair - A system for the correction of errors in which an incorrect base, which cannot form hydrogen bonds with the corresponding base in the parent strand, is incorporated into the daughter strand. intent: meiotic gene conversion - The cell cycle process in which genetic information is transferred from one helix to another. name: ornithine metabolic process

intent: L-ornithine biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of ornithine, an amino acid only rarely found in proteins, but which is important in living organisms as an intermediate in the reactions of the urea cycle and in arginine biosynthesis. [synonyms: ornithine anabolism; ornithine biosynthesis; ornithine formation; ornithine synthesis; ornithine biosynthetic process] (GO biological_process)
name: L-ornithine biosynthetic process

intent: L-ornithine catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of L-ornithine. [synonyms: ornithine breakdown; ornithine catabolism; ornithine degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: L-ornithine catabolic process

intent: polyamine metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving polyamines, any organic compound containing two or more amino groups. [synonyms: polyamine metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: polyamine metabolic process

intent: polyamine biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of polyamines, any organic compound containing two or more amino groups. [synonyms: polyamine anabolism; polyamine biosynthesis; polyamine formation; polyamine synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: polyamine biosynthetic process

intent: spermine biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of spermine, a polybasic amine found in human sperm, in ribosomes and in some viruses and involved in nucleic acid packaging. [synonyms: spermine anabolism; spermine biosynthesis; spermine formation; spermine synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: spermine biosynthetic process

intent: polyamine catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of polyamines, any organic compound containing two or more amino groups. [synonyms: polyamine breakdown; polyamine catabolism; polyamine degradation; polyamine back-conversion; polyamine interconversion] (GO biological_process)
name: polyamine catabolic process

intent: creatine metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving creatine (N-(aminoiminomethyl)-N-methylglycine), a compound synthesized from the amino acids arginine, glycine, and methionine that occurs in muscle. [synonyms: creatine metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: creatine metabolic process

intent: creatine biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of creatine, N-[amino(imino)methyl]-N-methylglycine. Creatine is formed by a process beginning with amidino group transfer from L-arginine to glycine to form guanidinoacetate, followed by methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to guanidinoacetate; it is then is phosphorylated to form a pool that stores high energy phosphate for the replenishment of ATP during periods of high, or fluctuating energy demand. In animals, most creatine is transported to and used in muscle. [synonyms: creatine anabolism; creatine biosynthesis; creatine formation; creatine synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: creatine biosynthetic process

intent: creatinine catabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of creatinine, 2-amino-1,5-dihydro-1-methyl-4H-imidazol-4-one, an end product of creatine metabolism and a normal constituent of urine. [synonyms: creatinine breakdown; creatinine catabolism; creatinine degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: creatinine catabolic process

intent: phosphocreatine metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving phosphocreatine, a phosphagen of creatine present in high concentration in striated muscle which is synthesized and broken down by creatine phosphokinase to buffer ATP concentration. It acts as an immediate energy reserve for muscle. [synonyms: phosphocreatine metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: phosphocreatine metabolic process

intent: protein targeting - The process of targeting specific proteins to particular regions of the cell, typically membrane-bounded subcellular organelles. Usually requires an organelle specific protein sequence motif. [synonyms: protein sorting along secretory pathway; nascent polypeptide association] (GO biological_process)
name: protein targeting

intent: protein import into nucleus - The directed movement of a protein from the cytoplasm to the nucleus. [synonyms: establishment of protein localization to nucleus; protein import into cell nucleus; protein nucleus import; protein transport from cytoplasm to nucleus] (GO biological_process)
name: protein import into nucleus

intent: NLS-bearing protein import into nucleus - The directed movement of a protein bearing a nuclear localization signal (NLS) from the cytoplasm into the nucleus, across the nuclear envelope. [synonyms: NLS-bearing substrate import into cell nucleus; NLS-bearing substrate import into nucleus; NLS-bearing substrate transport from cytoplasm to nucleus; NLS-bearing substrate-nucleus import] (GO biological_process)
name: NLS-bearing protein import into nucleus

intent: ribosomal protein import into nucleus - The directed movement of a ribosomal protein from the cytoplasm into the nucleus, across the nuclear membrane. At least some ribosomal proteins, including rpl12, uses the importin 11 pathway as a major route into the nucleus. [synonyms: ribosomal protein import into cell nucleus; ribosomal protein transport from cytoplasm to nucleus; ribosomal protein-nucleus import] (GO biological_process)
name: ribosomal protein import into nucleus

intent: protein export from nucleus - The directed movement of a protein from the nucleus into the cytoplasm. [synonyms: protein export from cell nucleus; protein export out of nucleus; protein transport from nucleus to cytoplasm; protein-nucleus export; copper-induced protein export from nucleus] (GO biological_process)
name: protein export from nucleus

intent: protein targeting to membrane - The process of directing proteins towards a membrane, usually using signals contained within the protein. [synonyms: protein membrane targeting; protein-membrane targeting] (GO biological_process)
name: protein targeting to membrane

intent: cotranslational protein targeting to membrane - The targeting of proteins to a membrane that occurs during translation. The transport of most secretory proteins, particularly those with more than 100 amino acids, into the endoplasmic reticulum lumen occurs in this manner, as does the import of some proteins into mitochondria. [synonyms: cotranslational membrane targeting; cotranslational protein membrane targeting; cotranslational protein-membrane targeting] (GO biological_process)
name: cotranslational protein targeting to membrane

intent: SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane - The targeting of proteins to a membrane that occurs during translation and is dependent upon two key components, the signal-recognition particle (SRP) and the SRP receptor. SRP is a cytosolic particle that transiently binds to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) signal sequence in a nascent protein, to the large ribosomal unit, and to the SRP receptor in the ER membrane. [synonyms: SRP-dependent cotranslational membrane targeting; SRP-dependent cotranslational protein-membrane targeting; ER translocation] (GO biological_process)
name: SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane

intent: SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane, docking - The process in which an SRP-bound ribosome forms a complex with the SRP receptor in the ER membrane, allowing the ribosome to bind to the membrane, during cotranslational membrane targeting. [synonyms: protein docking during SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane; SRP-dependent cotranslational membrane targeting, docking; SRP-dependent cotranslational protein-membrane targeting, docking] (GO biological_process)
name: SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane, docking

intent: SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane, translocation - The process during cotranslational membrane targeting wherein proteins move across a membrane. SRP and its receptor initiate the transfer of the nascent chain across the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane; they then dissociate from the chain, which is transferred to a set of transmembrane proteins, collectively called the translocon. Once the nascent chain translocon complex is assembled, the elongating chain passes directly from the large ribosomal subunit into the centers of the translocon, a protein-lined channel within the membrane. The growing chain is never exposed to the cytosol and does not fold until it reaches the ER lumen. [synonyms: SRP-dependent cotranslational membrane targeting, translocation; SRP-dependent cotranslational protein-membrane targeting, translocation; translocation during SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane; ER translocation] (GO biological_process)
name: SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane, translocation

intent: SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane, signal sequence recognition - The process in which SRP binds to the signal peptide in a nascent protein, causing protein elongation to pause, during cotranslational membrane targeting. [synonyms: signal sequence recognition during SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane; SRP-dependent cotranslational membrane targeting, signal sequence recognition; SRP-dependent cotranslational protein-membrane targeting, signal sequence recognition] (GO biological_process)
name: SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane, signal sequence recognition

intent: post-translational protein targeting to endoplasmic reticulum membrane - The targeting of proteins to a membrane that occurs after their translation. Some secretory proteins exhibit posttranslational transport into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lumen: they are synthesized in their entirety on free cytosolic ribosomes and then released into the cytosol, where they are bound by chaperones which keep them in an unfolded state, and subsequently are translocated across the ER membrane. [synonyms: posttranslational endoplasmic reticulum membrane targeting; posttranslational endoplasmic reticulum protein-membrane targeting; posttranslational protein endoplasmic reticulum membrane targeting; posttranslational protein targeting to endoplasmic reticulum membrane; posttranslational protein targeting to ER membrane; SRP-independent endoplasmic reticulum protein-membrane targeting] (GO biological_process)
name: post-translational protein targeting to endoplasmic reticulum membrane

intent: protein retention in ER lumen - The retention in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lumen of soluble resident proteins. Sorting receptors retrieve proteins with ER localization signals, such as KDEL and HDEL sequences or some transmembrane domains, that have escaped to the cis-Golgi network and return them to the ER. Abnormally folded proteins and unassembled subunits are also selectively retained in the ER. [synonyms: maintenance of protein location in ER lumen] (GO biological_process)
name: protein retention in ER lumen

intent: protein targeting to lysosome - The process of directing proteins towards the lysosome using signals contained within the protein. [synonyms: protein-lysosome targeting] (GO biological_process)
name: protein targeting to lysosome

intent: protein targeting to vacuole - The process of directing proteins towards the vacuole, usually using signals contained within the protein. [synonyms: protein vacuolar targeting; protein-vacuolar targeting; protein-vacuole targeting; vacuolar protein sorting] (GO biological_process)
name: protein targeting to vacuole

intent: vacuolar protein processing - Protein processing that takes place in the vacuole. Most protein processing in the vacuole represents proteolytic cleavage of precursors to form active enzymes. [synonyms: vacuolar protein maturation; vacuolar proteolysis] (GO biological_process)
name: vacuolar protein processing

intent: protein targeting to peroxisome - The process of directing proteins towards the peroxisome, usually using signals contained within the protein. [synonyms: protein-peroxisome targeting] (GO biological_process)
name: protein targeting to peroxisome

intent: lipid metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving lipids, compounds soluble in an organic solvent but not, or sparingly, in an aqueous solvent. Includes fatty acids; neutral fats, other fatty-acid esters, and soaps; long-chain (fatty) alcohols and waxes; sphingoids and other long-chain bases; glycolipids, phospholipids and sphingolipids; and carotenes, polyprenols, sterols, terpenes and other isoprenoids. [synonyms: lipid metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: lipid metabolic process

intent: fatty acid metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving fatty acids, aliphatic monocarboxylic acids liberated from naturally occurring fats and oils by hydrolysis. [synonyms: fatty acid metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: fatty acid metabolic process

intent: fatty acid biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a fatty acid, any of the aliphatic monocarboxylic acids that can be liberated by hydrolysis from naturally occurring fats and oils. Fatty acids are predominantly straight-chain acids of 4 to 24 carbon atoms, which may be saturated or unsaturated; branched fatty acids and hydroxy fatty acids also occur, and very long chain acids of over 30 carbons are found in waxes. [synonyms: fatty acid anabolism; fatty acid biosynthesis; fatty acid formation; fatty acid synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: fatty acid biosynthetic process

intent: hexadecanal biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of hexadecanal, the C16 straight chain aldehyde. name: hexadecanal biosynthetic process

intent: fatty acid beta-oxidation - A fatty acid oxidation process that results in the complete oxidation of a long-chain fatty acid. Fatty acid beta-oxidation begins with the addition of coenzyme A to a fatty acid, and occurs by successive cycles of reactions during each of which the fatty acid is shortened by a two-carbon fragment removed as acetyl coenzyme A; the cycle continues until only two or three carbons remain (as acetyl-CoA or propionyl-CoA respectively). (GO biological_process)
name: fatty acid beta-oxidation

intent: neutral lipid metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving neutral lipids, lipids only soluble in solvents of very low polarity. [synonyms: neutral lipid metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: neutral lipid metabolic process

intent: monoacylglycerol biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of monoacylglycerol, any ester of glycerol in which any one of its hydroxyl groups has been acylated with a fatty acid, the other being non-esterified. [synonyms: monoacylglycerol anabolism; monoacylglycerol biosynthesis; monoacylglycerol formation; monoacylglycerol synthesis; monoglyceride biosynthesis; monoglyceride biosynthetic process] (GO biological_process)
name: monoacylglycerol biosynthetic process

name: glycerophospholipid metabolic process

intent: diacylglycerol biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of diacylglycerol, a glyceride in which any two of the R groups (positions not specified) are acyl groups while the remaining R group can be either H or an alkyl group. intent: phosphatidylserine metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving phosphatidylserines, any of a class of glycerophospholipids in which the phosphatidyl group is esterified to the hydroxyl group of L-serine. They are important constituents of cell membranes. [synonyms: phosphatidylserine metabolism] (GO biological_process)

[synonyms: dihydrosphingosine-1-phosphate biosynthesis; dihydrosphingosine-1-phosphate biosynthetic process; sphinganine-1-phosphate anabolism; sphinganine-1-phosphate biosynthesis; sphinganine-1-phosphate formation; sphinganine-1-phosphate synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: sphinganine-1-phosphate biosynthetic process

[synonyms: glycosylceramide metabolism] (GO biological_process)

intent: canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction - An intracellular signaling cassette characterized by the I-kappaB-kinase (IKK)-dependent activation of NF-kappaB, also known as the canonical NF-kappaB signaling cascade. In a resting state, NF-kappaB dimers are bound to I-kappaB proteins, sequestering NF-kappaB in the cytoplasm. Phosphorylation of I-kappaB targets I-kappaB for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, thus releasing the NF-kappaB dimers, which can translocate to the nucleus to bind DNA and regulate transcription. The canonical NF-kappaB pathway is mainly stimulated by proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-1beta, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha, antigen ligands, and toll-like receptors (TLRs). [synonyms: canonical NF-kappaB signaling cascade; I-kappaB kinase/NF-kappaB cascade; I-kappaB kinase/NF-kappaB signal transduction; I-kappaB kinase/NF-kappaB signaling; p50-dependent NF-kappaB signaling; NF-kappaB cascade] (GO biological_process)

intent: activation of NF-kappaB-inducing kinase activity - The stimulation of the activity of NF-kappaB-inducing kinase through phosphorylation at specific residues. [synonyms: activation of NIK activity; positive regulation of NF-kappaB-inducing kinase activity] (GO biological_process)
name: activation of NF-kappaB-inducing kinase activity

intent: I-kappaB phosphorylation - The process of introducing a phosphate group into an inhibitor of kappa B (I-kappaB) protein. Phosphorylation of I-kappaB targets I-kappaB for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, thus releasing bound NF-kappaB dimers, which can translocate to the nucleus to bind DNA and regulate transcription. [synonyms: IkappaB phosphorylation; IKB phosphorylation; inhibitor of kappaB phosphorylation; inhibitor of NF-kappaB phosphorylation] (GO biological_process)

intent: JNK cascade - A MAPK cascade containing at least the JNK (MAPK8) MAP kinase. It starts with the activation of JUN3K (a MAPK3K), which activates JNKK a MAP2K), which in turn activates JNK. The JNK cascade is activated by stress signals, as well as by G protein-coupled receptors, growth factors, and cytokines, and results in cellular responses such as cell proliferation, cell differentiation, apoptosis and inflammation. [synonyms: c-Jun N-terminal kinase cascade; MAPK8 cascade; JNK1 cascade; JNK2 cascade; JNK3 cascade; MAPK10 cascade; MAPK9 cascade; SAPK cascade; stress-activated protein kinase cascade] (GO biological_process)
name: JNK cascade

intent: JUN phosphorylation - The process of introducing a phosphate group into a JUN protein. (GO biological_process)
name: JUN phosphorylation

intent: cell surface receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT - A cell surface receptor signaling pathway in which ligand binding causes the receptor to dimerize, bringing the receptor-associated JAKs into close proximity. The JAKs then phosphorylate and activate each other on tyrosine residues.This leads to the activation of associated STAT protein, causing the STATs to dissociate from the receptor, translocate to the nucleus. The pathway ends with regulation of target gene expression by STAT proteins. [synonyms: JAK-STAT signal transduction; receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT; JAK-STAT cascade] (GO biological_process)
name: cell surface receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT

intent: tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT protein - The process of introducing a phosphate group to a tyrosine residue of a STAT (Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription) protein. [synonyms: tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat1 protein; tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat2 protein; tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat3 protein; tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat4 protein; tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat5 protein; tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat6 protein; tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat7 protein] (GO biological_process)
name: tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT protein

intent: small GTPase-mediated signal transduction - An intracellular signaling cassette in which a small monomeric GTPase relays a signal. [synonyms: small GTPase mediated signal transduction; Ras family protein signal transduction] (GO biological_process)
name: small GTPase-mediated signal transduction

intent: Ras protein signal transduction - An intracellular signaling cassette in which a small monomeric GTPase of the Ras subfamily relays a signal. [synonyms: Ras mediated signal transduction] (GO biological_process)
name: Ras protein signal transduction

intent: Rho protein signal transduction - An intracellular signaling cassette in which a small monomeric GTPase of the Rho subfamily relays a signal. [synonyms: Rho mediated signal transduction] (GO biological_process)
name: Rho protein signal transduction

intent: cell-cell signaling - Any process that mediates the transfer of information from one cell to another. This process includes signal transduction in the receiving cell and, where applicable, release of a ligand and any processes that actively facilitate its transport and presentation to the receiving cell. name: cell-cell signaling

intent: chemical synaptic transmission - The vesicular release of classical neurotransmitter molecules from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of neurotransmitter receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. name: chemical synaptic transmission

intent: neurotransmitter secretion - The regulated release of neurotransmitter from the presynapse into the synaptic cleft via calcium-regulated exocytosis during synaptic transmission. [synonyms: neurotransmitter release; neurotransmitter secretory pathway] (GO biological_process)
name: neurotransmitter secretion

intent: neuron-neuron synaptic transmission - The process of synaptic transmission from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse. [synonyms: nerve-nerve synaptic transmission] (GO biological_process)
name: neuron-neuron synaptic transmission

intent: synaptic transmission, cholinergic - The vesicular release of acetylcholine from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of dopamine receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. This process encompasses both spontaneous and evoked release of neurotransmitter and all parts of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Evoked transmission starts with the arrival of an action potential at the presynapse. [synonyms: cholinergic synaptic transmission] (GO biological_process)
name: synaptic transmission, cholinergic

intent: ensheathment of neurons - The process in which glial cells envelop neuronal cell bodies and/or axons to form an insulating layer. This can take the form of myelinating or non-myelinating ensheathment. [synonyms: ionic insulation of neurons by glial cells] (GO biological_process)
name: ensheathment of neurons

intent: neuromuscular synaptic transmission - The process of synaptic transmission from a neuron to a muscle, across a synapse. (GO biological_process)
name: neuromuscular synaptic transmission

intent: multicellular organism development - The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a multicellular organism over time from an initial condition (e.g. a zygote or a young adult) to a later condition (e.g. a multicellular animal or an aged adult). (GO biological_process)
name: multicellular organism development

intent: gamete generation - The generation and maintenance of gametes in a multicellular organism. A gamete is a haploid reproductive cell. [synonyms: gametogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: gamete generation

intent: pole cell development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the pole cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. (GO biological_process)
name: pole cell development

intent: pole cell fate determination - The cell fate determination process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a pole cell regardless of its environment; upon determination, the cell fate cannot be reversed. (GO biological_process)
name: pole cell fate determination

intent: pole cell formation - Formation of a small group of cells (pole cells) at the posterior pole of the insect blastula. name: pole cell formation

intent: germ cell development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an immature germ cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure (gamete). name: germ cell development

intent: cystoblast division - Any of the rounds of incomplete mitosis undergone by a cystoblast to form a cyst of interconnected cells. [synonyms: cystoblast cell division] (GO biological_process)
name: cystoblast division

intent: spermatogenesis - The developmental process by which male germ line stem cells self renew or give rise to successive cell types resulting in the development of a spermatozoa. [synonyms: generation of spermatozoa] (GO biological_process)
name: spermatogenesis

name: spermatogonial cell division

intent: primary spermatocyte growth - The phase of growth and gene expression that male germ cells undergo as they enter the spermatocyte stage. The cells grow in volume and transcribe most of the gene products needed for the morphological events that follow meiosis. (GO biological_process)
name: primary spermatocyte growth

intent: spermatid development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a spermatid over time, from its formation to the mature structure. [synonyms: spermatid cell development; spermiogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: spermatid development

intent: Nebenkern assembly - Fusion of mitochondria during insect spermatid differentiation to form two masses, which wrap around each other to form a densely packed sphere called the Nebenkern. [synonyms: Nebenkern formation] (GO biological_process)
name: Nebenkern assembly

intent: sperm axoneme assembly - The assembly and organization of the sperm flagellar axoneme, the bundle of microtubules and associated proteins that forms the core of the eukaryotic sperm flagellum, and is responsible for movement. (GO biological_process)
name: sperm axoneme assembly

intent: spermatid nucleus differentiation - The specialization of the spermatid nucleus during the development of a spermatid into a mature male gamete competent for fertilization. [synonyms: spermatid nuclear differentiation] (GO biological_process)
name: spermatid nucleus differentiation

intent: spermatid nucleus elongation - The change in shape of the spermatid nucleus from a spherical structure to an elongated organelle, during the latter part of spermatid differentiation. [synonyms: spermatid nuclear elongation] (GO biological_process)
name: spermatid nucleus elongation

intent: sperm individualization - The resolution of the male germline syncytium or cyst into individual gametes by packaging each spermatid into its own plasma membrane. (GO biological_process)
name: sperm individualization

intent: female gamete generation - Generation of the female gamete; specialised haploid cells produced by meiosis and along with a male gamete takes part in sexual reproduction. (GO biological_process)
name: female gamete generation

intent: germarium-derived egg chamber formation - Construction of a stage-1 egg chamber in the anterior part of the germarium, from the progeny of germ-line and somatic stem cells. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. (GO biological_process)
name: germarium-derived egg chamber formation

intent: germarium-derived oocyte fate determination - The cell fate determination process in which a germarium-derived cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into an oocyte cell regardless of its environment; upon determination, the cell fate cannot be reversed. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: maintenance of oocyte identity; oocyte cell fate determination] (GO biological_process)
name: germarium-derived oocyte fate determination

intent: growth of a germarium-derived egg chamber - Growth of the egg chamber between the time it leaves the germarium and the onset of vitellogenesis. [synonyms: egg chamber growth] (GO biological_process)
name: growth of a germarium-derived egg chamber

intent: vitellogenesis - The production of yolk. Yolk is a mixture of materials used for embryonic nutrition. [synonyms: yolk formation; yolk production] (GO biological_process)
name: vitellogenesis

intent: follicle cell of egg chamber migration - The directed movement of an ovarian follicle cell that takes place during oogenesis. During egg chamber formation, follicle cells migrate to envelop the germ-line cysts and move in between cysts. At stage 10B, follicle cells migrate centripetally between the nurse cells and the oocyte, enclosing the anterior of the egg. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: follicle cell migration] (GO biological_process)
name: follicle cell of egg chamber migration

intent: border follicle cell migration - The directed movement of a border cell through the nurse cells to reach the oocyte. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: border cell migration] (GO biological_process)
name: border follicle cell migration

intent: follicle cell of egg chamber-cell adhesion - The attachment of a somatic follicle cell to another somatic follicle cell or to its substratum, the germline cells. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: ovarian follicle cell adhesion; follicle cell adhesion] (GO biological_process)
name: follicle cell of egg chamber-cell adhesion

intent: ovarian nurse cell to oocyte transport - Transfer of constituents synthesized in the ovarian nurse cells to the oocyte, through the ring canals, as the egg chamber is growing. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: nurse cell to oocyte transport] (GO biological_process)
name: ovarian nurse cell to oocyte transport

intent: female germline ring canal formation - Assembly of the intercellular bridges that connect the germ-line cells of a female cyst. [synonyms: nurse cell ring canal formation; ovarian ring canal formation] (GO biological_process)
name: female germline ring canal formation

intent: nurse cell nucleus anchoring - Attachment of the nurse cell nucleus to the plasma membrane. (GO biological_process)
name: nurse cell nucleus anchoring

intent: chorion-containing eggshell formation - The construction of a chorion-containing eggshell. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: eggshell formation] (GO biological_process)
name: chorion-containing eggshell formation

intent: vitelline membrane formation involved in chorion-containing eggshell formation - Construction of the vitelline membrane portion of a chorion-containing eggshell. name: vitelline membrane formation involved in chorion-containing eggshell formation

intent: egg chorion assembly - Construction of the chorion portion of the egg, which is a protective, noncellular membrane that surrounds the eggs of various animals including insects and fish. [synonyms: eggshell chorion formation; insect chorion formation] (GO biological_process)
name: egg chorion assembly

intent: eggshell chorion gene amplification - Amplification by up to 60-fold of the loci containing the chorion gene clusters. (GO biological_process)
name: eggshell chorion gene amplification

intent: oocyte construction - The synthesis, deposition, and organization of the materials in a cell of an ovary; where the cell can then undergo meiosis and form an ovum. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: oocyte arrangement] (GO biological_process)
name: oocyte construction

intent: oocyte axis specification - The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of an axis in the oocyte. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: oocyte axis determination] (GO biological_process)
name: oocyte axis specification

intent: oocyte dorsal/ventral axis specification - The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of the dorsal/ventral axis of the oocyte. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. name: oocyte dorsal/ventral axis specification

intent: maternal specification of dorsal/ventral axis, oocyte, germ-line encoded - Polarization of the oocyte along the dorsal-ventral axis, by a gene product encoded by cells of the germ line. intent: oocyte nucleus migration involved in oocyte dorsal/ventral axis specification - The directed movement of the oocyte nucleus within the cell as part of the establishment and maintenance of the dorsal/ventral axis of the oocyte. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: oocyte axis determination, oocyte nuclear migration; oocyte axis determination, oocyte nucleus migration; oocyte nuclear migration during oocyte axis determination; oocyte nucleus migration during oocyte axis determination; establishment of oocyte nucleus localisation involved in oocyte dorsal/ventral axis specification; establishment of oocyte nucleus localization involved in oocyte dorsal-ventral axis specification; establishment of oocyte nucleus localization involved in oocyte dorsal/ventral axis determination; establishment of oocyte nucleus localization involved in oocyte dorsal/ventral axis specification; establishment of oocyte nucleus localization involved in oocyte dorsoventral axis specification; oocyte nucleus migration during oocyte axis specification; establishment of localization of oocyte nucleus during oocyte axis determination; establishment of oocyte nucleus localization during oocyte axis determination] (GO biological_process)
name: oocyte nucleus migration involved in oocyte dorsal/ventral axis specification

intent: maternal specification of dorsal/ventral axis, oocyte, soma encoded - Polarization of the oocyte along the dorsal-ventral axis, by a gene product encoded by somatic cells. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: maternal determination of dorsal/ventral axis, oocyte, soma encoded; maternal specification of dorsal-ventral axis, oocyte, soma encoded; maternal specification of dorsoventral axis, oocyte, soma encoded] (GO biological_process)
name: maternal specification of dorsal/ventral axis, oocyte, soma encoded

intent: oocyte anterior/posterior axis specification - Polarization of the oocyte along its anterior-posterior axis. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster. [synonyms: oocyte anterior/posterior axis determination] (GO biological_process)
name: oocyte anterior/posterior axis specification

intent: germ plasm assembly - The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form the germ plasm, the differentiated cytoplasm associated with an oocyte, egg or early embryo that will be inherited by the cells that will give rise to the germ line. name: germ plasm assembly

intent: germ plasm RNA localization - Any process in which RNA is transported to, or maintained in, the germ plasm. [synonyms: establishment and maintenance of germ plasm RNA localization; germ plasm RNA localisation; oocyte pole plasm RNA localization; pole plasm RNA localization] (GO biological_process)
name: germ plasm RNA localization

intent: regulation of germ plasm oskar mRNA localization - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the process in which oskar mRNA is transported to, or maintained in, the germ plasm. [synonyms: regulation of germ plasm oskar mRNA localisation; regulation of oocyte pole plasm oskar mRNA localization; regulation of pole plasm oskar mRNA localization] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of germ plasm oskar mRNA localization

intent: germ plasm protein localization - Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, the germ plasm. [synonyms: establishment and maintenance of germ plasm protein localization; germ plasm protein localisation; oocyte pole plasm protein localization; pole plasm protein localization] (GO biological_process)
name: germ plasm protein localization

intent: negative regulation of oskar mRNA translation - Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the rate that oskar mRNAs are effectively translated into protein. name: negative regulation of oskar mRNA translation

intent: insemination - The introduction of semen or sperm into the genital tract of a female. (GO biological_process)
name: insemination

intent: sperm displacement - The physical displacement of sperm stored from previous mating encounters. (GO biological_process)
name: sperm displacement

intent: peptide pheromone maturation - The generation of a mature, active peptide pheromone via processes unique to its processing and modification. An example of this process is found in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. [synonyms: pheromone processing] (GO biological_process)
name: peptide pheromone maturation

intent: single fertilization - The union of male and female gametes to form a zygote. [synonyms: zygote biosynthesis; zygote formation] (GO biological_process)
name: single fertilization

intent: binding of sperm to zona pellucida - The process in which the sperm binds to the zona pellucida glycoprotein layer of the egg. [synonyms: ZPG binding] (GO biological_process)

intent: acrosome reaction - The discharge, by sperm, of a single, anterior secretory granule following the sperm's attachment to the zona pellucida of the oocyte. (GO biological_process)
name: acrosome reaction

intent: penetration of zona pellucida - The infiltration by sperm of the zona pellucida to reach the oocyte. The process involves digestive enzymes from a modified lysosome called the acrosome, situated at the head of the sperm. (GO biological_process)
name: penetration of zona pellucida

intent: fusion of sperm to egg plasma membrane involved in single fertilization - The binding and fusion of a sperm, with the plasma membrane of the oocyte as part of the process of single fertilization. name: fusion of sperm to egg plasma membrane involved in single fertilization

intent: egg activation - The process in which the egg becomes metabolically active, initiates protein and DNA synthesis and undergoes structural changes to its cortex and/or cytoplasm. (GO biological_process)
name: egg activation

intent: pronuclear fusion - The merging of two pronuclei in a fertilized egg to fuse and produce a single zygotic genome. (GO biological_process)

intent: regulation of mitotic cell cycle - Any process that modulates the rate or extent of progress through the mitotic cell cycle. [synonyms: modulation of preblastoderm mitotic cell cycle progression; preblastoderm mitotic cell cycle modulation; preblastoderm mitotic cell cycle regulation; regulation of preblastoderm mitotic cell cycle progression; regulation of progression through preblastoderm mitotic cell cycle; preblastoderm mitotic cell cycle regulator] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of preblastoderm mitotic cell cycle

intent: regulation of syncytial blastoderm mitotic cell cycle - A cell cycle process that modulates the rate or extent of the progression through the syncytial blastoderm mitotic cell cycle. [synonyms: modulation of syncytial blastoderm cell cycle progression; regulation of progression through syncytial blastoderm mitotic cell cycle; regulation of syncytial blastoderm cell cycle; regulation of syncytial blastoderm cell cycle progression; syncytial blastoderm cell cycle modulation; syncytial blastoderm cell cycle regulation; syncytial blastoderm cell cycle regulator] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of syncytial blastoderm mitotic cell cycle

intent: cellularization - The separation of a multi-nucleate cell or syncytium into individual cells. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster embryo development. (GO biological_process)
name: cellularization

intent: blastoderm segmentation - The hierarchical steps resulting in the progressive subdivision of the anterior/posterior axis of the embryo. (GO biological_process)
name: blastoderm segmentation

intent: tripartite regional subdivision - Subdivision of the embryo along the anterior/posterior axis into anterior, posterior and terminal regions. (GO biological_process)
name: tripartite regional subdivision

intent: zygotic specification of dorsal/ventral axis - The specification of the dorsal/ventral axis of the embryo, through the products of genes expressed in the zygote. name: zygotic specification of dorsal/ventral axis

intent: zygotic determination of anterior/posterior axis, embryo - The specification of the anterior/posterior axis of the embryo by products of genes expressed in the zygote; exemplified in insects by the gap genes, pair rule genes and segment polarity gene cascade. (GO biological_process)

intent: anterior region determination - Specification of the anterior (head and thoracic segments) of the embryo by the gap genes; exemplified in insects by the actions of hunchback gene product. (GO biological_process)

intent: thorax and anterior abdomen determination - Specification of the central (trunk) regions of the embryo by the gap genes; exemplified in insects by the actions of the Kruppel gene product. (GO biological_process)

intent: terminal region determination - Specification of the terminal regions (the two non-segmented ends) of the embryo by the gap genes; exemplified in insects by the actions of huckebein and tailless gene products. (GO biological_process)
name: terminal region determination

intent: periodic partitioning - The regionalization process that divides the spatial regions of an embryo into serially repeated regions. (GO biological_process)
name: periodic partitioning

intent: periodic partitioning by pair rule gene - Allocation of cells to parasegments in the embryo, through the action of overlapping series of pair rule gene activities. (GO biological_process)
name: periodic partitioning by pair rule gene

intent: segment polarity determination - Division of the 14 parasegments of the embryo into anterior and posterior compartments; exemplified by the actions of the segment polarity gene products. (GO biological_process)
name: segment polarity determination

intent: determination of left/right symmetry - The establishment of an organism's body plan or part of an organism with respect to the left and right halves. The pattern can either be symmetric, such that the halves are mirror images, or asymmetric where the pattern deviates from this symmetry. [synonyms: determination of left/right asymmetry] (GO biological_process)
name: determination of left/right symmetry

intent: gastrulation - A complex and coordinated series of cellular movements that occurs at the end of cleavage during embryonic development of most animals. The details of gastrulation vary from species to species, but usually result in the formation of the three primary germ layers, ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. (GO biological_process)
name: gastrulation

intent: ventral furrow formation - Formation of a ventral indentation (furrow) from the blastoderm epithelium, which is internalized to form a tube in the interior of the embryo, marking the start of gastrulation. (GO biological_process)
name: ventral furrow formation

intent: ventral midline determination - The regionalization process in which the area where the ventral midline will form is specified. [synonyms: determination of anterior border of ventral midline; determination of posterior border of ventral midline] (GO biological_process)
name: ventral midline determination

intent: posterior midgut invagination - Formation of a cup-shaped invagination at the posterior end of the embryo, bringing the posterior midgut and hindgut primordia into the interior. (GO biological_process)

intent: anterior midgut invagination - Internalization of the anterior midgut into the interior of the embryo. (GO biological_process)
name: anterior midgut invagination

intent: cephalic furrow formation - Formation of a partial necklace of inturning tissue on the lateral sides of the embryo, along the dorsal-ventral axis. This furrow demarcates head from thorax in the developing protostome. (GO biological_process)
name: cephalic furrow formation

intent: germ-band extension - Elongation of the germ band on the ventral side of the embryo, accompanied by a halving in width. The elongation process pushes the posterior midgut invagination closed and compresses the amnioserosa further. (GO biological_process)
name: germ-band extension

intent: amnioserosa formation - Formation of the amnioserosa, an epithelium that occupies a hole in the embryonic dorsal epidermis. name: amnioserosa formation

intent: segment specification - The process in which segments assume individual identities; exemplified in insects by the actions of the products of the homeotic genes. (GO biological_process)
name: segment specification

intent: specification of segmental identity, head - The specification of the characteristic structures of the head segments following establishment of segment boundaries. Identity is considered to be the aggregate of characteristics by which a structure is recognized. (GO biological_process)
name: specification of segmental identity, head

intent: specification of segmental identity, labial segment - The specification of the characteristic structures of the labial segment following establishment of segment boundaries. Identity is considered to be the aggregate of characteristics by which a structure is recognized. (GO biological_process)
name: specification of segmental identity, labial segment

intent: specification of segmental identity, maxillary segment - The specification of the characteristic structures of the maxillary segment following establishment of segment boundaries. Identity is considered to be the aggregate of characteristics by which a structure is recognized. (GO biological_process)
name: specification of segmental identity, maxillary segment

intent: specification of segmental identity, antennal segment - The specification of the characteristic structures of the antennal segment following establishment of segment boundaries. Identity is considered to be the aggregate of characteristics by which a structure is recognized. (GO biological_process)
name: specification of segmental identity, antennal segment

intent: specification of segmental identity, thorax - The specification of the characteristic structures of the thoracic segments following establishment of segment boundaries. Identity is considered to be the aggregate of characteristics by which a structure is recognized. (GO biological_process)
name: specification of segmental identity, thorax

intent: specification of segmental identity, abdomen - The specification of the characteristic structures of the abdominal segments following establishment of segment boundaries. Identity is considered to be the aggregate of characteristics by which a structure is recognized. (GO biological_process)
name: specification of segmental identity, abdomen

intent: compartment pattern specification - The regionalization process in which embryonic segments are divided into compartments that will result in differences in cell differentiation. [synonyms: compartment specification] (GO biological_process)

intent: anterior compartment pattern formation - The process giving rise to specification of cell identity in the anterior compartments of the segmented embryo. [synonyms: anterior compartment pattern specification] (GO biological_process)
name: anterior compartment pattern formation

intent: posterior compartment specification - The process involved in the specification of cell identity in the posterior compartments of the segmented embryo. (GO biological_process)
name: posterior compartment specification

intent: pattern specification process - Any developmental process that results in the creation of defined areas or spaces within an organism to which cells respond and eventually are instructed to differentiate. [synonyms: pattern biosynthesis; pattern formation] (GO biological_process)
name: pattern specification process

intent: germ-band shortening - The spreading of the amnioserosa from its compressed state to cover the whole of the dorsal surface.
