intent: photosystem I reaction center - A photochemical system containing P700, the chlorophyll a dimer that functions as a primary electron donor. Functioning as a light-dependent plastocyanin-ferredoxin oxidoreductase, it transfers electrons from plastocyanin to ferredoxin. [synonyms: photosystem I reaction centre] (GO cellular_component)
name: photosystem I reaction center

intent: photosystem II reaction center - An integral membrane complex containing P680, the chlorophyll a molecule that functions as a primary electron donor. In the light, functioning as a water-plastoquinone oxidoreductase, it transfers electrons from water to plastoquinone. [synonyms: photosystem II reaction centre] (GO cellular_component)
name: photosystem II reaction center

intent: etioplast prolamellar body - A three dimensional regular lattice found in etioplasts. It is composed of a continuous system of tubules but when exposed to light the symmetrical arrangement is rapidly lost as tubules become pinched off into two dimensional sections of lattice. These for perforated sheets of membrane that move apart, extend and increase, finally establishing the typical granal and intergranal lamellae of the mature chloroplast. (GO cellular_component)
name: etioplast prolamellar body

intent: granum - Distinct stack of lamellae seen within chloroplasts. Grana contain the pigments, electron transfer compounds, and enzymes essential to the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis. (GO cellular_component)
name: granum

intent: chloroplast thylakoid lumen - The cavity enclosed within the chloroplast thylakoid membrane. An example of this component is found in Arabidopsis thaliana. (GO cellular_component)
name: chloroplast thylakoid lumen

intent: elaioplast - A leucoplast in which oil is stored. (GO cellular_component)
name: elaioplast

intent: plasmodesmatal cytoplasmic sleeve - The space between the plasma membrane and the desmotubule of a plasmodesma. [synonyms: plasmodesmatal cytoplasmic annulus] (GO cellular_component)
name: plasmodesmatal cytoplasmic sleeve

intent: plastid ribosome - A ribosome contained within a plastid. (GO cellular_component)
name: plastid ribosome

intent: plasmodesmatal plasma membrane - The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding a plasmodesma. (GO cellular_component)
name: plasmodesmatal plasma membrane

intent: cellulose microfibril - A microfibril composed of cellulose arranged in orthogonal layers. Cellulose is a straight chain polysaccharide composed of B(14) linked glucose subunits. It is a major component of plant cell walls. Higher plant microfibrils are about 10nm in diameter and extremely long in relation to their width. The cellulose molecules are oriented parallel to the long axis of the microfibril in a paracrystalline array, which provides great tensile strength. The microfibrils are held in place by the wall matrix and their orientation is closely controlled by the cell. (GO cellular_component)
name: cellulose microfibril

intent: primary plasmodesma - A plasmodesma that consists of a simple, single channel; found predominantly in young tissue and formed as a function of cell plate formation during cytokinesis. [synonyms: simple plasmodesma] (GO cellular_component)
name: primary plasmodesma

intent: secondary plasmodesma - A plasmodesma with a branched structure, often with many channels leading into a larger central cavity; found in older tissues and usually derived from preexisting primary plasmodesmata. (GO cellular_component)
name: secondary plasmodesma

intent: embryo sac development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the embryo sac over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The process begins with the meiosis of the megasporocyte to form four haploid megaspores. Three of the megaspores disintegrate, and the fourth undergoes mitosis giving rise to a binucleate syncytial embryo sac. The two haploid nuclei migrate to the opposite poles of the embryo sac and then undergo two rounds of mitosis generating four haploid nuclei at each pole. One nucleus from each set of four migrates to the center of the cell. Cellularization occurs, resulting in an eight-nucleate seven-celled structure. This structure contains two synergid cells and an egg cell at the micropylar end, and three antipodal cells at the other end. A binucleate endosperm mother cell is formed at the center. The two polar nuclei fuse resulting in a mononucleate diploid endosperm mother cell. The three antipodal cells degenerate. [synonyms: female gametophyte development] (GO biological_process)
name: embryo sac development

intent: megasporogenesis - The process in which the megasporocyte undergoes meiosis, giving rise to four haploid megaspores in the nucellus. [synonyms: megaspore development; megaspore mother cell meiosis; meiosis of the megasporocyte; meiotic division of the megasporocyte] (GO biological_process)
name: megasporogenesis

intent: pollen development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the pollen grain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The process begins with the meiosis of the microsporocyte to form four haploid microspores. The nucleus of each microspore then divides by mitosis to form a two-celled organism, the pollen grain, that contains a tube cell as well as a smaller generative cell. The pollen grain is surrounded by an elaborate cell wall. In some species, the generative cell immediately divides again to give a pair of sperm cells. In most flowering plants, however this division takes place later, in the tube that develops when a pollen grain germinates. [synonyms: formation of generative and vegetative cells; male gametophyte development; male gametophyte formation; microgametophyte development; pollen grain formation] (GO biological_process)
name: pollen development

intent: microsporogenesis - The process in which the microsporocyte undergoes meiosis, giving rise to four haploid microspores. [synonyms: microspore development] (GO biological_process)
name: microsporogenesis

intent: antipodal cell differentiation - The process in which an uncellularized nucleus cellularizes and acquires the specialized features of an antipodal cell. (GO biological_process)
name: antipodal cell differentiation

intent: embryo sac cellularization - The process in which the eight-nucleate single celled female gametophyte develops into the seven-celled female gametophyte. This mature structure contains two synergid cells and an egg cell at the micropylar end, and three antipodal cells at the other end. A binucleate endosperm mother cell is formed at the center. An example of this process is found in Arabidopsis thaliana. [synonyms: cellularization of the embryo sac; female gametophyte cellularization; megagametophyte cellularization] (GO biological_process)
name: embryo sac cellularization

intent: embryo sac central cell differentiation - The process in which the two uncellularized polar nuclei cellularize, fuse and acquire the specialized features of a mononucleate diploid central cell. [synonyms: embryo sac endosperm mother cell differentiation; female gametophyte central cell differentiation] (GO biological_process)
name: embryo sac central cell differentiation

intent: embryo sac egg cell differentiation - The process in which an uncellularized embryo sac nucleus cellularizes and acquires the specialized features of an egg cell. An example of this process is found in Arabidopsis thaliana. [synonyms: female gametophyte egg cell differentiation; female gamete generation] (GO biological_process)
name: embryo sac egg cell differentiation

intent: megagametogenesis - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the embryo sac over time, from its formation as the megaspore to the mature structure. The process begins when three of the four haploid megaspores disintegrate, and the fourth undergoes mitosis giving rise to a binucleate syncytial embryo sac. The two haploid nuclei migrate to the opposite poles of the embryo sac and then undergo two rounds of mitosis generating four haploid nuclei at each pole. One nucleus from each set of four migrates to the center of the cell. Cellularization occurs, resulting in an eight-nucleate seven-celled structure. This structure contains two synergid cells and an egg cell at the micropylar end, and three antipodal cells at the other end. A binucleate endosperm mother cell is formed at the center. [synonyms: embryo sac development from the megaspore; megagametophyte nucleus division] (GO biological_process)
name: megagametogenesis

intent: embryo sac nuclear migration - The directed movement of an embryo sac nucleus to the pole or center of the cell. [synonyms: embryo sac nucleus migration; female gametophyte nuclear migration; female gametophyte nucleus migration; megagametophyte nuclear migration; megagametophyte nucleus migration] (GO biological_process)
name: embryo sac nuclear migration

intent: synergid differentiation - The process in which an uncellularized nucleus cellularizes and acquires the specialized features of a synergid cell. [synonyms: synergid cell differentiation] (GO biological_process)
name: synergid differentiation

intent: fertilization - The union of gametes of opposite sexes during the process of sexual reproduction to form a zygote. It involves the fusion of the gametic nuclei (karyogamy) and cytoplasm (plasmogamy). [synonyms: syngamy; cell-cell fusion] (GO biological_process)
name: fertilization

intent: double fertilization forming a zygote and endosperm - Fertilization where one of the two sperm nuclei from the pollen tube fuses with the egg nucleus to form a 2n zygote, and the other fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the 3n primary endosperm nucleus and then develops into the endosperm. The ploidy level of the 2n zygote and 3n primary endosperm nucleus is determined by the ploidy level of the parents involved. An example of this component is found in Arabidopsis thaliana. [synonyms: double fertilization] (GO biological_process)
name: double fertilization forming a zygote and endosperm

intent: amyloplast starch grain - Plant storage body for amylose and amylopectin, 1-100um in diameter, and located in amyloplasts. Also contains small amounts of enzymes, amino acids, lipids and nucleic acids. The shape of the grain varies widely amongst species, but is often spherical or disk-shaped. [synonyms: amyloplast starch granule] (GO cellular_component)
name: amyloplast starch grain

intent: chloroplast starch grain - Plant storage body for amylose and amylopectin, 1-100um in diameter, and located in chloroplasts. Also contains small amounts of enzymes, amino acids, lipids and nucleic acids. The shape of the grain varies widely amongst species, but is often spherical or disk-shaped. [synonyms: chloroplast starch granule] (GO cellular_component)
name: chloroplast starch grain

intent: chloroplast stroma - The space enclosed by the double membrane of a chloroplast but excluding the thylakoid space. It contains DNA, ribosomes and some temporary products of photosynthesis. (GO cellular_component)
name: chloroplast stroma

intent: proplastid stroma - The space enclosed by the double membrane of a proplastid. (GO cellular_component)
name: proplastid stroma

intent: chloroplast ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase complex - A complex, located in the chloroplast, containing either both large and small subunits or just small subunits which carries out the activity of producing 3-phosphoglycerate from carbon dioxide and ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate. An example of this component is found in Arabidopsis thaliana. [synonyms: chloroplast RubisCO complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: chloroplast ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase complex

intent: preprophase band - A dense band of microtubules, 1-3 pm wide, that appears just beneath the cell membrane before the start of cell division in the cells of higher plants. It precedes the onset of prophase and then disappears as mitosis begins, yet it somehow determines the plane of orientation of the new cell plate forming in late telophase and marks the zone of the parental cell wall where fusion with the growing cell plate ultimately occurs. (GO cellular_component)
name: preprophase band

intent: chromoplast stroma - The space enclosed by the double membrane of a chromoplast but excluding the photosynthetic material. (GO cellular_component)
name: chromoplast stroma

intent: leucoplast stroma - The space enclosed by the double membrane of a leucoplast. (GO cellular_component)
name: leucoplast stroma

intent: elaioplast stroma - The space enclosed by the double membrane of an elaioplast. (GO cellular_component)
name: elaioplast stroma

intent: etioplast stroma - The space enclosed by the double membrane of an etioplast but excluding the prothylakoid space. It contains the etioplast DNA. (GO cellular_component)
name: etioplast stroma

intent: thylakoid - A membranous cellular structure that bears the photosynthetic pigments in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria. In cyanobacteria thylakoids are of various shapes and are attached to, or continuous with, the plasma membrane. In eukaryotes they are flattened, membrane-bounded disk-like structures located in the chloroplasts; in the chloroplasts of higher plants the thylakoids form dense stacks called grana. Isolated thylakoid preparations can carry out photosynthetic electron transport and the associated phosphorylation. [synonyms: photosynthetic membrane] (GO cellular_component)
name: thylakoid

intent: detection of external stimulus - The series of events in which an external stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: perception of external stimulus] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of external stimulus

intent: detection of abiotic stimulus - The series of events in which an (non-living) abiotic stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: perception of abiotic stimulus] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of abiotic stimulus

intent: detection of light stimulus - The series of events in which a light stimulus (in the form of photons) is received and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: detection of light; perception of light] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of light stimulus

intent: detection of visible light - The series of events in which a visible light stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal. A visible light stimulus is electromagnetic radiation that can be perceived visually by an organism; for organisms lacking a visual system, this can be defined as light with a wavelength within the range 380 to 780 nm. [synonyms: perception of visible light] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of visible light

intent: red, far-red light phototransduction - The sequence of reactions within a cell required to convert absorbed photons from red or far-red light into a molecular signal; the red, far-red light range is defined as having a wavelength within the range 660-730 nm. [synonyms: red-sensitive opsin; phytochrome signaling pathway] (GO biological_process)
name: red, far-red light phototransduction

intent: UV-A, blue light phototransduction - The sequence of reactions within a cell required to convert absorbed photons from UV-A or blue light into a molecular signal; the UV-A, blue light range is defined as having a wavelength within the range of 315 to 400 nm. [synonyms: blue-sensitive opsin; short-wave-sensitive opsin; violet-sensitive opsin] (GO biological_process)
name: UV-A, blue light phototransduction

intent: detection of UV - The series of events in which an ultraviolet radiation (UV light) stimulus is received and converted into a molecular signal. Ultraviolet radiation is electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength in the range of 10 to 380 nanometers. [synonyms: detection of ultraviolet light stimulus; detection of ultraviolet radiation stimulus; detection of UV light stimulus; detection of UV radiation stimulus; perception of UV] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of UV

intent: detection of gravity - The series of events in which a gravitational stimulus is received and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: perception of gravity] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of gravity

intent: detection of chemical stimulus - The series of events in which a chemical stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: chemoperception; detection of chemical substance; chemoreception; perception of chemical stimulus; perception of chemical substance] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of chemical stimulus

intent: detection of nutrient - The series of events in which a nutrient stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: detection of nutrients; nutrient sensing; perception of nutrients] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of nutrient

intent: detection of biotic stimulus - The series of events in which a biotic stimulus, one caused or produced by a living organism, is received and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: perception of biotic stimulus] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of biotic stimulus

intent: detection of virus - The series of events in which a stimulus from a virus is received and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: perception of virus] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of virus

intent: detection of nematode - The series of events in which a stimulus from a nematode is received and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: perception of nematode] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of nematode

intent: detection of insect - The series of events in which a stimulus from an insect is received and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: perception of insect] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of insect

intent: detection of symbiont - The series of events in which a stimulus from a symbiont (an organism living in close physical association with an organism of a different species) is received and converted into a molecular signal. The symbiont is defined as the smaller of the organisms involved in a symbiotic interaction. [synonyms: recognition of symbiont; perception of symbiont] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of symbiont

intent: detection of symbiotic fungus - The series of events in which a stimulus from a symbiotic fungus, a fungus living in close physical association with another organism, is received and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: detection of symbiotic fungi; perception of symbiotic fungi; perception of symbiotic fungus] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of symbiotic fungus

intent: detection of symbiotic bacterium - The series of events in which a stimulus from a symbiotic bacterium, a bacterium living in close physical association with another organism, is received and converted into a molecular signal. [synonyms: detection of symbiotic bacteria; perception of symbiotic bacteria; perception of symbiotic bacterium] (GO biological_process)
name: detection of symbiotic bacterium

intent: response to external stimulus - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an external stimulus. [synonyms: response to environmental stimulus] (GO biological_process)
name: response to external stimulus

intent: tropism - The movement of an organism, or part of an organism, in response to an external source of stimulus, usually toward or away from it. (GO biological_process)
name: tropism

intent: response to biotic stimulus - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a biotic stimulus, a stimulus caused or produced by a living organism. [synonyms: response to biotic stress] (GO biological_process)
name: response to biotic stimulus

intent: response to symbiont - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a symbiont, an organism living with an organism of a different species in close physical association. The symbiont is defined as the smaller of the organisms involved in a symbiotic interaction. [synonyms: response of host to symbiont] (GO biological_process)
name: response to symbiont

intent: response to symbiotic bacterium - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a symbiotic bacterium, a bacterium living in close physical association with another organism. [synonyms: response to symbiotic bacteria] (GO biological_process)
name: response to symbiotic bacterium

intent: response to symbiotic fungus - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a symbiotic fungus, a fungus living in close physical association with another organism. [synonyms: response to symbiotic fungi] (GO biological_process)
name: response to symbiotic fungus

intent: response to wounding - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating damage to the organism. [synonyms: physiological response to wounding] (GO biological_process)
name: response to wounding

intent: response to mechanical stimulus - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a mechanical stimulus. [synonyms: mechanical stimulus response; chemi-mechanical coupling] (GO biological_process)
name: response to mechanical stimulus

intent: response to virus - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a virus. [synonyms: response to viruses] (GO biological_process)
name: response to virus

intent: RNAi-mediated antiviral immune response - A post-transcriptional gene silencing pathway mediated by the action of regulatory RNAs that protects against foreign organism invasion by restricting viral replication and dissemination. [synonyms: RNAi-mediated antiviral immunity; virus induced gene silencing; virus-induced gene silencing; virus-induced PTGS; VIGS; viral gene silencing in virus induced gene silencing; viral triggering of virus induced gene silencing] (GO biological_process)
name: RNAi-mediated antiviral immune response

intent: response to bacterium - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a bacterium. [synonyms: response to bacteria] (GO biological_process)
name: response to bacterium

intent: response to fungus - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a fungus. [synonyms: response to fungi] (GO biological_process)
name: response to fungus

intent: response to nematode - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a nematode. [synonyms: response to nematodes] (GO biological_process)
name: response to nematode

intent: response to insect - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from an insect. [synonyms: response to insects] (GO biological_process)
name: response to insect

intent: plant-type hypersensitive response - The rapid, localized death of plant cells in response to invasion by a pathogen. [synonyms: HR-PCD; plant hypersensitive response; HR] (GO biological_process)
name: plant-type hypersensitive response

intent: systemic acquired resistance - The salicylic acid-mediated response to a pathogen which confers broad spectrum resistance. [synonyms: salicylic acid-dependent systemic resistance] (GO biological_process)
name: systemic acquired resistance

intent: response to abiotic stimulus - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an abiotic (not derived from living organisms) stimulus. [synonyms: response to abiotic stress] (GO biological_process)
name: response to abiotic stimulus

intent: response to gravity - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a gravitational stimulus. [synonyms: response to gravitational stimulus] (GO biological_process)
name: response to gravity

intent: gravitropism - The orientation of plant parts under the stimulation of gravity. [synonyms: geotropism] (GO biological_process)
name: gravitropism

intent: cold acclimation - Any process that increases freezing tolerance of an organism in response to low, nonfreezing temperatures. (GO biological_process)
name: cold acclimation

intent: response to herbicide - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a herbicide stimulus. Herbicides are chemicals used to kill or control the growth of plants. [synonyms: herbicide susceptibility/resistance] (GO biological_process)
name: response to herbicide

intent: response to toxic substance - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a toxic stimulus. [synonyms: detoxification response; toxin resistance; toxin susceptibility/resistance] (GO biological_process)
name: response to toxic substance

intent: response to blue light - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a blue light stimulus. Blue light is electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength of between 440 and 500nm. [synonyms: blue light response; blue-light response; response to blue light stimulus] (GO biological_process)
name: response to blue light

intent: phototropism - The movement of an organism, or part of an organism, in response to a light stimulus, usually toward or away from it. (GO biological_process)
name: phototropism

intent: response to red or far red light - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a red or far red light stimulus. Red light is electromagnetic radiation of wavelength of 580-700nm. Far red light is electromagnetic radiation of wavelength 700-800nm. An example of this response is seen at the beginning of many plant species developmental stages. These include germination, and the point when cotyledon expansion is triggered. In certain species these processes take place in response to absorption of red light by the pigment molecule phytochrome, but the signal can be reversed by exposure to far red light. During the initial phase the phytochrome molecule is only present in the red light absorbing form, but on absorption of red light it changes to a far red light absorbing form, triggering progress through development. An immediate short period of exposure to far red light entirely returns the pigment to its initial state and prevents triggering of the developmental process. A thirty minute break between red and subsequent far red light exposure renders the red light effect irreversible, and development then occurs regardless of whether far red light exposure subsequently occurs. (GO biological_process)
name: response to red or far red light

intent: photomorphogenesis - The control of plant growth, development, and differentiation by the duration and nature of light, independent of photosynthesis. [synonyms: plant development in response to light] (GO biological_process)
name: photomorphogenesis

intent: shade avoidance - Shade avoidance is a set of responses that plants display when they are subjected to the shade of another plant. It often includes elongation, altered flowering time, increased apical dominance and altered partitioning of resources. Plants are able to distinguish between the shade of an inanimate object (e.g. a rock) and the shade of another plant due to the altered balance between red and far-red light in the shade of a plant; this balance between red and far-red light is perceived by phytochrome. (GO biological_process)
name: shade avoidance

intent: response to light intensity - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a light intensity stimulus. (GO biological_process)
name: response to light intensity

intent: photosynthetic acclimation - A response to light intensity in which exposure to medium-intensity light results in increased tolerance to high-intensity light. [synonyms: light acclimatization; photoacclimation] (GO biological_process)
name: photosynthetic acclimation

intent: response to high light intensity - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a high light intensity stimulus. (GO biological_process)
name: response to high light intensity

intent: response to low light intensity stimulus - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a low light intensity stimulus. Low light intensity is defined as a level of electromagnetic radiation at or below 0.1 micromols/m2. (GO biological_process)
name: response to low light intensity stimulus

intent: response to absence of light - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an absence of light stimuli. [synonyms: response to darkness] (GO biological_process)
name: response to absence of light

intent: skotomorphogenesis - The control of plant growth, development, and differentiation in response to growth in darkness. [synonyms: etiolation] (GO biological_process)
name: skotomorphogenesis

intent: photoperiodism - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of detection of, or exposure to, a period of light or dark of a given length, measured relative to a particular duration known as the 'critical day length'. The critical day length varies between species. [synonyms: response to day length; response to night length; response to photoperiod] (GO biological_process)
name: photoperiodism

intent: entrainment of circadian clock - The synchronization of a circadian rhythm to environmental time cues such as light. [synonyms: regulation of circadian rhythm phase] (GO biological_process)
name: entrainment of circadian clock

intent: UV protection - Any process in which an organism or cell protects itself from ultraviolet radiation (UV), which may also result in resistance to repeated exposure to UV. [synonyms: ultraviolet protection; ultraviolet resistance; ultraviolet tolerance; UV resistance; UV tolerance] (GO biological_process)
name: UV protection

intent: response to salt stress - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating an increase or decrease in the concentration of salt (particularly but not exclusively sodium and chloride ions) in the environment. [synonyms: response to ionic osmotic stress; salinity response] (GO biological_process)
name: response to salt stress

intent: thigmotropism - The movement of an organism, or part of an organism, such as leaves or tendrils, in response to a touch stimulus, usually toward or away from it. (GO biological_process)
name: thigmotropism

intent: anatomical structure morphogenesis - The process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized. Morphogenesis pertains to the creation of form. [synonyms: anatomical structure organization; morphogenesis; embryogenesis and morphogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: anatomical structure morphogenesis

intent: photosystem II oxygen evolving complex - A complex, composed of a cluster of manganese, calcium and chloride ions bound to extrinsic proteins, that catalyzes the splitting of water to O2 and 4 H+. In cyanobacteria there are five extrinsic proteins in OEC (PsbO, PsbP-like, PsbQ-like, PsbU and PsbV), while in plants there are only three (PsbO, PsbP and PsbQ). [synonyms: OEC (PSII) complex; oxygen evolving complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: photosystem II oxygen evolving complex

intent: PSII associated light-harvesting complex II, core complex - The pigment-protein complex primarily associated to PSII in higher plants, green algae and cyanobacteria that directly transfers electrons to the reaction center. [synonyms: PSII associated light-harvesting complex II, core complex, LHCIIa subcomplex; PSII associated light-harvesting complex II, core complex, LHCIIc subcomplex; PSII associated light-harvesting complex II, core complex, LHCIId subcomplex] (GO cellular_component)
name: PSII associated light-harvesting complex II, core complex

intent: PSII associated light-harvesting complex II, peripheral complex - Pigment-protein complex primarily associated to PSII in plants, green algae and cyanobacteria. Involved in state transitions that cause migration to PSI under certain environmental conditions such as high light. (GO cellular_component)
name: PSII associated light-harvesting complex II, peripheral complex

intent: plastid organization - A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a plastid. [synonyms: plastid organisation; plastid organization and biogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: plastid organization

intent: response to trehalose - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a trehalose stimulus. [synonyms: response to trehalose stimulus] (GO biological_process)
name: response to trehalose

intent: homogentisate prenyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the transfer of a prenyl group from one compound (donor) to homogentisic acid. (GO molecular_function)
name: homogentisate prenyltransferase activity

intent: homogentisate farnesyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: homogentisic acid + farnesyl diphosphate = 2-methyl-6-farnesylplastoquinol. (GO molecular_function)
name: homogentisate farnesyltransferase activity

intent: homogentisate geranylgeranyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: (2E,6E,10E)-geranylgeranyl diphosphate + H+ + homogentisate = 6-geranylgeranyl-2-methylbenzene-1,4-diol + CO2 + diphosphate. [synonyms: HGGT activity; homogentisate geranylgeranyl transferase activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: homogentisate geranylgeranyltransferase activity

intent: homogentisate solanesyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: all-trans-nonaprenyl diphosphate + H+ + homogentisate = 2-methyl-6-all-trans-nonaprenylbenzene-1,4-diol + CO2 + diphosphate. 2-methyl-6-solanyl-1,4-benzoquinonone is also known as 2-methyl-6-solanesylplastoquinol and all-trans-nonaprenyl diphosphate as solanesyl diphosphate. [synonyms: homogentisate solanyltransferase activity; HST activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: homogentisate solanesyltransferase activity

intent: leaf shaping - The developmental process that pertains to the organization of a leaf in three-dimensional space once the structure has initially formed. [synonyms: leaf structural organization] (GO biological_process)
name: leaf shaping

intent: negative regulation of anion channel activity - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of the anion channel activity. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of anion channel activity

intent: regulation of plant-type hypersensitive response - Any endogenous process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the plant hypersensitive response. [synonyms: regulation of HR; regulation of HR-PCD; regulation of plant hypersensitive response] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of plant-type hypersensitive response

intent: regulation of ethylene biosynthetic process - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of an ethylene biosynthetic process. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of ethylene biosynthetic process

intent: positive regulation of ethylene biosynthetic process - Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of an ethylene biosynthetic process. (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of ethylene biosynthetic process

intent: negative regulation of ethylene biosynthetic process - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of an ethylene biosynthetic process. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of ethylene biosynthetic process

intent: extracellular isoamylase complex - A protein complex whose composition varies amongst species; in rice it probably exists in a homo-tetramer to homo-hexamer form and in Gram negative bacteria as a dimer. Functions in the hydrolysis of alpha-(1,6)-D-glucosidic branch linkages. Isoamylases in animals are localized in the extracellular space. (GO cellular_component)
name: extracellular isoamylase complex

intent: chloroplast isoamylase complex - A protein complex whose composition varies amongst species; in rice it probably exists in a homo-tetramer to homo-hexamer form and in Gram negative bacteria as a dimer. Functions in the hydrolysis of alpha-(1,6)-D-glucosidic branch linkages. Isoamylases in plants are intracellular and probably chloroplast localized. (GO cellular_component)
name: chloroplast isoamylase complex

intent: chromocenter - A region in which centric, heterochromatic portions from more than one chromosomes form a compact structure. (GO cellular_component)
name: chromocenter

intent: perinucleolar chromocenter - A chromocenter adjacent to the nucleolus. (GO cellular_component)
name: perinucleolar chromocenter

intent: regulation of gibberellin biosynthetic process - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of gibberellins. [synonyms: regulation of gibberellic acid biosynthetic process] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of gibberellin biosynthetic process

intent: positive regulation of gibberellin biosynthetic process - Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of gibberellins. [synonyms: positive regulation of gibberellic acid biosynthetic process] (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of gibberellin biosynthetic process

intent: negative regulation of gibberellin biosynthetic process - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of gibberellins. [synonyms: negative regulation of gibberellic acid biosynthetic process] (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of gibberellin biosynthetic process

intent: stomatal complex development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the stomatal complex over time from its formation to the mature structure. The stomatal complex is the stomatal guard cells and their associated epidermal cells. (GO biological_process)
name: stomatal complex development

intent: stomatal complex patterning - The regionalization process of establishing the non-random spatial arrangement of stomatal complex on the surface of a leaf. The stomatal complex is the stomatal guard cells and their associated epidermal cells. (GO biological_process)
name: stomatal complex patterning

intent: stomatal complex formation - The process that gives rise to the stomatal complex. This process pertains to the initial formation of a structure from unspecified parts. The stomatal complex is the stomatal guard cells and their associated epidermal cells. (GO biological_process)
name: stomatal complex formation

intent: guard cell fate commitment - The process in which the developmental fate of a cell becomes restricted such that it will develop into a stomatal guard cell. Guard cells are located in the leaf epidermis and pairwise surround stomatal pores, which allow CO2 influx for photosynthetic carbon fixation and water loss via transpiration to the atmosphere. [synonyms: stomatal cell fate commitment] (GO biological_process)
name: guard cell fate commitment

intent: temperature compensation of the circadian clock - The process in which the circadian clock maintains robust and accurate timing over a broad range of physiological temperatures. The circadian clock is an endogenous 24-h timer found in most eukaryotes and in photosynthetic bacteria. The clock drives rhythms in the physiology, biochemistry, and metabolism of the organisms. [synonyms: regulation of the circadian clock by temperature] (GO biological_process)
name: temperature compensation of the circadian clock

intent: phaseic acid biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of phaseic acid (PA), a catabolite of the plant hormone abscisic acid (ABA). (GO biological_process)
name: phaseic acid biosynthetic process

intent: regulation of chlorophyll biosynthetic process - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of chlorophyll, any compound of magnesium complexed in a porphyrin (tetrapyrrole) ring and which functions as a photosynthetic pigment, from less complex precursors. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of chlorophyll biosynthetic process

intent: cell wall polysaccharide metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving cell wall polysaccharides. (GO biological_process)
name: cell wall polysaccharide metabolic process

intent: cell wall proteoglycan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving cell wall peptidoglycan, a group of glycoproteins that consist of a core-protein backbone O-glycosylated by one or more complex carbohydrates. [synonyms: cell wall proteoglycan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: cell wall proteoglycan metabolic process

intent: double-stranded methylated DNA binding - Binding to double-stranded methylated DNA. Methylation of cytosine or adenine in DNA is an important mechanism for establishing stable heritable epigenetic marks. (GO molecular_function)
name: double-stranded methylated DNA binding

intent: COP9 signalosome assembly - The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a COP9 signalosome. [synonyms: signalosome assembly] (GO biological_process)
name: COP9 signalosome assembly

intent: regulation of G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle - Any signaling pathway that modulates the activity of a cell cycle cyclin-dependent protein kinase to modulate the switch from G2 phase to M phase of the mitotic cell cycle. [synonyms: regulation of mitotic entry] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle

intent: glucomannan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving glucomannan, a polysaccharide composed of D-glucose and D-mannose. The mannose units form the backbone structure (a linear main chain) with the D-glucose as single side-units. [synonyms: glucomannan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: glucomannan metabolic process

intent: galactoglucomannan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving galactoglucomannan, a polysaccharide composed of D-glucose, D-galactose and D-mannose. The mannose units form the backbone structure (a linear main chain) decorated with a mixture of D-glucose and D-galactose side-units. [synonyms: galactoglucomannan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: galactoglucomannan metabolic process

intent: galacturonan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving galacturonan, a pectin polymer containing a backbone of alpha-(1->4)-linked D-galacturonic acid residues. [synonyms: galacturonan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: galacturonan metabolic process

intent: homogalacturonan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving homogalacturonan, a pectin characterized by a backbone of alpha-(1->4)-linked D-galacturonic acid residues that can be methyl-esterified at C-6 and carry acetyl groups on O-2 and O-3. [synonyms: homogalacturonan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: homogalacturonan metabolic process

intent: rhamnogalacturonan I metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving rhamnogalacturonan I (RGI), a branched pectin with a backbone of alternating alpha-(1->2)-linked rhamnose and alpha-(1->4)-linked D-galacturonic acid residues that carries neutral side-chains of predominantly beta-(1->4)-D-galactose and/or alpha-(1->5)-L-arabinose residues attached to the rhamnose residues of the RGI backbone. [synonyms: rhamnogalacturonan I metabolism; RGI metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: rhamnogalacturonan I metabolic process

intent: xylogalacturonan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving xylogalacturonan, a pectin characterized by a backbone of alpha-(1->4)-linked D-galacturonic acid residues substituted on C-3 with beta-D-xylopyranose residues. [synonyms: xylogalacturonan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: xylogalacturonan metabolic process

intent: rhamnogalacturonan I side chain metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving the side chains of the pectin, rhamnogalacturonan I. [synonyms: rhamnogalacturonan I side chain metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: rhamnogalacturonan I side chain metabolic process

intent: pectic galactan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving galactan, a polymer of D-galactosyl units that can be found as a side chain of the pectin rhamnogalacturonan I. [synonyms: pectic galactan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: pectic galactan metabolic process

intent: arabinogalactan protein metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving a cell wall arabinogalactan II glycoprotein, which is composed of a group of core protein of highly varying length and domain complexity. These are O-glycosylated at one or more hydroxyproline residues by arabinogalactan (AG) type II groups, which consist of (1->3)-beta-galactan and (1->6)-beta-linked galactan chains connected to each other by (1->3,1->6)-linked branch points, O-3 and O-6 positions substituted with terminal arabinosyl residues. Also, rhamnose, fucose, glucuronic and galacturonic acid can be present in the glycan structures. [synonyms: arabinogalactan protein metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: arabinogalactan protein metabolic process

intent: classical arabinogalactan protein metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving a cell wall arabinogalactan II glycoprotein, which is composed of a group of core protein containing Hyp, Ala, Ser, Thr and Gly as the major amino acid constituents, and the C-terminus is GPI anchored. [synonyms: classical-arabinogalactan protein metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: classical arabinogalactan protein metabolic process

intent: non-classical arabinogalactan protein metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving a cell wall arabinogalactan II glycoprotein where other amino acids besides Hyp, Ala, Ser, Thr and Gly can be present and grouped into regions, such as a Cys-rich or Asn-rich domains. [synonyms: non-classical arabinogalactan protein metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: non-classical arabinogalactan protein metabolic process

intent: xyloglucan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving xyloglucan, the cross-linking glycan composed of (1->4)-beta-D-glucan backbone substituted at regular intervals with beta-D-xylosyl-(1->6) residues, which is present in the primary cell wall of most higher plants. [synonyms: xyloglucan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: xyloglucan metabolic process

intent: mannan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving mannan, a group of polysaccharides containing a backbone composed of a polymer of D-mannose units. [synonyms: mannan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: mannan metabolic process

intent: glucuronoxylan metabolic process - The chemical reactions and pathways involving xylan, a polymer containing a beta-(1->4)-linked D-xylose backbone decorated with glucuronic acid side units. [synonyms: glucuronoxylan metabolism] (GO biological_process)
name: glucuronoxylan metabolic process

intent: glucuronoxylan biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glucuronoxylan, a polymer containing a beta-1,4-linked D-xylose backbone substituted with glucuronic acid residues. [synonyms: glucuronoxylan anabolism; glucuronoxylan biosynthesis; glucuronoxylan formation; glucuronoxylan synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: glucuronoxylan biosynthetic process

intent: polyprenyldihydroxybenzoate methyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: a 3,4-dihydroxy-5-all-trans-polyprenylbenzoate + S-adenosyl-L-methionine = a 3-methoxy,4-hydroxy-5-all-trans-polyprenylbenzoate + S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + H+. [synonyms: 3,4-dihydroxy-5-polyprenylbenzoic acid O-methyltransferase activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: polyprenyldihydroxybenzoate methyltransferase activity

intent: hydrogen peroxide-mediated programmed cell death - Programmed cell death induced by hydrogen peroxide. Programmed cell death is the cell death resulting from activation of endogenous cellular processes. [synonyms: programmed cell death in response to hydrogen peroxide] (GO biological_process)
name: hydrogen peroxide-mediated programmed cell death

intent: regulation of brassinosteroid biosynthetic process - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of brassinosteroids. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of brassinosteroid biosynthetic process

intent: negative regulation of brassinosteroid biosynthetic process - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of brassinosteroids. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of brassinosteroid biosynthetic process

intent: abscisic acid binding - Binding to abscisic acid, a plant hormone that regulates aspects of plant growth. [synonyms: ABA binding; abscisate binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: abscisic acid binding

intent: methyl-CpNpG binding - Binding to a methylated cytosine/unspecified/guanine trinucleotide. (GO molecular_function)
name: methyl-CpNpG binding

intent: methyl-CpNpN binding - Binding to a methylated cytosine/unspecified/unspecified trinucleotide. (GO molecular_function)
name: methyl-CpNpN binding

intent: fatty acid omega-oxidation - A fatty acid oxidation process in which the methyl group at the end of the fatty acid molecule (the omega carbon) is first oxidized to a hydroxyl group, then to an oxo group, and finally to a carboxyl group. The long chain dicarboxylates derived from omega-oxidation then enter the beta-oxidation pathway for further degradation. (GO biological_process)
name: fatty acid omega-oxidation

intent: seed maturation - A process in seed development that occurs after embryogenesis by which a quiescent state is established in a seed. Seed maturation is characterized by storage compound accumulation, acquisition of desiccation tolerance, growth arrest and the entry into a dormancy period of variable length that is broken upon germination. (GO biological_process)
name: seed maturation

intent: bract development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the bract over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A bract is a leaf, usually different in form from the foliage leaves, subtending a flower or inflorescence. (GO biological_process)
name: bract development

intent: bract morphogenesis - The process in which the anatomical structure of a bract are generated and organized. A bract is a leaf, usually different in form from the foliage leaves, subtending a flower or inflorescence. (GO biological_process)
name: bract morphogenesis

intent: bract formation - The process that gives rise to a bract. This process pertains to the initial formation of a structure from unspecified parts. A bract is a leaf, usually different in form from the foliage leaves, subtending a flower or inflorescence. (GO biological_process)
name: bract formation

intent: carotenoid dioxygenase activity - Catalysis of the oxidative cleavage of carotenoids. [synonyms: carotenoid-cleaving dioxygenase] (GO molecular_function)
name: carotenoid dioxygenase activity

intent: 9,10 (9', 10')-carotenoid-cleaving dioxygenase activity - Catalysis of the oxidative cleavage of carotenoids at the (9, 10) and/or (9', 10') double bond. (GO molecular_function)
name: 9,10 (9', 10')-carotenoid-cleaving dioxygenase activity

intent: cellular response to sulfur starvation - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of deprivation of sulfur. (GO biological_process)
name: cellular response to sulfur starvation

intent: regulation of glucosinolate biosynthetic process - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glucosinolates, substituted thioglucosides found in rapeseed products and related cruciferae. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of glucosinolate biosynthetic process

intent: stomatal lineage progression - The process in which an unspecialized epidermal cell progresses through a series of divisions that culminate in the production of a stomatal complex. (GO biological_process)
name: stomatal lineage progression

intent: guard cell development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the guard cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. (GO biological_process)
name: guard cell development

intent: guard cell morphogenesis - Generation and organization of the polarized cell that is capable of turgor driven movement. [synonyms: guard cell morphogenesis during differentiation] (GO biological_process)
name: guard cell morphogenesis

intent: meristemoid mother cell division - The asymmetric cell division by which a meristemoid mother cells (MMC) give rise to a meristemoid and another cell. The other cell may itself become a MMC or may generate an epidermal cell. Any cell that undergoes this type of division is a MMC. [synonyms: meristemoid division] (GO biological_process)
name: meristemoid mother cell division

intent: guard mother cell differentiation - The process in which a meristemoid acquires the specialized features of a guard mother cell. (GO biological_process)
name: guard mother cell differentiation

intent: nuclear dicing body - A small round nuclear body, measuring 0.2-0.8 microns in diameter that is diffusely distributed throughout the nucleoplasm. Several proteins known to be involved in miRNA processing have been localized to these structures. D-bodies are thought to be involved in primary-miRNA processing and/or storage/assembly of miRNA processing complexes. [synonyms: D body] (GO cellular_component)
name: nuclear dicing body

intent: response to alkaline pH - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a pH stimulus with pH > 7. pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution. [synonyms: response to basic pH; response to alkalinity] (GO biological_process)
name: response to alkaline pH

intent: response to acidic pH - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a pH stimulus with pH < 7. pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution. [synonyms: response to acidity] (GO biological_process)
name: response to acidic pH

intent: vegetative meristem growth - The increase in size or mass of a vegetative meristem, a population of undifferentiated cells in a plant shoot which maintains a continuous balance between the production of stem cells and the incorporation of their derivatives into lateral organ primordia. (GO biological_process)
name: vegetative meristem growth

intent: root meristem growth - The increase in size or mass of a root meristem, a population of undifferentiated cells in a plant root which maintains a continuous balance between the production of stem cells and the incorporation of their derivatives into the growth of the root. (GO biological_process)
name: root meristem growth

intent: inflorescence meristem growth - The increase in size or mass of an inflorescence meristem, a population of undifferentiated cells in a plant shoot which produces small leaves and then floral meristems, which will give rise to flowers. (GO biological_process)
name: inflorescence meristem growth

intent: floral meristem growth - The increase in size or mass of a floral meristem, a population of undifferentiated cells in a plant that gives rise to a flower. (GO biological_process)
name: floral meristem growth

intent: regulation of cell fate commitment - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell fate commitment. Cell fate commitment is the commitment of cells to specific cell fates and their capacity to differentiate into particular kinds of cells. Positional information is established through protein signals that emanate from a localized source within a cell (the initial one-cell zygote) or within a developmental field. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of cell fate commitment

intent: negative regulation of cell fate commitment - Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency or rate of cell fate commitment. Cell fate commitment is the commitment of cells to specific cell fates and their capacity to differentiate into particular kinds of cells. Positional information is established through protein signals that emanate from a localized source within a cell (the initial one-cell zygote) or within a developmental field. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of cell fate commitment

intent: positive regulation of cell fate commitment - Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency or rate of cell fate commitment. Cell fate commitment is the commitment of cells to specific cell fates and their capacity to differentiate into particular kinds of cells. Positional information is established through protein signals that emanate from a localized source within a cell (the initial one-cell zygote) or within a developmental field. (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of cell fate commitment

intent: cell proliferation in dorsal spinal cord - The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of the dorsal spinal cord cell population. (GO biological_process)
name: cell proliferation in dorsal spinal cord

intent: centriole-centriole cohesion - The cell cycle process in which the two centrioles within a centrosome remain tightly paired. (GO biological_process)
name: centriole-centriole cohesion

intent: exit from mitosis - The cell cycle transition where a cell leaves M phase and enters a new G1 phase. M phase is the part of the mitotic cell cycle during which mitosis and cytokinesis take place. [synonyms: exit from mitotic division; mitotic exit] (GO biological_process)
name: exit from mitosis

intent: negative regulation of heart rate - Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency or rate of heart contraction. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of heart rate

intent: positive regulation of heart rate - Any process that activates or increases the frequency or rate of heart contraction. (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of heart rate

intent: light-activated monoatomic ion channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of a monoatomic ion by a channel that opens in response to a light stimulus. (GO molecular_function)
name: light-activated monoatomic ion channel activity

intent: mesenchymal cell proliferation - The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of a mesenchymal cell population. A mesenchymal cell is a cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses, rather than sheets. (GO biological_process)
name: mesenchymal cell proliferation

intent: regulation of mesenchymal cell proliferation - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of mesenchymal cell proliferation. A mesenchymal cell is a cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses, rather than sheets. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of mesenchymal cell proliferation

intent: nerve growth factor receptor activity - Combining with nerve growth factor (NGF), to prevent apoptosis in neurons and promote nerve growth, or to initiate a change in cell activity. [synonyms: beta-nerve growth factor receptor activity; NGF receptor activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: nerve growth factor receptor activity

intent: negative regulation of peptidase activity - Any process that stops or reduces the rate of peptidase activity, the hydrolysis of peptide bonds within proteins. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of peptidase activity

intent: gene expression - The process in which a gene's sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA). This includes the production of an RNA transcript and its processing, as well as translation and maturation for protein-coding genes. (GO biological_process)
name: gene expression

intent: regulation of gene expression - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of gene expression. Gene expression is the process in which a gene's coding sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA). [synonyms: regulation of protein expression; gene regulation; regulation of gene product expression] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of gene expression

intent: regulation of signaling receptor activity - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a signaling receptor activity. Receptor activity is when a molecule combines with an extracellular or intracellular messenger to initiate a change in cell activity. [synonyms: regulation of signalling receptor activity; regulation of receptor activity] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of signaling receptor activity

intent: regulation of gastrulation - Any process that modulates the rate or extent of gastrulation. Gastrulation is the complex and coordinated series of cellular movements that occurs at the end of cleavage during embryonic development of most animals. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of gastrulation

intent: GDP-galactose:mannose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: GDP-beta-L-galactose + alpha-D-mannose 1-phosphate = GDP-alpha-D-mannose + beta-L-galactose-1-phosphate. [synonyms: GDP-L-galactose:mannose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase activity; GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: GDP-galactose:mannose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase activity

intent: GDP-galactose:glucose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: GDP-beta-L-galactose + alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate = beta-L-galactose-1-phosphate + GDP-alpha-D-glucose. [synonyms: GDP-L-galactose:glucose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase activity; GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: GDP-galactose:glucose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase activity

intent: GDP-galactose:myoinositol-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: GDP-L-galactose + myo-inositol 1-phosphate = alpha-L-galactose-1-phosphate + GDP-myoinositol. (GO molecular_function)
name: GDP-galactose:myoinositol-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase activity

intent: gibberellin mediated signaling pathway - The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of gibberellin stimulus. [synonyms: gibberellin-mediated signalling] (GO biological_process)
name: gibberellin mediated signaling pathway

intent: response to sulfur dioxide - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a sulfur dioxide (SO2) stimulus. (GO biological_process)
name: response to sulfur dioxide

intent: chlororespiration - A respiratory electron flow (from NAD(P)H to plastoquinone (PQ) and O2) involving both a nonphotochemical reduction and re-oxidation of PQ pool. (GO biological_process)
name: chlororespiration

intent: stele development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the stele over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The stele is the central column of primary vascular tissue in the root and any tissue that it surrounds. (GO biological_process)
name: stele development

intent: microsporocyte differentiation - The process aimed at the progression of a microsporocyte cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. A microsporocyte is a diploid (2n) cell that undergoes meiosis and forms four haploid (1n) microspores; also called microspore mother cell and, in seed plants, pollen mother cell. [synonyms: pollen mother cell differentiation] (GO biological_process)
name: microsporocyte differentiation

intent: epidermal cell division - Any process resulting in the physical partitioning and separation of an epidermal cell, any of the cells making up the epidermis, into daughter cells. [synonyms: hypodermal cell division] (GO biological_process)
name: epidermal cell division

intent: regulation of epidermal cell division - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the physical partitioning and separation of an epidermal cell into daughter cells. An epidermal cell is any of the cells that make up the epidermis. [synonyms: regulation of hypodermal cell division] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of epidermal cell division

intent: pollen tube reception - An interaction between the pollen tube, part of the male gametophyte, and the female gametophyte (typically the synergid cells), that results in the arrest of pollen tube growth, rupture of the pollen tube and the release of the sperm cells. (GO biological_process)
name: pollen tube reception

intent: histone H3 acetyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + histone H3 = CoA + acetyl-histone H3. [synonyms: H3 histone acetylase activity; H3 histone acetyltransferase activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: histone H3 acetyltransferase activity

intent: histone H4 acetyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + histone H4 = CoA + acetyl-histone H4. [synonyms: H4 histone acetylase activity; H4 histone acetyltransferase activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: histone H4 acetyltransferase activity
