intent: neuroblast development - The process aimed at the progression of a neuroblast over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific state, to the mature neuroblast. It does not include processes where the neuroblast turns into a glial cell or a neuron. (GO biological_process)
name: neuroblast development

intent: primary neural tube formation - The formation of the neural tube from an epithelial cell sheet (the neuroepithelium or neural plate). In primary neurulation, the cells surrounding the neural plate direct the neural plate cells to proliferate, invaginate, and pinch off from the surface to form a hollow epithelial tube. Primary neurulation is the typical mechanism of formation of the anterior neural tube. [synonyms: primary neural tube morphogenesis; primary neurulation; neural rod cavitation] (GO biological_process)
name: primary neural tube formation

intent: secondary neural tube formation - The formation of the neural tube by coalescence of mesenchymal cells followed by their conversion to epithelial cells to form a solid cord that subsequently hollows out (cavitates) to create a hollow tube. Secondary neurulation is the typical mechanism of formation of the neural tube posterior to the posterior neuropore in mammals. [synonyms: medullary cord biosynthesis; medullary cord formation; secondary neurulation; medullary rod cavitation; neural rod formation; secondary neural tube rod cavitation] (GO biological_process)
name: secondary neural tube formation

intent: neural plate elongation - The process in which the neural plate is shaped by the intrinsic movement of the epidermal and neural plate regions. (GO biological_process)
name: neural plate elongation

intent: neural rod formation - The formation of a solid rod of neurectoderm derived from the neural keel. The neural rod is roughly circular in cross section. Neural rod formation occurs during primary neurulation in teleosts. (GO biological_process)
name: neural rod formation

intent: neural keel formation - The formation of a thickened region of the neurectoderm that is roughly triangular in cross section. The neural keel develops from the neural plate and develops into the neural rod. Neural keel formation occurs during primary neurulation in teleosts. (GO biological_process)
name: neural keel formation

intent: notochord formation - The formation of the notochord from the chordamesoderm. The notochord is composed of large cells packed within a firm connective tissue sheath and is found in all chordates at the ventral surface of the neural tube. In vertebrates, the notochord contributes to the vertebral column. (GO biological_process)
name: notochord formation

intent: neural crest formation - The formation of the specialized region of ectoderm between the neural ectoderm (neural plate) and non-neural ectoderm. The neural crest gives rise to the neural crest cells that migrate away from this region as neural tube formation proceeds. (GO biological_process)
name: neural crest formation

intent: mesenchymal cell fate commitment - The process in which a cell becomes committed to become a mesenchymal cell. (GO biological_process)
name: mesenchymal cell fate commitment

intent: mesenchymal cell development - The process aimed at the progression of a mesenchymal cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. (GO biological_process)
name: mesenchymal cell development

intent: neural crest cell development - The process aimed at the progression of a neural crest cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. (GO biological_process)
name: neural crest cell development

intent: neural crest cell differentiation - The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neural crest cell. (GO biological_process)
name: neural crest cell differentiation

intent: neural crest cell fate commitment - The process in which a cell becomes committed to become a neural crest cell. (GO biological_process)
name: neural crest cell fate commitment

intent: neural crest cell fate determination - The process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a neural crest cell regardless of its environment; upon determination, the cell fate cannot be reversed. (GO biological_process)
name: neural crest cell fate determination

intent: neural crest cell fate specification - The process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a neural crest cell in an environment that is neutral with respect to the developmental pathway; upon specification, the cell fate can be reversed. (GO biological_process)
name: neural crest cell fate specification

intent: Schwann cell differentiation - The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a Schwann cell. Schwann cells are found in the peripheral nervous system, where they insulate neurons and axons, and regulate the environment in which neurons function. (GO biological_process)
name: Schwann cell differentiation

intent: regulation of Schwann cell differentiation - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of Schwann cell differentiation

intent: negative regulation of Schwann cell differentiation - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation. [synonyms: down regulation of Schwann cell differentiation; down-regulation of Schwann cell differentiation; downregulation of Schwann cell differentiation; inhibition of Schwann cell differentiation] (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of Schwann cell differentiation

intent: positive regulation of Schwann cell differentiation - Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation. [synonyms: up regulation of Schwann cell differentiation; up-regulation of Schwann cell differentiation; upregulation of Schwann cell differentiation; activation of Schwann cell differentiation; stimulation of Schwann cell differentiation] (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of Schwann cell differentiation

intent: regulation of neuron maturation - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation, the process leading to the attainment of the full functional capacity of a neuron. This process is independent of morphogenetic change. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of neuron maturation

intent: positive regulation of neuron maturation - Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation. [synonyms: up regulation of neuron maturation; up-regulation of neuron maturation; upregulation of neuron maturation; activation of neuron maturation; stimulation of neuron maturation] (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of neuron maturation

intent: negative regulation of neuron maturation - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation. [synonyms: down regulation of neuron maturation; down-regulation of neuron maturation; downregulation of neuron maturation; inhibition of neuron maturation] (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of neuron maturation

intent: Schwann cell development - The process aimed at the progression of a Schwann cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. Schwann cells are found in the peripheral nervous system, where they insulate neurons and axons, and regulate the environment in which neurons function. (GO biological_process)
name: Schwann cell development

intent: establishment of endothelial blood-brain barrier - Establishment of the endothelial barrier between the blood and the brain. The endothelial cells in the brain capillaries are packed tightly together preventing the passage of most molecules from the blood into the brain. Only lipid soluble molecules or those that are actively transported can pass through the blood-brain barrier. [synonyms: establishment of endothelial BBB; establishment of endothelial blood/brain barrier] (GO biological_process)
name: establishment of endothelial blood-brain barrier

intent: dopamine secretion - The regulated release of dopamine by a cell. Dopamine is a catecholamine and a precursor of adrenaline and noradrenaline. It acts as a neurotransmitter in the central nervous system but it is also produced peripherally and acts as a hormone. (GO biological_process)
name: dopamine secretion

intent: glutamate secretion - The controlled release of glutamate by a cell. The glutamate is the most abundant excitatory neurotransmitter in the nervous system. (GO biological_process)
name: glutamate secretion

intent: regulation of glutamate secretion - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of glutamate secretion

intent: positive regulation of glutamate secretion - Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate. [synonyms: up regulation of glutamate secretion; up-regulation of glutamate secretion; upregulation of glutamate secretion; activation of glutamate secretion; stimulation of glutamate secretion] (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of glutamate secretion

intent: negative regulation of glutamate secretion - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate. [synonyms: down regulation of glutamate secretion; down-regulation of glutamate secretion; downregulation of glutamate secretion; inhibition of glutamate secretion] (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of glutamate secretion

intent: gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion - The regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid by a cell or a tissue. The gamma-aminobutyric acid is the principal inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain but is also found in several extraneural tissues. [synonyms: GABA secretion] (GO biological_process)
name: gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

intent: regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid. [synonyms: regulation of GABA secretion] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

intent: negative regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid. [synonyms: down regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion; down-regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion; downregulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion; negative regulation of GABA secretion; inhibition of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion] (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

intent: positive regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion - Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid. [synonyms: positive regulation of GABA secretion; up regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion; up-regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion; upregulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion; activation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion; stimulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion] (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

intent: acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission - The regulated release of acetylcholine by a cell. The acetylcholine acts as a neurotransmitter that acts in both the peripheral nervous system (PNS) and central nervous system (CNS). (GO biological_process)
name: acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission

intent: regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission

intent: positive regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission - Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine. [synonyms: up regulation of acetylcholine secretion; up-regulation of acetylcholine secretion; upregulation of acetylcholine secretion; activation of acetylcholine secretion; stimulation of acetylcholine secretion] (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission

intent: negative regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine. [synonyms: down regulation of acetylcholine secretion; down-regulation of acetylcholine secretion; downregulation of acetylcholine secretion; inhibition of acetylcholine secretion] (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission

name: regulation of dopamine secretion

intent: regulation of serotonin secretion - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin. [synonyms: regulation of serotonin release] (GO biological_process)

[synonyms: down regulation of serotonin secretion; down-regulation of serotonin secretion; downregulation of serotonin secretion; inhibition of serotonin secretion; positive regulation of serotonin release] (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of serotonin secretion

intent: positive regulation of serotonin secretion - Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin. [synonyms: up regulation of serotonin secretion; up-regulation of serotonin secretion; upregulation of serotonin secretion; activation of serotonin secretion; stimulation of serotonin secretion; positive regulation of serotonin release] (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of serotonin secretion

intent: postsynaptic density - An electron dense network of proteins within and adjacent to the postsynaptic membrane of an asymmetric, neuron-neuron synapse. Its major components include neurotransmitter receptors and the proteins that spatially and functionally organize them such as anchoring and scaffolding molecules, signaling enzymes and cytoskeletal components. [synonyms: neuronal postsynaptic density; post synaptic density; post-synaptic density; postsynaptic density of dendrite] (GO cellular_component)
name: postsynaptic density

intent: response to cycloalkane - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cycloalkane stimulus. A cycloalkane is a cyclic saturated hydrocarbon having the general formula CnH2n. (GO biological_process)
name: response to cycloalkane

intent: response to isoquinoline alkaloid - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an isoquinoline alkaloid stimulus. An isoquinoline alkaloid is any member of a group of compounds with the heterocyclic ring structure of benzo(c)pyridine which is a structure characteristic of the group of opium alkaloids. (GO biological_process)
name: response to isoquinoline alkaloid

intent: response to tropane - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a tropane stimulus. Tropane is a nitrogenous bicyclic organic compound mainly known for a group of alkaloids derived from it (called tropane alkaloids), which include, among others, atropine and cocaine. (GO biological_process)
name: response to tropane

intent: response to purine-containing compound - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a purine-containing compound stimulus. [synonyms: response to purine] (GO biological_process)
name: response to purine-containing compound

intent: response to amine - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an amine stimulus. An amine is a compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups. [synonyms: response to amine stimulus] (GO biological_process)
name: response to amine

intent: response to fluoxetine - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a fluoxetine stimulus. Fluoxetine increases the extracellular level of the neurotransmitter serotonin by inhibiting its reuptake into the presynaptic cell, increasing the level of serotonin available to bind to the postsynaptic receptor. [synonyms: response to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor; response to SSRI] (GO biological_process)
name: response to fluoxetine

intent: junctional sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane - The part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane that contains calcium release channels, is devoted to calcium release and is juxtaposed to transverse tubule membrane. The junctional sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane consists of the junctional region of the terminal cisterna membrane. (GO cellular_component)
name: junctional sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane

intent: free sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane - The part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane that contains calcium pumps and is devoted to calcium uptake. The free sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane consists of the longitudinal sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane and the non-junctional region of the terminal cisterna membrane. (GO cellular_component)
name: free sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane

intent: oscillatory muscle contraction - A process in which force is generated within oscillatory skeletal muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. Oscillatory muscle contraction occurs in insect wing muscles and is characterized by asynchrony between action potential and contraction and by stretch activation. (GO biological_process)
name: oscillatory muscle contraction

intent: intercalated disc - A complex cell-cell junction at which myofibrils terminate in cardiomyocytes; mediates mechanical and electrochemical integration between individual cardiomyocytes. The intercalated disc contains regions of tight mechanical attachment (fasciae adherentes and desmosomes) and electrical coupling (gap junctions) between adjacent cells. [synonyms: intercalated disk] (GO cellular_component)
name: intercalated disc

intent: C zone - A region of the A band in which myosin-binding protein C is located and that can be seen by electron microscopy. This is a functional zone that also includes myosin. (GO cellular_component)
name: C zone

intent: striated muscle tissue development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a striated muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Striated muscle contain fibers that are divided by transverse bands into striations, and cardiac and skeletal muscle are types of striated muscle. Skeletal muscle myoblasts fuse to form myotubes and eventually multinucleated muscle fibers. The fusion of cardiac cells is very rare and can only form binucleate cells. (GO biological_process)
name: striated muscle tissue development

intent: branchiomeric skeletal muscle development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The branchiomeric muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls facial expression, pharyngeal and laryngeal function, operating the jaw. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle. Branchiomeric muscles of mammals correspond to the gill musculature of fish. (GO biological_process)
name: branchiomeric skeletal muscle development

intent: regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of somitomeric trunk muscle development. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development

intent: positive regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development - Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of somitomeric trunk muscle development. The somitomeric trunk muscle is derived from somitomeric mesoderm. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle. (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development

intent: negative regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of somitomeric trunk muscle development. The somitomeric trunk muscle is derived from somitomeric mesoderm. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development

intent: regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development. Branchiomeric skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development

intent: positive regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development - Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development. Branchiomeric skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development

intent: negative regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development. Branchiomeric skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development

intent: myoblast fate commitment in head - The process, taking place in the head, whereby the developmental fate of a cell becomes restricted such that it will develop into a myoblast. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers. (GO biological_process)
name: myoblast fate commitment in head

intent: myoblast fate commitment in trunk - The process taking place in the trunk whereby the developmental fate of a cell becomes restricted such that it will develop into a myoblast. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers. (GO biological_process)
name: myoblast fate commitment in trunk

intent: regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of satellite cell activation. The satellite cell activation is the process that initiates satellite cell division by causing it to move from quiescence to the G1 stage of the cell cycle. The cell swells and there are a number of other small changes. The cells then start to divide. Following cell division the cells will differentiate. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration

intent: positive regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration - Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of activation of satellite cell involved in skeletal muscle regeneration. The activation of satellite cell is the process that initiates satellite cell division by causing it to move from quiescence to the G1 stage of the cell cycle. The cell swells and there are a number of other small changes. The cells then start to divide. Following cell division the cells will differentiate. (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration

intent: skeletal muscle satellite cell activation - The change of a skeletal muscle satellite cell from a mitotically quiescent to a mitotically active state following exposure to some activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand. In adult muscle, satellite cells become activated to divide and differentiate in response to muscle damage. (GO biological_process)
name: skeletal muscle satellite cell activation

intent: tonic skeletal muscle contraction - A process in which force is generated within tonic skeletal muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The tonic skeletal muscle is characterized by long lasting contractile responses and high resistance to fatigue. (GO biological_process)
name: tonic skeletal muscle contraction

intent: twitch skeletal muscle contraction - A process in which force is generated within twitch skeletal muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The twitch skeletal muscle responds to neurostimulations with a contraction followed by a relaxation. (GO biological_process)
name: twitch skeletal muscle contraction

intent: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by calcium ion signaling - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by changing the calcium ion signals that trigger contraction. [synonyms: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by calcium ion signalling] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by calcium ion signaling

intent: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by modulation of calcium ion sensitivity of myofibril - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by changing calcium ion binding affinity of the myofibril. [synonyms: regulation of calcium ion sensitivity of myofibril involved in skeletal muscle contraction] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by modulation of calcium ion sensitivity of myofibril

intent: regulation of twitch skeletal muscle contraction - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of twitch skeletal muscle contraction. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of twitch skeletal muscle contraction

intent: regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of extraocular skeletal muscle development. Extraocular skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the extraocular skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The extraocular muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls eye movements. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development

intent: negative regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development - Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of extraocular skeletal muscle development. Extraocular skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the extraocular skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The extraocular muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls eye movements. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development

intent: positive regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development - Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of extraocular skeletal muscle development. Extraocular skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the extraocular skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The extraocular muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls eye movements. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle. (GO biological_process)
name: positive regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development

intent: regulation of the force of skeletal muscle contraction - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the force of skeletal muscle contraction. The force of skeletal muscle contraction is produced by acto-myosin interaction processes through the formation of cross bridges. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of the force of skeletal muscle contraction

intent: regulation of the velocity of shortening of skeletal muscle modulating contraction - Any process that modulates velocity of shortening of a skeletal muscle contraction. The shortening leads to reduction of the length of muscle fibers and sarcomeres. [synonyms: regulation of the velocity of shortening of skeletal muscle during contraction] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of the velocity of shortening of skeletal muscle modulating contraction

intent: skeletal muscle regeneration at neuromuscular junction - The regrowth of muscle tissue to repair injured or damaged muscle fibers in the postnatal stage at the neuromuscular junction. Regeneration of neuromuscular junctions occurs in an orderly way and relies on communication between nerve and muscle. Skeletal myofibers regenerate after injury and form neuro-muscular junctions with motor axons similar to normal ones. Regenerating myofibers develop within the basal lamina sheaths (satellite cells) of original myofibers. (GO biological_process)
name: skeletal muscle regeneration at neuromuscular junction

intent: spectrin-associated cytoskeleton - The part of the cytoskeleton composed of spectrin, protein 4.1 and ankyrin. Spectrin-associated cytoskeleton is associated with the plasma membrane. (GO cellular_component)
name: spectrin-associated cytoskeleton

intent: skeletal muscle atrophy - A process, occurring in skeletal muscle, that is characterized by a decrease in protein content, fiber diameter, force production and fatigue resistance in response to different conditions such as starvation, aging and disuse. (GO biological_process)
name: skeletal muscle atrophy

intent: regulation of skeletal muscle adaptation - Any process in which skeletal muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors. These adaptive events occur in both muscle fibers and associated structures (motoneurons and capillaries), and they involve alterations in regulatory mechanisms, contractile properties and metabolic capacities. [synonyms: regulation of skeletal muscle plasticity] (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of skeletal muscle adaptation

intent: skeletal muscle hypertrophy - The enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of an organ due to an increase in size (not length) of individual muscle fibers without cell division. In the case of skeletal muscle cells this happens due to the additional synthesis of sarcomeric proteins and assembly of myofibrils. (GO biological_process)

intent: longitudinal sarcoplasmic reticulum - The portion of the free sarcoplasmic reticulum consisting of longitudinal tubules that connect terminal cisternae. (GO cellular_component)

intent: terminal cisterna - The portion of sarcoplasmic reticulum devoted to calcium ion storage and calcium ion release. (GO cellular_component)
name: terminal cisterna

intent: longitudinal sarcoplasmic reticulum lumen - The region between the inner and outer lipid bilayers of the longitudinal sarcoplasmic reticulum envelope. The longitudinal sarcoplasmic reticulum lumen is continuous with the lumen contained within the terminal cisternae. (GO cellular_component)
name: longitudinal sarcoplasmic reticulum lumen

intent: terminal cisterna lumen - The region between the inner and outer lipid bilayers of the terminal cisterna envelope. This space is enriched in calsequestrin. (GO cellular_component)
name: terminal cisterna lumen

intent: smooth muscle adaptation - Any process in which smooth muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors. These adaptive events occur in both muscle fibers and associated structures (motoneurons and capillaries), and they involve alterations in regulatory mechanisms, contractile properties and metabolic capacities. [synonyms: smooth muscle plasticity] (GO biological_process)
name: smooth muscle adaptation

intent: smooth muscle hyperplasia - A process, occurring in smooth muscle, in which there is an increase in cell number by cell division, often leading to an increase in the size of an organ. (GO biological_process)
name: smooth muscle hyperplasia

intent: regulation of somitogenesis - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of somitogenesis. (GO biological_process)
name: regulation of somitogenesis

intent: release of sequestered calcium ion into cytosol by sarcoplasmic reticulum - The process in which the release of sequestered calcium ion by sarcoplasmic reticulum into cytosol occurs via calcium release channels. [synonyms: release of sequestered calcium ion by sarcoplasmic reticulum into cytosol] (GO biological_process)
name: release of sequestered calcium ion into cytosol by sarcoplasmic reticulum

intent: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by regulation of release of sequestered calcium ion - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction via the regulation of the release of sequestered calcium ion by sarcoplasmic reticulum into cytosol. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the endoplasmic reticulum of striated muscle, specialised for the sequestration of calcium ions that are released upon receipt of a signal relayed by the T tubules from the neuromuscular junction. (GO biological_process)

intent: melibiose transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of melibiose from one side of a membrane to the other. intent: oligosaccharide transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of oligosaccharide from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: endosomal oligosaccharide transporter] (GO molecular_function)

intent: raffinose transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of raffinose from one side of a membrane to the other. intent: polysaccharide transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of polysaccharides from one side of a membrane to the other. A polysaccharide is a polymer of many (typically more than 10) monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically. (GO molecular_function)

intent: beta-glucan transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of beta-glucans from one side of a membrane to the other. Beta-glucans are compounds composed of glucose residues linked by beta-glucosidic bonds. (GO molecular_function)
name: beta-glucan transmembrane transporter activity

intent: lipid III floppase activity - Enables the transbilayer of capsular-polysaccharides (Und-PP-GlcNAc-ManNAcA-Fuc4NAc (lipid III)) from the inner to the outer leaflet of the cytoplasmic membrane during the assembly of ECA. [synonyms: undecaprenol-pyrophosphate O-antigen flippase activity; capsular polysaccharide transmembrane transporter activity; capsule polysaccharide transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: lipid III floppase activity

intent: glucuronoside transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a glucuronosides from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: glucuronide transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: glucuronoside transmembrane transporter activity

intent: pyrimidine nucleotide-sugar transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a pyrimidine nucleotide-sugar from one side of a membrane to the other. name: pyrimidine nucleotide-sugar transmembrane transporter activity

intent: polyol transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a polyol from one side of a membrane to the other. A polyol is any polyhydric alcohol. [synonyms: sugar/polyol channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: polyol transmembrane transporter activity

intent: arabitol transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of an arabitol from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: arabinitol transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: arabitol transmembrane transporter activity

intent: glycerol transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of glycerol from one side of a membrane to the other. Glycerol is 1,2,3-propanetriol, a sweet, hygroscopic, viscous liquid, widely distributed in nature as a constituent of many lipids. (GO molecular_function)
name: glycerol transmembrane transporter activity

intent: glycerol-3-phosphate transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of glycerol-3-phosphate from one side of a membrane to the other. Glycerol-3-phosphate is a phosphoric monoester of glycerol. (GO molecular_function)

intent: amino acid transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. name: acidic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity

intent: aromatic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of aromatic amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Aromatic amino acids have an aromatic ring. [synonyms: hydroxy/aromatic amino acid permease activity; valine/tyrosine/tryptophan permease activity; aromatic amino acid transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: aromatic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity

intent: basic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of basic amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: basic amino acid permease activity; cationic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity; basic amino acid transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: basic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity

intent: neutral L-amino acid transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of neutral L-amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. name: neutral L-amino acid transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-amino acid transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of an L-amino acid from one side of a membrane to the other. L-amino acids are the L-enantiomers of amino acids. [synonyms: L-amino acid transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)

intent: L-alanine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-alanine from one side of a membrane to the other. L-alanine is the L-enantiomer of 2-aminopropanoic acid. [synonyms: L-alanine transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)

intent: L-asparagine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-asparagine from one side of a membrane to the other. intent: L-aspartate transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-aspartate from one side of a membrane to the other. L-aspartate is the anion derived from aspartic acid. intent: L-cystine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-cystine from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: cystine/diaminopimelate porter activity; L-cystine transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)

intent: gamma-aminobutyric acid transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of gamma-aminobutyric acid from one side of a membrane to the other. name: gamma-aminobutyric acid transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-glutamine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-glutamine from one side of a membrane to the other. L-glutamine is 2-amino-4-carbamoylbutanoic acid. [synonyms: asparagine/glutamine permease activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: L-glutamine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: glycine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of glycine from one side of a membrane to the other. Glycine is aminoethanoic acid. name: glycine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-isoleucine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-isoleucine from one side of a membrane to the other. L-isoleucine is (2R*,3R*)-2-amino-3-methylpentanoic acid. name: L-isoleucine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-lysine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-lysine from one side of a membrane to the other. L-lysine is 2,6-diaminohexanoic acid. [synonyms: histidine/arginine/lysine/ornithine porter activity; L-lysine permease; lysine permease activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: L-lysine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-leucine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-leucine from one side of a membrane to the other. L-leucine is 2-amino-4-methylpentanoic acid. name: L-leucine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-methionine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-methionine from one side of a membrane to the other. L-methionine is 2-amino-4-(methylthio)butanoic acid. [synonyms: L-methionine transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)

intent: L-phenylalanine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-phenylalanine from one side of a membrane to the other. L-phenylalanine is 2-amino-3-phenylpropanoic acid. intent: L-proline transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-proline from one side of a membrane to the other. L-proline is pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid. name: L-proline transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-serine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-serine from one side of a membrane to the other. L-serine is the L-enantiomer of 2-amino-3-hydroxypropanoic acid. [synonyms: L-serine permease activity; threonine/serine:sodium symporter activity; L-serine transporter activity; serine transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: L-serine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-threonine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-threonine from one side of a membrane to the other. L-threonine is (2R*,3S*)-2-amino-3-hydroxybutanoic acid. [synonyms: L-threonine permease activity; threonine/serine:sodium symporter activity; L-threonine transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: L-threonine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-tryptophan transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-tryptophan from one side of a membrane to the other. Tryptophan is 2-amino-3-(1H-indol-3-yl)propanoic acid. [synonyms: L-tryptophan permease activity; valine/tyrosine/tryptophan permease activity; L-tryptophan transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: L-tryptophan transmembrane transporter activity

intent: amino-acid betaine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of betaine from one side of a membrane to the other. Betaine is the N-trimethyl derivative of an amino acid. [synonyms: betaine transmembrane transporter activity; betaine/GABA:sodium symporter activity; glycine betaine/proline porter activity; proline/glycine/betaine:hydrogen/sodium symporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: amino-acid betaine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: methylammonium transmembrane transporter activity - Enables directed movement of methylammonium, CH3NH2, from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)
name: methylammonium transmembrane transporter activity

intent: polyamine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of polyamines, organic compounds containing two or more amino groups, from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: amine/amide/polyamine channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: polyamine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: urea transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of urea from one side of a membrane to the other. Urea is the water soluble compound H2N-CO-NH2. [synonyms: urea transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: urea transmembrane transporter activity

intent: nucleobase transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a nucleobase, any nitrogenous base that is a constituent of a nucleoside, nucleotide, or nucleic acidfrom one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)
name: nucleobase transmembrane transporter activity

intent: adenine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of adenine, 6-aminopurine, from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)
name: adenine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: guanine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of guanine, 2-amino-6-hydroxypurine, from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)
name: guanine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: cytosine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of cytosine, 4-amino-2-hydroxypyrimidine from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)
name: cytosine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: uracil transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of uracil, 2,4-dioxopyrimidine, from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: uracil/uridine permease activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: uracil transmembrane transporter activity

intent: purine nucleoside transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a purine nucleoside, a purine base covalently bonded to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar, from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)
name: purine nucleoside transmembrane transporter activity

intent: cytidine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of cytidine, cytosine riboside, from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)
name: cytidine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: uridine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of uridine, uracil riboside, from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: uracil/uridine permease activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: uridine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: pyrimidine nucleoside transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a pyrimidine nucleoside, a pyrimidine base covalently bonded to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)
name: pyrimidine nucleoside transmembrane transporter activity

intent: nucleotide transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a nucleotide, any compound consisting of a nucleoside that is esterified with (ortho)phosphate, from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)

intent: purine nucleotide transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a purine nucleotide, any compound consisting of a purine nucleoside esterified with (ortho)phosphate, from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)

intent: ADP transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of ADP, adenosine diphosphate, from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)

intent: pyrimidine nucleotide transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a pyrimidine nucleotide, any compound consisting of a pyrimidine nucleoside esterified with (ortho)phosphate, from one side of a membrane to the other. (GO molecular_function)
name: pyrimidine nucleotide transmembrane transporter activity

intent: choline transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of choline from one side of a membrane to the other. Choline (2-hydroxyethyltrimethylammonium) is an amino alcohol that occurs widely in living organisms as a constituent of certain types of phospholipids and in the neurotransmitter acetylcholine. [synonyms: choline permease activity; amino acid/choline transmembrane transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: choline transmembrane transporter activity

intent: lipopolysaccharide transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of lipopolysaccharides from one side of a membrane to the other. A lipopolysaccharide is any of a group of related, structurally complex components of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria. Lipopolysaccharides consist three covalently linked regions, lipid A, core oligosaccharide, and an O side chain. Lipid A is responsible for the toxicity of the lipopolysaccharide. [synonyms: LPS transmembrane transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: lipopolysaccharide transmembrane transporter activity

intent: biopterin transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of biopterin from one side of a membrane to the other. Biopterin is a growth factor for certain protozoans and some insects; it is widely distributed in tissues and functions in a reduced form, tetrahydrobiopterin, as a hydroxylation coenzyme. [synonyms: biopterin transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: biopterin transmembrane transporter activity

intent: biotin transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of biotin from one side of a membrane to the other. Biotin is cis-tetrahydro-2-oxothieno(3,4-d)imidazoline-4-valeric acid; the (+) enantiomer is very widely distributed in cells and serves as a carrier in a number of enzymatic beta-carboxylation reactions. [synonyms: biotin transporter activity; vitamin B7 transporter activity; vitamin H transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: biotin transmembrane transporter activity

intent: carnitine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of carnitine across a membrane. Carnitine is a compound that participates in the transfer of acyl groups across the inner mitochondrial membrane. [synonyms: vitamin Bt transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: carnitine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: O-acyl-L-carnitine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of O-acyl-L-carnitine from one side of a membrane to the other. O-acyl-L-carnitine is the condensation product of a carboxylic acid and carnitine and is the transport form for a fatty acid crossing the mitochondrial membrane. [synonyms: acylcarnitine transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: O-acyl-L-carnitine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: coenzyme A transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of coenzyme A from one side of a membrane to the other. Coenzyme A, 3'-phosphoadenosine-(5')diphospho(4')pantatheine, is an acyl carrier in many acylation and acyl-transfer reactions in which the intermediate is a thiol ester. [synonyms: coenzyme A transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: coenzyme A transmembrane transporter activity

intent: L-ascorbic acid transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-ascorbate from one side of a membrane to the other. L-ascorbate, (2R)-2-[(1S)-1,2-dihydroxyethyl]-4-hydroxy-5-oxo-2,5-dihydrofuran-3-olate, is vitamin C and has co-factor and anti-oxidant activities in many species. [synonyms: L-ascorbate transporter activity; vitamin C transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: L-ascorbic acid transmembrane transporter activity

intent: FAD transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the directed movement of flavin-adenine dinucleotide (FAD) from one side of a membrane to the other. FAD forms the coenzyme of the prosthetic group of various flavoprotein oxidoreductase enzymes, in which it functions as an electron acceptor by being reversibly converted to its reduced form. [synonyms: flavin adenine dinucleotide transmembrane transporter activity; flavin-adenine dinucleotide transmembrane transporter activity; FAD carrier activity; flavin adenine dinucleotide carrier activity; flavin-adenine dinucleotide carrier activity; FAD transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: FAD transmembrane transporter activity

intent: 5-formyltetrahydrofolate transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of 5-formyltetrahydrofolate, the formylated derivative of tetrahydrofolate, from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: 5-formyltetrahydrofolate transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: 5-formyltetrahydrofolate transmembrane transporter activity

intent: heme transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of heme from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: haem transporter activity; heme transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: heme transmembrane transporter activity

intent: pantothenate transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the directed movement of pantothenate across a membrane. Pantothenate is the anion of pantothenic acid, the amide of beta-alanine and pantoic acid; it is a B complex vitamin that is a constituent of coenzyme A and is distributed ubiquitously in foods. [synonyms: vitamin B5 transmembrane transporter activity; pantothenate transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: pantothenate transmembrane transporter activity

intent: thiamine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of thiamine from one side of a membrane to the other. Thiamine is vitamin B1, a water soluble vitamin present in fresh vegetables and meats, especially liver. [synonyms: thiamin permease activity; thiamin transmembrane transporter activity; thiamine permease activity; vitamin B1 transporter activity; thiamin uptake transporter activity; thiamine uptake transmembrane transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: thiamine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: cycloheximide transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of cycloheximide from one side of a membrane to the other. Cycloheximide is an antibiotic produced by Streptomyces which interferes with protein synthesis in eukaryotes. [synonyms: cycloheximide transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: cycloheximide transmembrane transporter activity

intent: fluconazole transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of fluconazole from one side of a membrane to the other. Fluconazole is an antifungal drug used for oral candidiasis and cryptococcal meningitis; it is still under study for treatment of vaginal candidiasis and other fungal infections. [synonyms: fluconazole transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: fluconazole transmembrane transporter activity

intent: fatty acid transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of fatty acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Fatty acids are aliphatic monocarboxylic acids liberated from naturally occurring fats and oils by hydrolysis. [synonyms: fatty acyl transporter activity; peroxisomal fatty acyl transporter; fatty acid transporter activity; fatty-acyl group transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: fatty acid transmembrane transporter activity

intent: aminophospholipid flippase activity - Enables the transfer of aminophospholipids from the exoplasmic to the cytosolic leaflet of a membrane, using energy from the hydrolysis of ATP. Aminophospholipids contain phosphoric acid as a mono- or diester and an amino (NH2) group. [synonyms: aminophospholipid transmembrane transporter activity; aminophospholipid transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: aminophospholipid flippase activity

intent: water channel activity - Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of water through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel. [synonyms: aquaporin] (GO molecular_function)
name: water channel activity

intent: proton channel activity - Enables the facilitated diffusion of a hydrogen ion (by an energy-independent process) involving passage through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel without evidence for a carrier-mediated mechanism. [synonyms: hydrogen ion channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: proton channel activity

intent: glycerol channel activity - Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of glycerol through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel. (GO molecular_function)
name: glycerol channel activity

intent: methylammonium channel activity - Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of methylammonium through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel. Methylammonium is CH3NH2. (GO molecular_function)
name: methylammonium channel activity

intent: urea channel activity - Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of urea through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel. (GO molecular_function)
name: urea channel activity

intent: channel activity - Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of a solute through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel. Stereospecificity is not exhibited but this transport may be specific for a particular molecular species or class of molecules. [synonyms: channel/pore class transporter activity; nonselective channel activity; alpha-type channel activity; channel-forming toxin activity; pore class transporter activity; substrate-specific channel activity; pore activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: channel activity

intent: calcium-activated potassium channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of a potassium cation by a channel that opens when a calcium cation has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts. (GO molecular_function)
name: calcium-activated potassium channel activity

intent: outward rectifier potassium channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of a potassium ion by an outwardly-rectifying voltage-gated channel. An outwardly rectifying current-voltage relation is one where at any given driving force the outward flow of K+ ions exceeds the inward flow for the opposite driving force. (GO molecular_function)
name: outward rectifier potassium channel activity

intent: ATP-activated inward rectifier potassium channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of a potassium ion by an inwardly-rectifying voltage-gated channel, where the inward rectification is due to a voltage-dependent block of the channel pore by ATP. An inwardly rectifying current-voltage relation is one where at any given driving force the inward flow of K+ ions exceeds the outward flow for the opposite driving force. (GO molecular_function)
name: ATP-activated inward rectifier potassium channel activity

intent: organellar voltage-gated chloride channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of a chloride ion by a voltage-gated channel. The membrane is an organellar membrane. [synonyms: organellar voltage gated chloride channel activity; organellar voltage-dependent chloride channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: organellar voltage-gated chloride channel activity

intent: stretch-activated, monoatomic cation-selective, calcium channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of a calcium ion by a channel that opens in response to a mechanical stress in the form of stretching. [synonyms: stretch-activated, cation-selective, calcium channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: stretch-activated, monoatomic cation-selective, calcium channel activity

intent: ligand-gated monoatomic ion channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of an ion by a channel that opens when a specific ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts. [synonyms: ionotropic receptor activity; ligand-gated ion channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: ligand-gated monoatomic ion channel activity

intent: kainate selective glutamate receptor activity - An ionotropic glutamate receptor activity that exhibits fast gating by glutamate, acts by opening a cation channel permeable to sodium and potassium, and for which kainate is an agonist. (GO molecular_function)
name: kainate selective glutamate receptor activity

intent: intracellularly gated calcium channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of a calcium ion by a channel that opens when a specific intracellular ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts. [synonyms: calcium-release channel activity; intracellular ligand-gated calcium channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: intracellularly gated calcium channel activity

intent: store-operated calcium channel activity - A ligand-gated ion channel activity which transports calcium in response to emptying of intracellular calcium stores. (GO molecular_function)
name: store-operated calcium channel activity

intent: ligand-gated sodium channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of a sodium ion by a channel that opens when a specific ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts. [synonyms: acid-sensing ion channel activity; epithelial sodium channel] (GO molecular_function)
name: ligand-gated sodium channel activity

intent: fructose uniporter activity - Enables the transfer of a solute or solutes from one side of a membrane to the other according to the reaction: fructose(out) = fructose(in). (GO molecular_function)
name: fructose uniporter activity

intent: porin activity - Enables the transfer of substances, sized less than 1000 Da, from one side of a membrane to the other. The transmembrane portions of porins consist exclusively of beta-strands which form a beta-barrel. They are found in the outer membranes of Gram-negative bacteria, mitochondria, plastids and possibly acid-fast Gram-positive bacteria. [synonyms: porin; outer membrane exporter porin] (GO molecular_function)
name: porin activity

intent: secondary active transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of a solute from one side of a membrane to the other, up its concentration gradient. [synonyms: coupled carrier; electrochemical potential-driven transporter activity; porter activity; porters; secondary carrier-type facilitators; energizer of outer membrane receptor-mediated transport activity; heavy metal ion porter activity; ion-gradient-driven energizer activity; multidrug endosomal transmembrane transporter activity; nitrite/nitrate porter activity; galactose/glucose (methylgalactoside) porter activity; active transporter] (GO molecular_function)

intent: uniporter activity - Catalysis of the transport of a single molecular species across a membrane; transport is independent of the movement of any other molecular species. [synonyms: facilitated diffusion carrier; single-species transporter activity; uniport] (GO molecular_function)
name: uniporter activity

intent: symporter activity - Enables the active transport of a solute across a membrane by a mechanism whereby two or more species are transported together in the same direction in a tightly coupled process not directly linked to a form of energy other than chemiosmotic energy. [synonyms: symport; cotransporter activity; porter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: symporter activity

intent: solute:monoatomic cation symporter activity - Enables the transfer of a solute or solutes from one side of a membrane to the other according to the reaction: solute(out) + cation(out) = solute(in) + cation(in). [synonyms: solute:cation symporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: solute:monoatomic cation symporter activity

intent: solute:proton symporter activity - Enables the transfer of a solute or solutes from one side of a membrane to the other according to the reaction: solute(out) + H+(out) = solute(in) + H+(in). [synonyms: solute:hydrogen symporter activity; heavy metal ion:hydrogen symporter activity; high affinity metal ion uptake transporter activity; L-idonate/D-gluconate:hydrogen symporter activity; low affinity metal ion uptake transporter activity; proline/glycine/betaine:hydrogen/sodium symporter activity] (GO molecular_function)

name: organophosphate ester transport

intent: monosaccharide transmembrane transport - The process in which a monosaccharide is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. name: monosaccharide transmembrane transport

intent: pentose transmembrane transport - The process in which pentose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. A pentose is any aldose with a chain of five carbon atoms in the molecule. [synonyms: pentose transport] (GO biological_process)
name: pentose transmembrane transport

intent: arabinose transmembrane transport - The process in which arabinose, a pentose monosaccharide that occurs in both D and L configurations, is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. [synonyms: arabinose transport] (GO biological_process)
name: arabinose transmembrane transport

intent: D-ribose transmembrane transport - The process in which D-ribose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. As beta-D-ribofuranose, D-ribose forms the glycose group of all ribonucleosides, ribonucleotides and ribonucleic acids, and also of ribose phosphates, various glycosides, some coenzymes and some forms of vitamin B12. [synonyms: D-ribose transport] (GO biological_process)
name: D-ribose transmembrane transport

intent: D-xylose transmembrane transport - The process in which D-xylose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. D-xylose (the naturally occurring enantiomer is always D-) is a constituent of plant polysaccharides. [synonyms: D-xylose transport] (GO biological_process)
name: D-xylose transmembrane transport

intent: D-allose transmembrane transport - The process in which D-allose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. name: D-allose transmembrane transport

intent: fructose transmembrane transport - The directed movement of fructose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. [synonyms: fructose transport] (GO biological_process)
name: fructose transmembrane transport

intent: fucose transmembrane transport - The process in which fucose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. Fucose is 6-deoxygalactose and has two enantiomers, D-fucose and L-fucose. [synonyms: fucose transport] (GO biological_process)
name: fucose transmembrane transport

intent: galactose transmembrane transport - The process in which galactose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. D-galactose is widely distributed in combined form in plants, animals and microorganisms as a constituent of oligo- and polysaccharides; it also occurs in galactolipids and as its glucoside in lactose and melibiose. [synonyms: galactose transport] (GO biological_process)
name: galactose transmembrane transport

intent: beta-glucoside transport - The directed movement of beta-glucosides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Beta-glucosides are glycosides in which the sugar group is a glucose residue, and the anomeric carbon of the bond is in a beta configuration. (GO biological_process)
name: beta-glucoside transport

intent: glucose-6-phosphate transport - The directed movement of glucose-6-phosphate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. name: glucose-6-phosphate transport

intent: mannose transmembrane transport - The process in which mannose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. Mannose is the aldohexose manno-hexose, the C-2 epimer of glucose. The D-(+)-form is widely distributed in mannans and hemicelluloses and is of major importance in the core oligosaccharide of N-linked oligosaccharides of glycoproteins. [synonyms: mannose transport] (GO biological_process)
name: mannose transmembrane transport

intent: rhamnose transmembrane transport - The process in which rhamnose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. Rhamnose occurs commonly as a compound of plant glycosides, in polysaccharides of gums and mucilages, and in bacterial polysaccharides. It is also a component of some plant cell wall polysaccharides and frequently acts as the sugar components of flavonoids. [synonyms: rhamnose transport] (GO biological_process)
name: rhamnose transmembrane transport

intent: N-acetylgalactosamine transport - The directed movement of N-acetylgalactosamine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. name: N-acetylgalactosamine transport

intent: N-acetylglucosamine transport - The directed movement of N-acetylglucosamine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. (GO biological_process)

intent: methylgalactoside transport - The directed movement of methylgalactoside into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. name: methylgalactoside transport

intent: disaccharide transport - The directed movement of disaccharides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Disaccharides are sugars composed of two monosaccharide units. (GO biological_process)
name: disaccharide transport

intent: lactose transport - The directed movement of lactose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Lactose is a disaccharide 4-O-beta-D-galactopyranosyl-D-glucose, and constitutes roughly 5% of the milk in almost all mammals. (GO biological_process)
name: lactose transport

intent: maltose transport - The directed movement of maltose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. name: maltose transport

intent: melibiose transport - The directed movement of melibiose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Melibiose is the disaccharide 6-O-alpha-D-galactopyranosyl-D-glucose. (GO biological_process)
name: melibiose transport

intent: sucrose transport - The directed movement of sucrose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Sucrose is the disaccharide fructofuranosyl-glucopyranoside. (GO biological_process)
name: sucrose transport

intent: trehalose transport - The directed movement of trehalose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Trehalose is a disaccharide that consists of two molecules of glucose and is isomeric with sucrose. (GO biological_process)
name: trehalose transport

intent: oligosaccharide transport - The directed movement of oligosaccharides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Oligosaccharides are molecules with between two and (about) 20 monosaccharide residues connected by glycosidic linkages. (GO biological_process)
name: oligosaccharide transport

intent: raffinose transport - The directed movement of raffinose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Raffinose occurs in plants almost as commonly as sucrose and is present in cereal grains, cotton seeds, and many legumes. It is synthesized from sucrose by transfer of a galactopyranoside from myo-inositol. (GO biological_process)
name: raffinose transport

intent: polysaccharide transport - The directed movement of polysaccharides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. A polysaccharide is a polymer of many (typically more than 10) monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically. (GO biological_process)
name: polysaccharide transport

intent: beta-glucan transport - The directed movement of beta-glucans into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Beta-glucans are compounds composed of glucose residues linked by beta-glucosidic bonds. (GO biological_process)
name: beta-glucan transport

intent: capsular polysaccharide transport - The directed movement of capsular polysaccharides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. name: capsular polysaccharide transport

intent: teichoic acid transport - The directed movement of teichoic acid into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. (GO biological_process)
name: teichoic acid transport

intent: hexuronide transmembrane transport - The directed movement of hexuronide across a membrane. intent: glucuronoside transport - The directed movement of glucuronosides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. name: glucuronoside transport

intent: nucleotide-sugar transmembrane transport - The directed movement of nucleotide-sugars into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. intent: UDP-N-acetylgalactosamine transmembrane transport - The directed movement of UDP-N-acetylgalactosamine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. intent: myo-inositol transport - The directed movement of myo-inositol into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. name: alpha-pinene-oxide decyclase activity

name: dichloromuconate cycloisomerase activity

name: anthranilate-CoA ligase activity

name: 4-chlorobenzoate-CoA ligase activity
