intent: slime layer - A slime layer is an easily removed, diffuse, unorganized layer of extracellular material that surrounds a cell. Specifically this consists mostly of exopolysaccharides, glycoproteins, and glycolipids. (GO cellular_component)
name: slime layer

intent: S-layer - A crystalline protein layer surrounding some bacteria. (GO cellular_component)
name: S-layer

intent: glial cell-derived neurotrophic factor receptor binding - A growth factor that binds selectively and non-covalently to glial cell-derived neurotrophic factor receptors. [synonyms: glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor receptor ligand; glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor receptor binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: glial cell-derived neurotrophic factor receptor binding

intent: membrane coat - Any of several different proteinaceous coats that can associate with membranes. intent: clathrin coat - A membrane coat found on coated pits and some coated vesicles; consists of polymerized clathrin triskelions, each comprising three clathrin heavy chains and three clathrin light chains, linked to the membrane via one of the AP adaptor complexes. [synonyms: clathrin cage] (GO cellular_component)
name: clathrin coat

intent: AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex - Any of several heterotetrameric complexes that link clathrin (or another coat-forming molecule, as hypothesized for AP-3 and AP-4) to a membrane surface; they are found on coated pits and coated vesicles, and mediate sorting of cargo proteins into vesicles. [synonyms: HA1; HA1 clathrin adaptor; AP-1 related adapter complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: AP-1 adaptor complex

[synonyms: HA2; HA2 clathrin adaptor] (GO cellular_component)
name: AP-2 adaptor complex

intent: AP-3 adaptor complex - A heterotetrameric AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex that consists of beta3, delta, mu3 and sigma3 subunits and is found associated with endosomal membranes. AP-3 does not appear to associate with clathrin in all organisms. In at least humans, the AP-3 complex can be heterogeneric due to the existence of multiple subunit isoforms encoded by different genes (beta3A and beta3B, mu3A and mu3B, and sigma3A and sigma3B). (GO cellular_component)
name: AP-3 adaptor complex

intent: AP-4 adaptor complex - An AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex that consists of beta4, epsilon, mu4 and sigma4 subunits and is found associated with membranes in the trans-Golgi network; it is not clear whether AP-4 forms clathrin coats in vivo. (GO cellular_component)
name: AP-4 adaptor complex

intent: clathrin vesicle coat - A clathrin coat found on a vesicle. (GO cellular_component)

intent: COPI vesicle coat - One of two multimeric complexes that forms a membrane vesicle coat. The mammalian COPI subunits are called alpha-, beta-, beta'-, gamma-, delta-, epsilon- and zeta-COP. name: COPI vesicle coat

intent: COPII vesicle coat - One of two multimeric complexes that forms a membrane vesicle coat. intent: clathrin coat of endocytic vesicle - A clathrin coat found on an endocytic vesicle. [synonyms: clathrin coat of endocytotic vesicle] (GO cellular_component)

intent: clathrin coat of synaptic vesicle - A clathrin coat found on a synaptic vesicle. (GO cellular_component)

intent: clathrin coat of coated pit - The coat found on coated pits and the coated vesicles derived from coated pits; comprises clathrin and the AP-2 adaptor complex. (GO cellular_component)

intent: transport vesicle - Any of the vesicles of the constitutive secretory pathway, which carry cargo from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, between Golgi cisternae, from the Golgi to the ER (retrograde transport) or to destinations within or outside the cell. name: transport vesicle

COPII-associated vesicles transport proteins from the rough endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus (anterograde transport). [synonyms: COPII-associated ER to Golgi transport vesicle; COPII-associated vesicle; COPII-coated vesicle; COPII vesicle; endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi transport vesicle; endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi transport vesicle; ER to Golgi constitutive secretory pathway transport vesicle; ER to Golgi transport vesicle; ER-Golgi transport vesicle] (GO cellular_component)
name: COPII-coated ER to Golgi transport vesicle

intent: coated vesicle - Small membrane-bounded organelle formed by pinching off of a coated region of membrane. Some coats are made of clathrin, whereas others are made from other proteins. (GO cellular_component)
name: coated vesicle

intent: clathrin-coated vesicle - A vesicle with a coat formed of clathrin connected to the membrane via one of the clathrin adaptor complexes. (GO cellular_component)
name: clathrin-coated vesicle

intent: COPI-coated vesicle - A vesicle with a coat formed of the COPI coat complex proteins. COPI-coated vesicles are found associated with Golgi membranes at steady state, are involved in Golgi to endoplasmic reticulum (retrograde) vesicle transport, and possibly also in intra-Golgi transport. [synonyms: coatomer] (GO cellular_component)
name: COPI-coated vesicle

intent: endocytic vesicle - A membrane-bounded intracellular vesicle formed by invagination of the plasma membrane around an extracellular substance. Endocytic vesicles fuse with early endosomes to deliver the cargo for further sorting. [synonyms: endocytotic transport vesicle; endocytotic vesicle] (GO cellular_component)
name: endocytic vesicle

intent: trans-Golgi network transport vesicle - A vesicle that mediates transport between the trans-Golgi network and other parts of the cell. [synonyms: TGN transport vesicle; trans-Golgi network constitutive secretory pathway transport vesicle] (GO cellular_component)
name: trans-Golgi network transport vesicle

intent: secretory granule - A small subcellular vesicle, surrounded by a membrane, that is formed from the Golgi apparatus and contains a highly concentrated protein destined for secretion. Processing of the contained protein may take place in secretory granules. [synonyms: secretory vesicle] (GO cellular_component)
name: secretory granule

intent: COPI-coated Golgi to ER transport vesicle - A vesicle that mediates transport from the Golgi to the endoplasmic reticulum. name: COPI-coated Golgi to ER transport vesicle

intent: COPI-coated inter-Golgi transport vesicle - A vesicle that mediates transport of cargo within the Golgi complex (for example, between cisternae of the Golgi stack). [synonyms: inter-Golgi transport constitutive secretory pathway transport vesicle] (GO cellular_component)
name: COPI-coated inter-Golgi transport vesicle

intent: alpha-1,6-mannosylglycoprotein 6-beta-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: UDP-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine + N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-1,2-alpha-D-mannosyl-1,3(6)-(N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-1,2-alpha-D-mannosyl,1,6(3))-beta-D-mannosyl-1,4-N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-R = UDP + N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-1,2-(N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-1,6)-1,2-alpha-D-mannosyl-1,3(6)-(N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-1,2-alpha-D-mannosyl-1,6(3))-beta-D-mannosyl-1,4-N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-R. name: alpha-1,6-mannosylglycoprotein 6-beta-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity

intent: manganese ion binding - Binding to a manganese ion (Mn). [synonyms: manganese binding; Mn binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: manganese ion binding

intent: sphingolipid biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of sphingolipids, any of a class of lipids containing the long-chain amine diol sphingosine or a closely related base (a sphingoid). name: sphingolipid biosynthetic process

name: sphingolipid catabolic process

intent: protein import into mitochondrial matrix - The import of proteins with mitochondrial targeting sequence from the cytosol across the mitochondrial outer and inner membranes into the matrix via TOM-TIM23-PAM. [synonyms: mitochondrial matrix protein import; protein transport into mitochondrial matrix; TOM-TIM23-PAM presequence matrix import pathway; mitochondrial translocation] (GO biological_process)
name: protein import into mitochondrial matrix

intent: molybdenum ion binding - Binding to a molybdenum ion (Mo). [synonyms: Mo ion binding; molybdenum binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: molybdenum ion binding

intent: bacteriocin biosynthetic process - The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a bacteriocin, any of a heterogeneous group of polypeptide antibiotics that are secreted by certain bacterial strains and are able to kill cells of other susceptible (frequently related) strains after adsorption at specific receptors on the cell surface. They include the colicins, and their mechanisms of action vary. [synonyms: bacteriocin anabolism; bacteriocin biosynthesis; bacteriocin formation; bacteriocin synthesis] (GO biological_process)
name: bacteriocin biosynthetic process

intent: bacteriocin immunity - A process that mediates resistance to a bacteriocin: any of a heterogeneous group of polypeptide antibiotics that are secreted by certain bacterial strains and are able to kill cells of other susceptible (frequently related) strains after adsorption at specific receptors on the cell surface. They include the colicins, and their mechanisms of action vary. (GO biological_process)
name: bacteriocin immunity

intent: cell differentiation - The cellular developmental process in which a relatively unspecialized cell, e.g. embryonic or regenerative cell, acquires specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize a specific cell. intent: regulation of cell adhesion - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of attachment of a cell to another cell or to the extracellular matrix. [synonyms: cell adhesion receptor regulator activity] (GO biological_process)

name: benzodiazepine receptor binding

intent: protein xylosyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the transfer of a beta-D-xylosyl residue from UDP-D-xylose to the serine hydroxyl group of an acceptor protein substrate. name: signaling receptor complex adaptor activity

intent: regulation of proteolysis - Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the hydrolysis of a peptide bond or bonds within a protein. [synonyms: regulation of peptidolysis] (GO biological_process)

One set of conditions favors early termination of transcription. In the classic example of the trp biosynthesis operon, translation of the gene for a short, trp-containing polypeptide called the trp operon leader peptide pauses either at a trp codon (if tryptophan is scarce) or the stop codon (if trp is readily available). Although the polypeptides encoded by leader peptide genes appear not to be stable once their translation is complete, it is suggested by recent studies that their nascent polypeptide chains interact specifically with ribosomes, specific uncharged tRNAs, or other cellular components to inhibit release at the stop codon and improve the function of transcriptional attenuation as a regulatory switch. name: alphav-beta5 integrin-vitronectin complex

intent: phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex, class III - A phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex that contains a catalytic class III phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) subunit bound to a regulatory (adaptor) subunit. intent: nuclear speck organization - A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of nuclear specks, a class of nuclear body in which splicing factors are localized. intent: ecdysone receptor signaling pathway - A nuclear receptor-mediated signaling pathway initiated by an ecdysone binding to an intracellular receptor of the nuclear receptor protein family, and ending with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription. name: ecdysone receptor signaling pathway

intent: ecdysone-mediated polytene chromosome puffing - The decondensing (loosening) and swelling of the chromosomal sites of hormone-responsive genes on polytene chromosomes in response to increased production of the steroid hormone 20-hydroxyecdysone (ecdysone) in Drosophila larvae approaching pupation. intent: induction of programmed cell death by ecdysone - Any process induced by the steroid hormone 20-hydroxyecdysone (ecdysone) that directly activates any of the steps required for programmed cell death. (GO biological_process)
name: induction of programmed cell death by ecdysone

intent: polytene chromosome puffing - The decondensing (loosening) and swelling of the chromosomal sites of target genes on polytene chromosomes following response to a stimulus, to facilitate sudden bursts of transcriptional activity in response to transient environmental signals. (GO biological_process)
name: polytene chromosome puffing

intent: heat shock-mediated polytene chromosome puffing - The decondensing (loosening) and swelling of the chromosomal sites of heat shock genes on polytene chromosomes in response to a heat shock stimulus. (GO biological_process)
name: heat shock-mediated polytene chromosome puffing

intent: induction of programmed cell death by hormones - Any process induced by hormones that directly activates any of the steps required for programmed cell death. (GO biological_process)
name: induction of programmed cell death by hormones

intent: axoneme assembly - The assembly and organization of an axoneme, the bundle of microtubules and associated proteins that forms the core of cilia (also called flagella) in eukaryotic cells and is responsible for their movements. [synonyms: ciliary axoneme assembly; cilium axoneme assembly; flagellar axoneme assembly; flagellum axoneme assembly; axoneme biogenesis; cilium axoneme biogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: axoneme assembly

intent: establishment or maintenance of apical/basal cell polarity - Any cellular process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance polarization of a cell's architecture along its apical/basal axis so that the apical and basal regions of the cell have different membrane, extracellular matrix and sub-membrane cellular components. (GO biological_process)
name: establishment or maintenance of apical/basal cell polarity

intent: establishment of apical/basal cell polarity - The specification and formation of the polarity of a cell along its apical/basal axis. (GO biological_process)
name: establishment of apical/basal cell polarity

intent: maintenance of apical/basal cell polarity - Retaining the established polarization of a cell along its apical/basal axis. (GO biological_process)
name: maintenance of apical/basal cell polarity

intent: phosphatidylinositol binding - Binding to an inositol-containing glycerophospholipid, i.e. phosphatidylinositol (PtdIns) and its phosphorylated derivatives. [synonyms: phosphoinositide binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: phosphatidylinositol binding

intent: sperm DNA condensation - The progressive compaction of the spermatid chromatin so that it reaches a level of condensation that is not compatible with nuclear activities such as transcription or DNA replication. [synonyms: sperm chromatin condensation; spermatogenesis, exchange of chromosomal proteins] (GO biological_process)
name: sperm DNA condensation

intent: response to nicotine - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nicotine stimulus. (GO biological_process)
name: response to nicotine

intent: behavioral response to nicotine - Any process that results in a change in the behavior of an organism as a result of a nicotine stimulus. [synonyms: behavioural response to nicotine] (GO biological_process)
name: behavioral response to nicotine

intent: larval midgut cell programmed cell death - The stage-specific programmed cell death of cells of the larval midgut, during histolysis of the larval organ. [synonyms: larval midgut cell death; programmed cell death of larval midgut cells] (GO biological_process)
name: larval midgut cell programmed cell death

intent: histone methyltransferase complex - A multimeric complex that is able to catalyze the addition of methyl groups to histone proteins. (GO cellular_component)
name: histone methyltransferase complex

intent: ESC/E(Z) complex - A multimeric protein complex that can methylate lysine-27 and lysine-9 residues of histone H3. In Drosophila the core subunits of the complex include ESC, E(Z), CAF1 (NURF-55) and SU(Z)12. In mammals the core subunits of the complex include EED, EZH2, SUZ12 and RBBP4. [synonyms: Extra Sex Combs/Enhancer of Zeste complex; polycomb repressive complex 2; PRC2 complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: ESC/E(Z) complex

intent: hemocyte migration - The directed movement of a hemocyte within the embryo. Hemocytes are blood cells associated with a hemocoel (the cavity containing most of the major organs of the arthropod body) which are involved in defense and clotting of hemolymph, but not involved in transport of oxygen. In Drosophila, embryonic hemocytes originate from the head mesoderm as a cluster of cells. The cluster splits into two and one group of cells crosses the amnioserosa. Both populations then spread toward the middle of the embryo and then disperse evenly throughout the embryo. [synonyms: arthropod blood cell migration; hemocyte cell migration] (GO biological_process)
name: hemocyte migration

intent: ecdysone binding - Binding to 20-hydroxyecdysone (ecdysone). Ecdysone is an ecdysteroid produced by the prothoracic glands of immature insects and the ovaries of adult females, which stimulates growth and molting. (GO molecular_function)
name: ecdysone binding

intent: FACT complex - A histone chaperone complex that facilitates nucleosome disassembly and reassembly upon DNA or RNA polymerase passage. [synonyms: Facilitates chromatin transcription complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: FACT complex

intent: PRC1 complex - A multiprotein complex that mediates monoubiquitination of lysine residues of histone H2A (lysine-118 in Drosophila or lysine-119 in mammals). The complex is required for stable long-term maintenance of transcriptionally repressed states and is involved in chromatin remodeling. [synonyms: Polycomb repressive complex 1] (GO cellular_component)
name: PRC1 complex

intent: operant conditioning - Learning to anticipate future events on the basis of past experience with the consequences of one's own behavior. [synonyms: instrumental conditioning] (GO biological_process)
name: operant conditioning

intent: appendage morphogenesis - The process in which the anatomical structures of appendages are generated and organized. An appendage is an organ or part that is attached to the trunk of an organism, such as a limb or a branch. (GO biological_process)
name: appendage morphogenesis

intent: limb morphogenesis - The process in which the anatomical structures of a limb are generated and organized. A limb is a paired appendage of a tetrapod used for locomotion or grasping. [synonyms: limb bud morphogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: limb morphogenesis

intent: genitalia morphogenesis - The process in which the anatomical structures of genitalia are generated and organized. The genitalia are the organs of reproduction or generation, external and internal. [synonyms: genital morphogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: genitalia morphogenesis

intent: embryonic appendage morphogenesis - The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the appendage are generated and organized. An appendage is an organ or part that is attached to the trunk of an organism, such as a limb or a branch. (GO biological_process)
name: embryonic appendage morphogenesis

intent: imaginal disc-derived appendage morphogenesis - The process in which the anatomical structures of appendages are generated and organized. An appendage is an organ or part that is attached to the trunk of an organism. (GO biological_process)
name: imaginal disc-derived appendage morphogenesis

intent: embryonic forelimb morphogenesis - The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the forelimb are generated and organized. The forelimbs are the front limbs of an animal, e.g. the arms of a human. [synonyms: embryonic arm morphogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: embryonic forelimb morphogenesis

intent: embryonic hindlimb morphogenesis - The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the hindlimbs are generated and organized. The hindlimbs are the posterior limbs of an animal. (GO biological_process)
name: embryonic hindlimb morphogenesis

intent: embryonic pectoral fin morphogenesis - The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the pectoral fin are generated and organized. Pectoral fins are bilaterally paired fins mounted laterally and located behind the gill covers of fish. These fins are used for lateral mobility and propulsion. (GO biological_process)
name: embryonic pectoral fin morphogenesis

intent: embryonic pelvic fin morphogenesis - The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the pelvic fin are generated and organized. The pelvic fins are bilaterally paired fins mounted in a ventral-lateral position on most fish. These fins are used primarily for lateral mobility and propulsion. (GO biological_process)
name: embryonic pelvic fin morphogenesis

intent: post-embryonic appendage morphogenesis - The process, occurring after embryonic development, by which the anatomical structures of an appendage are generated and organized. An appendage is an organ or part that is attached to the trunk of an organism, such as a limb or a branch. (GO biological_process)
name: post-embryonic appendage morphogenesis

intent: embryonic medial fin morphogenesis - The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the medial fin are generated and organized. Medial fins are unpaired fins of fish, usually located dorsomedially or ventromedially and primarily used for stability while swimming. [synonyms: embryonic unpaired fin morphogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: embryonic medial fin morphogenesis

intent: embryonic dorsal fin morphogenesis - The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the dorsal fin are generated and organized. A dorsal fin is an unpaired medial fin on the dorsal aspect of a fish that provides lateral stability while swimming. Generally fish have one or two dorsal fins. (GO biological_process)
name: embryonic dorsal fin morphogenesis

intent: embryonic caudal fin morphogenesis - The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the caudal fin are generated and organized. The caudal fin is an unpaired medial fin mounted at the caudal end of the fish and is the main fin used for propulsion. (GO biological_process)
name: embryonic caudal fin morphogenesis

intent: embryonic anal fin morphogenesis - The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the embryonic anal fin are generated and organized. An anal fin is an unpaired medial fin on the ventral aspect near the caudal end of a fish, which provides lateral stability while swimming. (GO biological_process)
name: embryonic anal fin morphogenesis

intent: post-embryonic genitalia morphogenesis - The process, occurring after embryonic development, by which the anatomical structures of the genitalia are generated and organized. [synonyms: post-embryonic genital morphogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: post-embryonic genitalia morphogenesis

intent: post-embryonic limb morphogenesis - The process, occurring after embryonic development, by which the anatomical structures of the limb are generated and organized. A limb is an appendage of an animal used for locomotion or grasping. (GO biological_process)
name: post-embryonic limb morphogenesis

name: post-embryonic forelimb morphogenesis

intent: post-embryonic hindlimb morphogenesis - The process, occurring after embryonic development, by which the anatomical structures of the hindlimb are generated and organized. (GO biological_process)

name: post-embryonic pectoral fin morphogenesis

name: post-embryonic pelvic fin morphogenesis

[synonyms: post-embryonic unpaired fin morphogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: post-embryonic medial fin morphogenesis

name: post-embryonic caudal fin morphogenesis

name: post-embryonic dorsal fin morphogenesis

name: post-embryonic anal fin morphogenesis

name: forelimb morphogenesis

name: hindlimb morphogenesis

Pectoral fins are bilaterally paired fins mounted laterally and located behind the gill covers of fish. These fins are used for lateral mobility and propulsion. (GO biological_process)
name: pectoral fin morphogenesis

name: pelvic fin morphogenesis

name: medial fin morphogenesis

A dorsal fin is an unpaired medial fin on the dorsal aspect of fish that provides lateral stability while swimming. Generally fish have one or two dorsal fins. (GO biological_process)
name: dorsal fin morphogenesis

name: caudal fin morphogenesis
