intent: mast cell migration - The movement of a mast cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body. (GO biological_process)
name: mast cell migration

intent: stress response to acid chemical - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a disturbance in organismal or cellular homeostasis caused by the chemical structure of the anion portion of a dissociated acid (rather than the acid acting as a proton donor). The acid chemical may be in gaseous, liquid or solid form. [synonyms: response to acid stress; stress response to acid] (GO biological_process)
name: stress response to acid chemical

intent: cellular stress response to acid chemical - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a disturbance in cellular homeostasis caused by the chemical structure of the anion portion of a dissociated acid (rather than the acid acting as a proton donor). The acid chemical may be in gaseous, liquid or solid form. [synonyms: cellular response to acid stress; cellular stress response to acid] (GO biological_process)
name: cellular stress response to acid chemical

intent: lymphoid lineage cell migration - The orderly movement of a lymphoid lineage cell from one site to another. A lymphoid lineage cell, also called a lymphoid lineage restricted progenitor cell, is a progenitor cell restricted to the lymphoid lineage. [synonyms: lymphoid lineage restricted progenitor cell migration] (GO biological_process)
name: lymphoid lineage cell migration

intent: lymphoid lineage cell migration into thymus - The movement of a lymphoid lineage cell (also called a lymphoid lineage restricted progenitor cell) into the thymus. Lymphoid lineage cells enter and exit the thymus several times as part of this process. [synonyms: lymphoid lineage restricted progenitor cell migration into thymus] (GO biological_process)
name: lymphoid lineage cell migration into thymus

intent: thymus epithelium morphogenesis - The process in which the thymus epithelium is generated and organized. [synonyms: thymic epithelium morphogenesis] (GO biological_process)
name: thymus epithelium morphogenesis

intent: Y-shaped link - A Y-shaped protein complex in the ciliary transition zone that connects the cilium axoneme to the ciliary necklace. Both protein sorting and protein gating occur at this point in the cilium allowing some, but not all proteins to enter the cilium. [synonyms: membrane-microtubule complex; Y-link; Y-link structure; Y-shaped assemblage; Y-shaped fiber; Y-shaped fibre; Y-shaped linker] (GO cellular_component)
name: Y-shaped link

intent: ciliary necklace - A protein complex located on the cilium membrane in the ciliary transition zone; it is connected to the cilium axoneme via Y-shaped links. [synonyms: cilial necklace; cilium necklace] (GO cellular_component)
name: ciliary necklace

intent: ciliary transition fiber - A nine-bladed, propeller-like protein complex that links the distal end of the basal body and the cilium to the plasma membrane. Functions in protein sorting and gating (i.e. active and passive transport of proteins in and out of the cilium). [synonyms: cilial transition fiber; cilial transition fibre; ciliary transition fibre; cilium transition fiber; cilium transition fibre; centriolar distal appendage; distal appendage of basal body; distal appendage of centriole; distal appendage of mother centriole; transition fiber; transition fibre] (GO cellular_component)
name: ciliary transition fiber

intent: axonemal central pair - Part of the axoneme consisting of the inner two microtubule doublets of the 9+2 axoneme occurring in most motile cilia. [synonyms: axonemal microtubule central pair; axoneme central pair; axoneme microtubule central pair; central-pair microtubules; central pair] (GO cellular_component)
name: axonemal central pair

intent: axonemal basal plate - Part of the axoneme consisting of a highly electron-dense region at the distal end of the ciliary transition zone within the axonemal lumen at which the axonemal central pair of microtubules is connected to the rest of the axonemal structure. [synonyms: axoneme basal plate; basal plate] (GO cellular_component)
name: axonemal basal plate

intent: ciliary tip - Part of the cilium where the axoneme ends. The ciliary tip has been implicated in ciliary assembly and disassembly, as well as signal transduction. [synonyms: cilial tip; cilium tip; flagellar tip; flagellum tip] (GO cellular_component)
name: ciliary tip

intent: ciliary inversin compartment - Proximal part of the ciliary shaft to which the inversin protein (also called Inv) specifically localizes. The inversin compartment appears to have a different protein composition than the rest of the cilium, although there is no structure that separates it form the distal part of the cilium. [synonyms: cilial inversin compartment; cilium inversin compartment; flagellar inversin compartment; flagellum inversin compartment; Inv compartment of the cilium; inversin compartment] (GO cellular_component)
name: ciliary inversin compartment

intent: ciliary shaft - The mid part of a cilium between the ciliary base and ciliary tip that extends into the extracellular space. [synonyms: cilial shaft; cilium shaft; flagellar shaft; flagellum shaft] (GO cellular_component)
name: ciliary shaft

intent: axonemal doublet microtubule - A cellular anatomical entity that is part of an axoneme consisting of a doublet microtubule. [synonyms: axonemal outer doublet; axoneme outer doublet; DMT; outer-doublet microtubules; outer doublet] (GO cellular_component)
name: axonemal doublet microtubule

intent: ciliary base - Area of the cilium (also called flagellum) where the basal body and the axoneme are anchored to the plasma membrane. The ciliary base encompasses the distal part of the basal body, transition fibers and transition zone and is structurally and functionally very distinct from the rest of the cilium. In this area proteins are sorted and filtered before entering the cilium, and many ciliary proteins localize specifically to this area. [synonyms: cilial base; cilium base; flagellar base; flagellum base] (GO cellular_component)
name: ciliary base

intent: synaptic vesicle protein transport vesicle - A cytoplasmic vesicle composed of both tubulovesicular and clear core vesicles that transport synaptic vesicle-associated proteins. Proteins carried by synaptic vesicle protein transport vesicles (STVs) include synaptophysin, synapsin Ia, synaptotagmin and synaptobrevin/vesicle-associated membrane protein 2 (VAMP2). STVs are packaged via the trans-Golgi network before being transported through the axon. [synonyms: STV] (GO cellular_component)
name: synaptic vesicle protein transport vesicle

intent: seed abscission - The controlled shedding of a seed. (GO biological_process)
name: seed abscission

intent: transcription preinitiation complex - A protein-DNA complex composed of proteins binding promoter DNA to form the transcriptional preinitiation complex (PIC), the formation of which is a prerequisite for transcription. [synonyms: DNA-templated transcriptional preinitiation complex; transcriptional pre-initiation complex; transcriptional preinitiation complex; PIC; preinitiation complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: transcription preinitiation complex

intent: mitochondrial double-strand break repair - The repair of double-strand breaks in mitochondrial DNA via homologous and nonhomologous mechanisms to reform a continuous DNA helix. [synonyms: mtDSB repair] (GO biological_process)
name: mitochondrial double-strand break repair

intent: mitochondrial double-strand break repair via homologous recombination - The repair of a double-strand break in mitochondrial DNA in which the broken DNA molecule is repaired using homologous sequences. [synonyms: mtDSB repair via homologous recombination] (GO biological_process)
name: mitochondrial double-strand break repair via homologous recombination

intent: calcium ion transmembrane import into cytosol - A process in which a calcium ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other into the cytosol by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. [synonyms: calcium transmembrane import into cytosol; cytosolic calcium ion transport] (GO biological_process)
name: calcium ion transmembrane import into cytosol

intent: left anterior flagellum - A cilium (also called flagellum) found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It originates at the left anterior basal body, extends laterally through the cytoplasm, crosses the right anterior axoneme, and exits as a membrane-bound flagellum on the anterior left side of the cell. [synonyms: left anterior cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: left anterior flagellum

intent: right anterior flagellum - A cilium (also called flagellum) found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It originates at the right anterior basal body, extends laterally through the cytoplasm, crosses the left anterior axoneme, and exits as a membrane-bound flagellum on the anterior right side of the cell. [synonyms: right anterior cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: right anterior flagellum

intent: left posteriolateral flagellum - A cilium (also called flagellum) found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is nucleated by the left posteriolateral basal body and extends cytoplasmically toward the cell posterior, marking the left anterior boundary of the lateral shield and the left lateral region of the funis before exiting at the left lateral region of the cell body. [synonyms: left posteriolateral cilium; left posterolateral cilium; left posterolateral flagellum] (GO cellular_component)
name: left posteriolateral flagellum

intent: right posteriolateral flagellum - A cilium (also called flagellum) found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is nucleated by the right posteriolateral basal body and extends cytoplasmically toward the cell posterior, marking the right anterior boundary of the lateral shield and the right lateral region of the funis before exiting at the right lateral region of the cell body. [synonyms: right posteriolateral cilium; right posterolateral cilium; right posterolateral flagellum] (GO cellular_component)
name: right posteriolateral flagellum

intent: left ventral flagellum - A cilium (also called flagellum) found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is nucleated by the left ventral basal body and exits the cell body proximally and dorsal to the ventral disc. [synonyms: left ventral cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: left ventral flagellum

intent: right ventral flagellum - A cilium (also called flagellum) found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is nucleated by the right ventral basal body and exits the cell body proximally and dorsal to the ventral disc. [synonyms: right ventral cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: right ventral flagellum

intent: left caudal flagellum - A cilium (also called flagellum) found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is nucleated by the left caudal basal body, extending cytoplasmically and exiting at the posterior end of the cell body. [synonyms: left caudal cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: left caudal flagellum

intent: right caudal flagellum - A cilium (also called flagellum) found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is nucleated by the right caudal basal body, extending cytoplasmically and exiting at the posterior end of the cell body. [synonyms: right caudal cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: right caudal flagellum

intent: left lateral basal body pair - Set of two basal bodies found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It comprises the anterior and ventral basal bodies located to the right of the left nucleus of the trophozoite when viewed dorsally. (GO cellular_component)
name: left lateral basal body pair

intent: left middle basal body pair - Set of two basal bodies found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It comprises the caudal and posteriolateral basal bodies located to the right of the left nucleus of the trophozoite when viewed dorsally. (GO cellular_component)
name: left middle basal body pair

intent: right lateral basal body pair - Set of two basal bodies found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It comprises the anterior and ventral basal bodies located to the left of the right nucleus of the trophozoite when viewed dorsally. (GO cellular_component)
name: right lateral basal body pair

intent: right middle basal body pair - Set of two basal bodies found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It comprises the caudal and posteriolateral basal bodies located to the left of the right nucleus of the trophozoite when viewed dorsally. (GO cellular_component)
name: right middle basal body pair

intent: left tetrad - Set of four basal bodies found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It comprises the left lateral basal body pair and the left middle basal body pair (i.e. the anterior, ventral, caudal and posteriolateral basal bodies located to the right of the left nucleus of the trophozoite when viewed dorsally). (GO cellular_component)
name: left tetrad

intent: right tetrad - Set of four basal bodies found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It comprises the right lateral basal body pair and the right middle basal body pair (i.e. the anterior, ventral, caudal and posteriolateral basal bodies located to the left of the right nucleus of the trophozoite when viewed dorsally). (GO cellular_component)
name: right tetrad

intent: median body - A non-membrane bound, semi-organized microtubule array of unknown function found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is located on the dorsal side of the trophozoite, slightly posterior to the ventral disc. [synonyms: parabasal body] (GO cellular_component)
name: median body

intent: lateral shield - Region of the ventral side of the cell body found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is located posterior on either side of the ventral groove; the upper boundary is the ventral disc, and the lower boundary is marked by the posteriolateral flagella. (GO cellular_component)
name: lateral shield

intent: cyst wall - The specialized envelope lying outside the cell membrane of a cyst. A cyst is a resting or dormant stage of a microorganism, usually a bacterium or a protist or rarely an invertebrate animal, that helps the organism to survive in unfavorable environmental conditions. In protists such as protozoan parasites alternating cystic- and non-cystic stages, the cyst wall is usually composed of carbohydrates and proteins. (GO cellular_component)
name: cyst wall

intent: left nucleus - One of the two nuclei found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is located on the left side of the cell when viewed from the dorsal side. (GO cellular_component)
name: left nucleus

intent: right nucleus - One of the two nuclei found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It is located on the right side of the cell when viewed from the dorsal side. (GO cellular_component)
name: right nucleus

intent: lateral part of cell - The region of a polarized cell other than its tips or ends (in some cell types, one end may be called the apex and the other the base). For example, in a polarized epithelial cell, the lateral part includes the cell sides which interface adjacent cells. (GO cellular_component)
name: lateral part of cell

intent: lateral cell cortex - The region directly beneath the plasma membrane of the lateral portion of the cell. (GO cellular_component)
name: lateral cell cortex

intent: vacuole fusion - Merging of two or more vacuoles, or of vacuoles and vesicles within a cell to form a single larger vacuole. (GO biological_process)
name: vacuole fusion

intent: lamellipodium organization - A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a lamellipodium. A lamellipodium is a thin sheetlike process extended by the leading edge of a crawling fibroblast; contains a dense meshwork of actin filaments. (GO biological_process)
name: lamellipodium organization

intent: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt1p-Pmt2p dimer complex - A protein dimer complex that possesses dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase activity and, in S. cerevisiae, is composed of Pmt1p-Pmt2p. [synonyms: Pmt1p-Pmt2p complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt1p-Pmt2p dimer complex

intent: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt1p-Pmt3p dimer complex - A protein dimer complex that possesses dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase activity and, in S. cerevisiae, is composed of Pmt1p-Pmt3p. [synonyms: Pmt1p-Pmt3p complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt1p-Pmt3p dimer complex

intent: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt5p-Pmt2p dimer complex - A protein dimer complex that possesses dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase activity and, in S. cerevisiae, is composed of Pmt5p-Pmt2p. [synonyms: Pmt5p-Pmt2p complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt5p-Pmt2p dimer complex

intent: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt5p-Pmt3p dimer complex - A protein dimer complex that possesses dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase activity and, in S. cerevisiae, is composed of Pmt5p-Pmt3p. [synonyms: Pmt5p-Pmt3p complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt5p-Pmt3p dimer complex

intent: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt4p homodimer complex - A protein dimer complex that possesses dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase activity and, in S. cerevisiae, is composed of Pmt4p. [synonyms: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt4p dimer; dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt4p-Pmt4p dimer complex; Pmt4p-Pmt4p complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase Pmt4p homodimer complex

intent: MutLgamma complex - A heterodimer involved in the recognition of base-base and small insertion/deletion mismatches. In S. cerevisiae the complex consists of two subunits, Mlh1 and Mlh3. (GO cellular_component)
name: MutLgamma complex

intent: archaeal or bacterial-type flagellum-dependent cell motility - Cell motility due to movement of bacterial- or archaeal-type flagella. (GO biological_process)
name: archaeal or bacterial-type flagellum-dependent cell motility

intent: archaeal-type flagellum - A non-membrane-bounded organelle superficially similar to a bacterial-type flagellum; they both consist of filaments extending outside the cell, and rotate to propel the cell, but the archaeal flagella (also called archaella) have a unique structure which lacks a central channel. Similar to bacterial type IV pilins, the archaeal flagellins (archaellins) are made with class 3 signal peptides and they are processed by a type IV prepilin peptidase-like enzyme. The archaellins are typically modified by the addition of N-linked glycans which are necessary for proper assembly and/or function. [synonyms: archaellum; archaeal flagellum; archaella] (GO cellular_component)
name: archaeal-type flagellum

intent: archaeal-type flagellum-dependent cell motility - Cell motility due to the motion of one or more archaeal-type flagella. An archaeal-type flagellum (also called archaellum) is a non-membrane-bounded organelle superficially similar to a bacterial-type flagellum, but having a different molecular structure and lacking a central channel. [synonyms: archaeal-type flagellar cell motility] (GO biological_process)
name: archaeal-type flagellum-dependent cell motility

intent: ventral disc lateral crest - Fibrillar repetitive structure surrounding the ventral disc edge in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). The composition of the lateral crest is not fully known yet. [synonyms: ventral disk lateral crest; lateral crest] (GO cellular_component)
name: ventral disc lateral crest

intent: ventral disc overlap zone - A region of the ventral disc of Giardia species (trophozoite stage) where two portions of the same array of microtubules overlap (the microtubule array makes a complete circle and overlaps on itself). [synonyms: ventral disk overlap zone; overlap zone] (GO cellular_component)
name: ventral disc overlap zone

intent: ventral disc microtubule array - A part of the ventral disc of Giardia species (trophozoite stage) consisting of a spiral array of microtubules linked to the ventral membrane. These microtubules form the base of the ventral disc dorsal microribbons that extend nearly perpendicular from the membrane. [synonyms: ventral disc spiral microtubule array; ventral disk microtubule array; spiral microtubule array] (GO cellular_component)
name: ventral disc microtubule array

intent: ventral disc dorsal microribbon - Trilaminar structure extending perpendicularly into the cytoplasm along the length of ventral disc microtubules in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). Constituents of dorsal microribbons (also called dorsal ribbons or microribbons) include alpha-coiled-helix proteins approximately 29 to 38 kDa in size. These proteins line the edges of the microribbons but are not found in microtubules. Tubulins are not found in microribbons. [synonyms: ventral disk dorsal microribbon; dorsal microribbon; dorsal ribbon; microribbon] (GO cellular_component)
name: ventral disc dorsal microribbon

intent: ventral disc crossbridge - Structure horizontally linking adjacent microribbons of the ventral disc in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). The composition of crossbridges is not fully known yet. [synonyms: ventral disk crossbridge; crossbridge] (GO cellular_component)
name: ventral disc crossbridge

intent: ventral disc supernumerary microtubule array - A partial left-handed spiral array of microtubules that lies generally dorsal to the main ventral disc microtubule array in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). [synonyms: ventral disk supernumerary microtubule array; supernumerary microtubule array] (GO cellular_component)
name: ventral disc supernumerary microtubule array

intent: ventral disc - Specialized organelle found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage) and characterized by a spiral array of microtubules and microtubule-associated structures including dorsal microribbons and crossbridges. The edge of the ventral disc narrows into a lateral crest. The ventral disk mediates mechanical attachment of the trophozoite to the host's intestinal wall, and contains the contractile proteins actinin, alpha-actinin, myosin, and tropomyosin working towards contraction of the disk involved in adherence. [synonyms: ventral adhesive disc; adhesive disc; ventral disk] (GO cellular_component)
name: ventral disc

intent: sperm cytoplasmic droplet - A small amount of cytoplasm surrounded by a cell membrane that is generally retained in spermatozoa after spermiogenesis, when the majority of the cytoplasm is phagocytosed by Sertoli cells to produce what are called residual bodies. Initially, the droplet is located at the neck just behind the head of an elongated spermatid. During epididymal transit, the cytoplasmic droplet migrates caudally to the annulus at the end of the midpiece; the exact position and time varies by species. The cytoplasmic droplet consists of lipids, lipoproteins, RNAs, a variety of hydrolytic enzymes, receptors, ion channels, and Golgi-derived vesicles. The droplet may be involved in regulatory volume loss (RVD) at ejaculation, and in most species, though not in humans, the cytoplasmic droplet is lost at ejaculation. Note that the cytoplasmic droplet is distinct from 'excessive residual cytoplasm' that sometimes remains in epididymal spermatozoa, particularly when spermiogenesis has been disrupted. [synonyms: sperm residual cytoplasm] (GO cellular_component)
name: sperm cytoplasmic droplet

intent: xylanase activity - Catalysis of the hydrolysis of xylans, homopolysaccharides composed of xylose residues. [synonyms: xylosidase activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: xylanase activity

intent: exoxylanase activity - A xylanase activity that acts on one of the ends of a xylan polymer which does not contain side chains. (GO molecular_function)
name: exoxylanase activity

intent: retina blood vessel maintenance - A retina homeostatic process preventing the degeneration of a retina blood vessel. [synonyms: maintenance of retina blood vessel; maintenance of retinal blood vessel; maintenance of choriocapillaris] (GO biological_process)
name: retina blood vessel maintenance

intent: cullin family protein binding - Binding to a member of the cullin family, hydrophobic proteins that act as scaffolds for ubiquitin ligases (E3). [synonyms: cullin binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: cullin family protein binding

intent: temperature-gated ion channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of an ion by a channel that opens in response to a temperature stimulus (e.g. exposure to a temperature range different than the optimal temperature for that organism). [synonyms: temperature gated ion channel activity; temperature-activated ion channel activity; temperature-dependent ion channel activity; heat-activated ion channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: temperature-gated ion channel activity

intent: temperature-gated cation channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of a cation by a channel that opens in response to a temperature stimulus (e.g. exposure to a temperature range different than the optimal temperature for that organism). [synonyms: temperature gated cation channel activity; temperature-activated cation channel activity; temperature-dependent cation channel activity; heat-activated cation channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: temperature-gated cation channel activity

intent: transverse flagellum - A motile cilium found in dinoflagellates. It coils around the cell and provides the forward thrust for motility. It is often contained in a furrow called the cingulum, and emerges from a flagellar pore located in the cingulum. [synonyms: transverse cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: transverse flagellum

intent: longitudinal flagellum - A motile cilium found in dinoflagellates. It trails the cell and acts as a steering rudder. It is often partially contained in a furrow called the sulcus, and emerges from a flagellar pore located in the sulcus. [synonyms: longitudinal cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: longitudinal flagellum

intent: cell surface furrow - A furrow that may be found on the cell surface. Examples include the cingulum and sulcus found in some dinoflagellates. [synonyms: cell surface groove; furrow; groove] (GO cellular_component)
name: cell surface furrow

intent: dinoflagellate cingulum - A cell surface furrow that wraps around a dinoflagellate cell; the transverse flagellum lies in it. [synonyms: girdle; transverse groove; cingulum] (GO cellular_component)
name: dinoflagellate cingulum

intent: dinoflagellate sulcus - A cell surface furrow that occurs on the ventral side of a dinoflagellate cell. It partially houses the longitudinal flagellum. The sulcus intersects with the cingulum on the ventral side of a dinoflagellate cell. [synonyms: longitudinal furrow; longitudinal groove; sulcus] (GO cellular_component)
name: dinoflagellate sulcus

intent: dinoflagellate epicone - The part of a dinoflagellate cell above the cingulum; also referred to as the anterior portion of a dinoflagellate cell. It is separated from the hypocone by the cingulum. [synonyms: episome; epitheca; epicone] (GO cellular_component)
name: dinoflagellate epicone

intent: dinoflagellate hypocone - The part of a dinoflagellate cell below the cingulum; also referred to as the posterior portion of a dinoflagellate cell. It is separated from the epicone by the cingulum. [synonyms: hyposome; hypotheca; hypocone] (GO cellular_component)
name: dinoflagellate hypocone

intent: dinoflagellate sulcal notch - A dinoflagellate sulcus that extends all the way to the posterior end of the cell (also known as antapex). The presence of a sulcal notch makes the dinoflagellate hypocone appear bilobed. [synonyms: dinoflagellate sulcus notch; sulcal notch] (GO cellular_component)
name: dinoflagellate sulcal notch

intent: PTEX complex - A protein complex that acts as a protein trafficking machinery and is responsible for the export of proteins across the parasitophorous (symbiont-containing) vacuolar membrane and into the human host cell. The PTEX complex is located in the vacuole membrane. It is ATP-powered, and comprises heat shock protein 101 (HSP101; a ClpA/B-like ATPase from the AAA+ superfamily, of a type commonly associated with protein translocons), a parasite protein termed PTEX150, and exported protein 2 (EXP2). EXP2 is the potential channel, as it is the membrane-associated component of the core PTEX complex. Two other proteins, PTEX88 and thioredoxin 2 (TRX2), were also identified as PTEX components. [synonyms: Plasmodium translocon of exported proteins] (GO cellular_component)
name: PTEX complex

intent: (R)-mandelate dehydrogenase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: (R)-mandelate + NAD+ = phenylglyoxylate + NADH + H+. [synonyms: D-mandelate dehydrogenase activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: (R)-mandelate dehydrogenase activity

intent: monoamine oxidase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: RCH2NHR' + H2O + O2 = RCHO + R'NH2 + H2O2. [synonyms: amine:oxygen oxidoreductase (deaminating) activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: monoamine oxidase activity

intent: cytoplasmic translational elongation through polyproline stretches - The successive addition of amino acid residues to a nascent polypeptide chain, proceeding through regions of multiple repeated proline codons, during protein biosynthesis in the cytoplasm. (GO biological_process)
name: cytoplasmic translational elongation through polyproline stretches

intent: potassium ion export across plasma membrane - The directed movement of potassium ions from inside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the extracellular region. [synonyms: potassium export across plasma membrane; potassium ion export from cell; potassium export; potassium ion export] (GO biological_process)
name: potassium ion export across plasma membrane

intent: UDP-galactose transmembrane import into Golgi lumen - The directed movement of UDP-galactose into the Golgi lumen across the Golgi membrane. [synonyms: UDP-galactose import into Golgi lumen] (GO biological_process)
name: UDP-galactose transmembrane import into Golgi lumen

intent: low-affinity basic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of basic amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Basic amino acids have a pH above 7. In low-affinity transport the transporter is able to bind the solute only if it is present at very high concentrations. [synonyms: low affinity basic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: low-affinity basic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity

intent: low-affinity L-arginine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-arginine from one side of a membrane to the other. In low-affinity transport the transporter is able to bind the solute only if it is present at very high concentrations. [synonyms: low affinity L-arginine transmembrane transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: low-affinity L-arginine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: high-affinity L-ornithine transmembrane transporter activity - Enables the transfer of L-ornithine from one side of a membrane to the other. In high-affinity transport the transporter is able to bind the solute even if it is only present at very low concentrations. [synonyms: high affinity L-ornithine transmembrane transporter activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: high-affinity L-ornithine transmembrane transporter activity

intent: distal tip cell migration - The orderly movement of a distal tip cell. (GO biological_process)
name: distal tip cell migration

intent: extrinsic component of omegasome membrane - The component of the omegasome membrane consisting of gene products and protein complexes that are loosely bound to one of its surfaces, but not integrated into the hydrophobic region. [synonyms: extrinsic to omegasome membrane; omegasome peripheral membrane] (GO cellular_component)
name: extrinsic component of omegasome membrane

intent: extrinsic component of phagophore assembly site membrane - The component of the phagophore assembly site membrane consisting of gene products and protein complexes that are loosely bound to one of its surfaces, but not integrated into the hydrophobic region. [synonyms: extrinsic to phagophore assembly site membrane; extrinsic component of pre-autophagosomal structure membrane; phagophore assembly site peripheral membrane] (GO cellular_component)
name: extrinsic component of phagophore assembly site membrane

intent: L-arginine import across plasma membrane - The directed movement of L-arginine from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol. [synonyms: L-arginine import into cell; arginine import] (GO biological_process)
name: L-arginine import across plasma membrane

name: A axonemal microtubule

intent: phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex, class I - A phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex that contains a catalytic and a regulatory subunit of a phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) enzyme, plus one or more adaptor proteins. Class I PI3Ks phosphorylate phosphatidylinositol [PI], phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate [PI(4)P] and phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate [PI(4,5)P2], and are divided into subclasses A and B according to the type of adaptor subunit with which they associate. The class I PI3K subfamily of genes comprises members in vertebrates, worm and fly, but none in yeast. [synonyms: class I phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex; class I PI3K complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex, class I

intent: phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex, class II - A phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex that contains a catalytic subunit of a phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) enzyme and one or more adaptor proteins. There is no known obligatory regulatory subunit. The class II PI3K (PI3KC2) subfamily of genes has members in vertebrates, worm and fly, but none in yeast. [synonyms: class II phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex; class II PI3K complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex, class II

intent: unencapsulated part of cell - The part of a cell encompassing the intracellular environment and the plasma membrane; it excludes any external encapsulating structures. [synonyms: non-encapsulated part of cell] (GO cellular_component)
name: unencapsulated part of cell

intent: platelet SNARE complex - A SNARE complex that is capable of fusing intracellular vesicles to the plasma membrane of platelets for exocytosis of alpha-granules or dense granules. Contains isoforms of VAMP, SNAP and syntaxin proteins. Ternary SNARE complexes interact in a circular array to form ring complexes or channels around the membrane fusion. A common composition in human is VAMP-8, SNAP-23 and syntaxin-2 or -4. (GO cellular_component)
name: platelet SNARE complex

intent: serpin family protein binding - Binding to a member of the serpin protein family (serine protease inhibitors or classified inhibitor family I4). Serpins are a broadly distributed family of protease inhibitors that use a conformational change to inhibit target enzymes. They are central in controlling many important proteolytic cascades. The majority of serpins inhibit serine proteases, but serpins that inhibit caspases and papain-like cysteine proteases have also been identified. Rarely, serpins perform a non-inhibitory function; for example, several human serpins function as hormone transporters and certain serpins function as molecular chaperones or tumor suppressors. (GO molecular_function)
name: serpin family protein binding

intent: cell-cell self recognition - A cell-cell recognition process by which a cell distinguishes between self and non self during cooperative behavior, such as early development. [synonyms: kin discrimination; kin recognition; self recognition] (GO biological_process)

In S. cerevisiae, this complex contains the ubiquitin ligases Asi1p and Asi3p. (GO cellular_component)

name: SCF-Rcy1/Pof6 ubiquitin ligase complex

intent: SCF-Saf1/Pof9 ubiquitin ligase complex - An SCF ubiquitin ligase complex in which the F-box protein is Saf1 in S. cerevisiae (Pof9 in S. pombe). (GO cellular_component)
name: SCF-Saf1/Pof9 ubiquitin ligase complex

intent: SCF-Skp2 ubiquitin ligase complex - An SCF ubiquitin ligase complex in which the F-box protein is Skp2 in S. cerevisiae. (GO cellular_component)

intent: SCF-YDR131C ubiquitin ligase complex - An SCF ubiquitin ligase complex in which the F-box protein is YDR131C in S. cerevisiae. (GO cellular_component)

name: SCF-Pof5 ubiquitin ligase complex

intent: SCF-Ucc1 ubiquitin ligase complex - An SCF ubiquitin ligase complex in which the F-box protein is YLR224W in S. cerevisiae. [synonyms: SCF-YLR224W ubiquitin ligase complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: SCF-Ucc1 ubiquitin ligase complex

intent: SCF-YLR352W ubiquitin ligase complex - An SCF ubiquitin ligase complex in which the F-box protein is YLR352W in S. cerevisiae. (GO cellular_component)

name: SCF-Hrt3/Pof7 ubiquitin ligase complex

intent: STAT family protein binding - Binding to a member of the signal transducers and activators of transcription (STAT) protein family. STATs are, as the name indicates, both signal transducers and transcription factors. STATs are activated by cytokines and some growth factors and thus control important biological processes including cell growth, cell differentiation, apoptosis and immune responses. [synonyms: signal transducers and activators of transcription family protein binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: STAT family protein binding

intent: SOCS family protein binding - Binding to a member of the suppressor of cytokine signaling (SOCS) family of proteins. SOCS represent an important mechanism to extinguish cytokine and growth factor receptor signaling. Individual SOCS proteins are typically induced by specific cytokines and growth factors, thereby generating a negative feedback loop. SOCS proteins have important functions in development and homeostasis, and in disease, particularly tumor suppression and anti-inflammatory functions. [synonyms: suppressor of cytokine signaling family protein binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: SOCS family protein binding

intent: double-strand break repair via classical nonhomologous end joining - An instance of double-strand break repair via nonhomologous end joining that requires a number of factors important for V(D)J recombination, including the KU70/80 heterodimer (KU), XRCC4, ligase IV, and DNA-PKcs in mammals. It does not produce translocations (as opposed to the alternative nonhomologous end joining). [synonyms: canonical nonhomologous end joining; C-NHEJ] (GO biological_process)
name: double-strand break repair via classical nonhomologous end joining

intent: double-strand break repair via alternative nonhomologous end joining - An instance of double-strand break repair via nonhomologous end joining that is independent of factors important for V(D)J recombination (as opposed to classical nonhomologous end joining). It often results in a deletion with microhomology (i.e. 5-25bp homology) at the repair junction. Among different subclasses of nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ), alternative NHEJ appears to play a significant role in the etiology of mutations that arise during cancer development and treatment. [synonyms: double-strand break repair via microhomology-mediated end joining; A-NHEJ; alt-NHEJ; MMEJ] (GO biological_process)
name: double-strand break repair via alternative nonhomologous end joining

intent: intracellularly phosphatidylinositol-3,5-bisphosphate-gated monatomic cation channel activity - Enables the transmembrane transfer of cations by a channel that opens when phosphatidylinositol-3,5-bisphosphate has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts. [synonyms: intracellular phosphatidylinositol-3,5-bisphosphate-sensitive monatomic cation channel activity; intracellular phosphatidylinositol-3,5-bisphosphate-sensitive cation channel activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: intracellularly phosphatidylinositol-3,5-bisphosphate-gated monatomic cation channel activity

intent: dinoflagellate apex - The anterior most point of a dinoflagellate epicone. [synonyms: apex] (GO cellular_component)
name: dinoflagellate apex

intent: dinoflagellate antapex - The anterior most point of a dinoflagellate hypocone. [synonyms: antapex] (GO cellular_component)
name: dinoflagellate antapex

name: dinoflagellate apical groove

intent: dinoflagellate apical horn - A horn-shaped dinoflagellate apex found in thecate species. (GO cellular_component)
name: dinoflagellate apical horn

intent: dinoflagellate antapical horn - A horn-shaped dinoflagellate antapex found in thecate species. (GO cellular_component)
name: dinoflagellate antapical horn

intent: glutamate receptor clustering - The neurotransmitter-gated ion channel clustering process in which glutamate receptors are localized to distinct domains in the cell membrane. [synonyms: glutamatergic receptor clustering] (GO biological_process)
name: glutamate receptor clustering

intent: iron ion transmembrane transporter inhibitor activity - Binds to and stops, prevents, or reduces the activity of an iron ion transmembrane transporter. [synonyms: iron channel inhibitor activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: iron ion transmembrane transporter inhibitor activity

intent: bacterial extracellular vesicle - Small membrane vesicle (< 1 um) that buds off a prokaryotic cell plasma membrane, able to carry proteins, phospholipids, lipopolysaccharides, nucleic acids, viruses, and more. Important in intercellular communication and pathogenesis; can exist within host cells. (GO cellular_component)
name: bacterial extracellular vesicle

intent: ocelloid - Eye-like subcellular structure found in dinoflagellates (a large group of single-celled eukaryotes). Consists of subcellular analogues to a cornea, lens, iris, and retina. Ocelloids are built from pre-existing organelles, including a cornea-like layer made of mitochondria and a retinal body made of anastomosing plastids. (GO cellular_component)
name: ocelloid

intent: establishment of RNA localization to telomere - The directed movement of RNA to a specific location in the telomeric region of a chromosome. [synonyms: establishment of RNA localisation to telomere] (GO biological_process)
name: establishment of RNA localization to telomere

intent: establishment of protein-containing complex localization to telomere - The directed movement of a protein-containing macromolecular complex to a specific location in the telomeric region of a chromosome. [synonyms: establishment of macromolecular complex localisation to telomere; establishment of macromolecular complex localization to telomere] (GO biological_process)
name: establishment of protein-containing complex localization to telomere

intent: cell surface receptor signaling pathway via STAT - An intracellular signal transduction process in which STAT proteins (Signal Transducers and Activators of Transcription) convey a signal to trigger a change in the activity or state of a cell. The STAT cascade begins with receptor activation followed by activation of STAT proteins by kinases. It proceeds through STA dimerization and subsequent nuclear translocation of STAT proteins, and ends with regulation of target gene expression by STAT proteins. [synonyms: kinase activated-STAT cascade; kinase-STAT cascade; receptor signaling pathway via STAT; STAT signalling pathway] (GO biological_process)
name: cell surface receptor signaling pathway via STAT

intent: tRNA (5-carboxymethoxyuridine(34)-5-O)-methyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: 5-carboxymethoxyuridine34 in tRNA + S-adenosyl-L-methionine = 5-methoxycarbonylmethoxyuridine34 in tRNA + S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine. The methylation occurs on the modified base. [synonyms: tRNA 5-carboxymethoxyuridine methyltransferase activity] (GO molecular_function)
name: tRNA (5-carboxymethoxyuridine(34)-5-O)-methyltransferase activity

intent: telomere maintenance via base-excision repair - A telomere maintenance process that occurs by base-excision repair of telomeric DNA in response to DNA damage. Telomeric sequences are particularly susceptible to oxidative DNA damage, due to their G-rich nature. (GO biological_process)
name: telomere maintenance via base-excision repair

intent: vascular endothelial cell response to fluid shear stress - Any response to fluid shear stress in a vascular endothelial cell. [synonyms: blood vessel endothelial cell response to fluid shear stress] (GO biological_process)
name: vascular endothelial cell response to fluid shear stress

intent: vascular endothelial cell response to laminar fluid shear stress - Any response to laminar fluid shear stress in a vascular endothelial cell. [synonyms: blood vessel endothelial cell response to laminar fluid shear stress] (GO biological_process)
name: vascular endothelial cell response to laminar fluid shear stress

intent: response to pulsatile fluid shear stress - Any response to fluid shear stress where the fluid is flowing across a solid surface with periodic variations. For example, the endothelium in straight parts of the artery tree is subjected to pulsatile shear stress with a significant forward direction, which is believed to be an important physiological stimulus enhancing vessel compliance and conferring anti-thrombotic, anti-adhesive, and anti-inflammatory effects. (GO biological_process)
name: response to pulsatile fluid shear stress

intent: response to oscillatory fluid shear stress - Any response to fluid shear stress where the fluid is moving across a solid surface with an oscillatory flow. Disturbed flow patterns at the arterial bifurcations and curvatures may cause endothelial dysfunction, which initiates atherosclerosis. (GO biological_process)
name: response to oscillatory fluid shear stress

intent: cellular response to pulsatile fluid shear stress - Any response to pulsatile fluid shear stress that occurs at the level of a cell. (GO biological_process)
name: cellular response to pulsatile fluid shear stress

intent: cellular response to oscillatory fluid shear stress - Any response to oscillatory fluid shear stress that occurs at the level of a cell. (GO biological_process)
name: cellular response to oscillatory fluid shear stress

intent: vascular endothelial cell response to pulsatile fluid shear stress - Any response to pulsatile fluid shear stress that occurs in a vascular endothelial cell. [synonyms: blood vessel endothelial cell response to pulsatile fluid shear stress] (GO biological_process)
name: vascular endothelial cell response to pulsatile fluid shear stress

intent: vascular endothelial cell response to oscillatory fluid shear stress - Any response to oscillatory fluid shear stress that occurs in a vascular endothelial cell. [synonyms: blood vessel endothelial cell response to oscillatory fluid shear stress] (GO biological_process)
name: vascular endothelial cell response to oscillatory fluid shear stress

intent: ferroptosis - A programmed cell death characterized morphologically by the presence of smaller than normal mitochondria with condensed mitochondrial membrane densities, reduction or vanishing of mitochondria crista, and outer mitochondrial membrane rupture. Activation of mitochondrial voltage-dependent anion channels and mitogen-activated protein kinases, upregulation of endoplasmic reticulum stress, and inhibition of cystine/glutamate antiporter are involved in the induction of ferroptosis. This process is characterized by the accumulation of lipid peroxidation products and lethal reactive oxygen species (ROS) derived from iron metabolism. Glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), heat shock protein beta-1, and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 function as negative regulators of ferroptosis by limiting ROS production and reducing cellular iron uptake, respectively. In contrast, NADPH oxidase and p53 act as positive regulators of ferroptosis by promotion of ROS production and inhibition of expression of SLC7A11 (a specific light-chain subunit of the cystine/glutamate antiporter), respectively. Misregulated ferroptosis has been implicated in multiple physiological and pathological processes. [synonyms: iron-dependent programmed cell death] (GO biological_process)
name: ferroptosis

intent: intracellular vesicle - Any vesicle that is part of the intracellular region. (GO cellular_component)
name: intracellular vesicle

intent: connective tissue replacement - The series of events leading to growth of connective tissue when loss of tissues that are incapable of regeneration occurs, or when fibrinous exudate cannot be adequately cleared. (GO biological_process)
name: connective tissue replacement

intent: viral terminase, small subunit - The part of the viral terminase complex that acts as a phage DNA-recognition component and regulates the activity of the large subunit. The small subunit usually assembles as a heterooligomer with the large subunit. [synonyms: virus terminase, small subunit] (GO cellular_component)
name: viral terminase, small subunit

intent: trans-Golgi to periciliary membrane compartment transport - The directed movement of substances from the trans-Golgi network to the periciliary membrane compartment, the specialized region of the plasma membrane surrounding the base of the cilium including the ciliary pocket, via vesicle-mediated transport. [synonyms: vesicle targeting, trans-Golgi to periciliary membrane compartment] (GO biological_process)
name: trans-Golgi to periciliary membrane compartment transport

intent: dolichol-phosphate-mannose synthase regulator activity - Binds to and modulates the activity of dolichol-phosphate-mannose synthase. (GO molecular_function)
name: dolichol-phosphate-mannose synthase regulator activity

intent: response to viscosity - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a viscosity stimulus. (GO biological_process)
name: response to viscosity

intent: cellular response to viscosity - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a viscosity stimulus. (GO biological_process)
name: cellular response to viscosity

intent: copper ion transport across blood-brain barrier - The directed movement of copper (Cu) ions passing through the blood-brain barrier. [synonyms: copper ion transport across BBB] (GO biological_process)
name: copper ion transport across blood-brain barrier

intent: copper ion transport across blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier - The directed movement of copper (Cu) ions passing through the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier. [synonyms: copper ion transport across BCSFB; copper ion transport across blood-CSF barrier; copper ion transport across blood/cerebrospinal fluid barrier; copper ion transport across blood/CSF barrier; copper ion transport across BCB] (GO biological_process)
name: copper ion transport across blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier

intent: disordered domain specific binding - Binding to a disordered domain of a protein. [synonyms: disordered protein domain specific binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: disordered domain specific binding

intent: neural tissue regeneration - The regrowth of neural tissue following its loss or destruction. [synonyms: neuroregeneration] (GO biological_process)
name: neural tissue regeneration

intent: calcineurin-mediated signaling - Any intracellular signal transduction in which the signal is passed on within the cell by activation of a transcription factor as a consequence of dephosphorylation by Ca(2+)-activated calcineurin. The process begins with calcium-dependent activation of the phosphatase calcineurin. Calcineurin is a calcium- and calmodulin-dependent serine/threonine protein phosphatase with a conserved function in eukaryotic species from yeast to humans. In yeast and fungi, calcineurin regulates stress signaling and cell cycle, and sporulation and virulence in pathogenic fungi. In metazoans, calcineurin is involved in cell commitment, organogenesis and organ development and immune function of T-lymphocytes. By a conserved mechanism, calcineurin phosphatase activates fungal Crz1 and mammalian NFATc by dephosphorylation and translocation of these transcription factors to the nucleus to regulate gene expression. [synonyms: calcineurin-mediated signalling; calcineurin signaling] (GO biological_process)
name: calcineurin-mediated signaling

intent: ciliary vesicle - A Golgi-derived vesicle to which the ciliary basal body docks via its transitional fibers. Its membrane is compositionally distinct from Golgi membranes, and will become the ciliary membrane once the ciliary vesicle is fused to the plasma membrane. The ciliary vesicle is thought to be formed by multiple smaller vesicles that attach to the transitional fibers and then fuse to form a larger vesicle. [synonyms: primary ciliary vesicle; CV] (GO cellular_component)
name: ciliary vesicle

intent: sperm motility - Any process involved in the controlled movement of a sperm cell. [synonyms: sperm movement] (GO biological_process)
name: sperm motility

intent: amoeboid sperm motility - Any process involved in the controlled movement of an amoeboid sperm cell. [synonyms: ameboid sperm motility; ameboid sperm movement; amoeboid sperm movement] (GO biological_process)
name: amoeboid sperm motility

intent: LEM domain binding - Binding to a LEM domain. The LEM domain (for lamina-associated polypeptide, emerin, MAN1 domain) is present in a group of nuclear proteins that bind chromatin through interaction of the LEM motif with the conserved DNA crosslinking protein, barrier-to-autointegration factor (BAF). [synonyms: lamina-associated polypeptide, emerin, MAN1 domain binding; LAP2, emerin, MAN1 domain binding] (GO molecular_function)
name: LEM domain binding

intent: blepharoplast - An intracellular non-membrane-bounded organelle found in multi-ciliated sperm cells of some primitive land plants, and consisting of many radially arranged ninefold symmetric cylinders. The blepharoplast is involved in de novo formation of multiple centrioles; it enlarges and then disintegrates into many procentrioles, which elongate and ultimately nucleate cilia on the surface of the sperm cell. (GO cellular_component)
name: blepharoplast

intent: 9+0 motile cilium - A motile cilium where the axoneme has a ring of nine outer microtubule doublets but no central microtubules (and is therefore called a 9+0 axoneme). [synonyms: motile 9+0 cilium; nodal cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: 9+0 motile cilium

intent: 9+2 motile cilium - A motile cilium where the axoneme has a ring of nine outer microtubule doublets plus two central microtubules (and is therefore called a 9+2 axoneme). [synonyms: motile 9+2 cilium; conventional motile cilium; sperm flagellum] (GO cellular_component)
name: 9+2 motile cilium

intent: non-motile cilium - A cilium which may have a variable array of axonemal microtubules but does not contain molecular motors. [synonyms: immotile cilium; nonmotile cilium; immotile primary cilium; nonmotile primary cilia; nonmotile primary cilium; sensory cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: non-motile cilium

intent: 9+0 non-motile cilium - A non-motile cilium where the axoneme has a ring of nine outer microtubule doublets but no central microtubules (and is therefore called a 9+0 axoneme). [synonyms: 9+0 immotile cilium; non-motile 9+0 cilium; primary cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: 9+0 non-motile cilium

intent: 9+2 non-motile cilium - A non-motile cilium where the axoneme has a ring of nine outer microtubule doublets plus two central microtubules (and is therefore called a 9+2 axoneme). [synonyms: non-motile 9+2 cilium; 9+2 immotile cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: 9+2 non-motile cilium

intent: photoreceptor cell cilium - A specialised 9+0 non-motile cilium found in photoreceptor cells. A ciliary transition zone called 'photoreceptor connecting cilium' links the photoreceptor outer segment to the inner segment. [synonyms: photoreceptor cilium] (GO cellular_component)
name: photoreceptor cell cilium

intent: extracellular exosome biogenesis - The assembly and secretion of an extracellular exosome, a membrane-bounded vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. [synonyms: exosome assembly or secretion; exosome biogenesis; exosome production; ILV assembly; intraluminal vesicle assembly] (GO biological_process)
name: extracellular exosome biogenesis

intent: DIM/DIP cell wall layer - A section of the Actinobacterium-type cell wall composed of (phenyl)phthiocerol, phthiodiolone, phthiotriol dimycocerosate, diphthioceranate and other compounds. (GO cellular_component)
name: DIM/DIP cell wall layer

intent: aerial mycelium formation - The process by which hyphae grow in an upward or outward direction from the surface of the substrate; from there, propagative spores develop in or on characteristic structures that are distinctive of some fungal and bacterial species. The species that form an aerial mycelium develop conidiophores at the ends of the aerial hyphae. [synonyms: aerial hyphal growth; fertile mycelium formation] (GO biological_process)
name: aerial mycelium formation

intent: acquisition of mycelium reproductive competence - A maturation process by which an organism acquires the ability to reproduce. In fungi, reproductive competence only occurs in a population of filamentous cells that form a mycelium. [synonyms: mycelium developmental competence] (GO biological_process)
name: acquisition of mycelium reproductive competence

intent: substrate mycelium formation - The process by which, in some fungal species, hyphae grow as a network of invasive thread-like filaments formed from chains of attached cells within a solid or semi-solid substrate. (GO biological_process)
name: substrate mycelium formation

intent: negative regulation of ferrichrome biosynthetic process in response to iron - Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the rate of ferrichrome biosynthetic process in response to an iron stimulus. (GO biological_process)
name: negative regulation of ferrichrome biosynthetic process in response to iron

intent: paraflagellar rod - A large lattice-like axial structure found in some flagellated protists which extends alongside the axoneme. Protein components of the paraflagellar rod are likely implicated, among other, in adenine nucleotide signaling and metabolism, and in calcium signaling. [synonyms: PFR] (GO cellular_component)
name: paraflagellar rod

intent: mastigoneme - A hair-like structure covering the flagella found in some algae (heterokonts and cryptophytes). It is approximately 15 nm in diameter, and usually consist of a tubular shaft that itself terminates in smaller hairs. It is composed of glycoproteins and, likely, carbohydrates. Mastigonemes may assist in locomotion by increasing the surface area of a flagellum. (GO cellular_component)

intent: fast, calcium ion-dependent exocytosis of neurotransmitter - The fast, initial phase of calcium ion-induced neurotransmitter release, via exocytosis, into the synaptic cleft. [synonyms: synchronous, calcium ion-dependent exocytosis of neurotransmitter] (GO biological_process)
name: fast, calcium ion-dependent exocytosis of neurotransmitter

intent: slow, calcium ion-dependent exocytosis of neurotransmitter - The slow, second phase of calcium ion-induced neurotransmitter release, via exocytosis, into the synaptic cleft. This depends on high affinity calcium sensors and decays slowly, typically with a decay constant of over 100ms. The underlying molecular mechanisms of this process are distinct from those of the earlier, fast phase of release. (GO biological_process)
name: slow, calcium ion-dependent exocytosis of neurotransmitter

intent: cerebellar neuron development - The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cerebellar neuron over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. (GO biological_process)

name: neuronal dense core vesicle

intent: symbiont entry into host cell via disruption of host cell envelope - The disruption by a symbiont of host cell envelope components to allow entry into the host cell. [synonyms: disruption of host cell envelope during viral entry] (GO biological_process)
name: symbiont entry into host cell via disruption of host cell envelope

intent: symbiont entry into host cell via disruption of host cell envelope lipopolysaccharide - The disruption by a symbiont of host cell wall lipopolysaccharides to allow entry into the host cell. [synonyms: degradation of host cell envelope lipopolysaccharide during viral entry; degradation of host lipopolysaccharide during virus entry; disruption by virus of host envelope lipopolysaccharide during virus entry; disassembly by virus of outer membrane lipopolysaccharide during viral entry] (GO biological_process)
name: symbiont entry into host cell via disruption of host cell envelope lipopolysaccharide

intent: symbiont entry into host cell via disruption of host cell glycocalyx - The disruption by a symbiont of host cell capsule to allow entry into the host cell. name: extrinsic component of postsynaptic endosome membrane

intent: symbiont genome ejection through host cell envelope, contractile tail mechanism - Entry of a symbiont's genome into the host cell through the host cell envelope via a contractile tail ejection system consisting of a baseplate, a central tube and an external contractile sheath. Upon binding to the host cell surface, the baseplate changes its conformation and triggers sheath contraction, driving the rigid internal tail tube through the cell envelope. Occurs in non-enveloped prokaryotic viruses. [synonyms: viral contractile tail ejection system; viral genome ejection through host cell envelope, contractile tail mechanism] (GO biological_process)
name: symbiont genome ejection through host cell envelope, contractile tail mechanism

intent: symbiont genome ejection through host cell envelope, long flexible tail mechanism - Entry of a symbiont's genome into the host cell through the host cell envelope via a long, flexible tail ejection system consisting a baseplate, a central tube and a terminator complex which attaches the tail to the phage capsid. Upon binding to the host cell surface, the baseplate changes its conformation and triggers genome ejection into the host cell cytoplasm. Occurs in non-enveloped prokaryotic viruses. [synonyms: viral long flexible tail ejection system; viral genome ejection through host cell envelope, long flexible tail mechanism] (GO biological_process)
name: symbiont genome ejection through host cell envelope, long flexible tail mechanism

intent: symbiont genome ejection through host cell envelope, short tail mechanism - Entry of a symbiont's genome into the host cell through the host cell envelope via a short tail ejection system consisting a central tube, the connector which attaches the tail to the phage capsid and releases inner core proteins. Upon binding to the host cell surface, the phage displays a tube-like extension of its short tail that penetrates both host membranes. This tail extension comes from the release of viral core proteins with channel forming properties. Occurs in non-enveloped prokaryotic viruses. [synonyms: viral short tail ejection system; viral genome ejection through host cell envelope, short tail mechanism] (GO biological_process)
name: symbiont genome ejection through host cell envelope, short tail mechanism

intent: symbiont entry into host cell via permeabilization of endosomal membrane - The entry of a symbiont into a host cell, following endocytosis, via permeabilization of the endosomal membrane by membrane penetration protein(s) of the symbiont. This process mediates the entry of some non-enveloped virus into eukaryotic cells. In some cases, viral membrane-penetration protein requires to be activated to display its membrane penetrating activity. Activation can be due to receptor binding or the acidic pH of the endosomal lumen. [synonyms: viral entry via permeabilization of endosomal membrane] (GO biological_process)
name: symbiont entry into host cell via permeabilization of endosomal membrane

intent: extrinsic component of presynaptic endosome membrane - The component of the presynaptic endosome membrane consisting of gene products and protein complexes that are loosely bound to one of its surfaces, but not integrated into the hydrophobic region. (GO cellular_component)
name: extrinsic component of presynaptic endosome membrane

intent: symbiont entry into host cell via permeabilization of inner membrane - The entry of a symbiont into the cytoplasm of a host cell, following fusion with the outer membrane, via permeabilization of the plasma (inner) membrane. In the case of some double stranded RNA viruses of prokaryotes this occurs via interaction of a membrane-interacting component of the capsid, leading to depolarization and permeabilization of the plasma membrane. [synonyms: viral entry via permeabilization of inner membrane] (GO biological_process)
name: symbiont entry into host cell via permeabilization of inner membrane

intent: viral genome circularization - The circularization of a viral genome following infection of a host cell. It can be mediated by covalent closure of the DNA sticky ends, recombinaison between redundant terminal sequences or via the binding of a protein at the viral DNA extremities. (GO biological_process)
name: viral genome circularization

intent: modification of postsynaptic structure - Any process that modifies the structure of a postsynapse. [synonyms: synapse remodelling] (GO biological_process)

intent: neuronal dense core vesicle membrane - The lipid bilayer surrounding a neuronal dense core vesicle. (GO cellular_component)

intent: neuronal dense core vesicle lumen - The volume enclosed by a neuronal dense core vesicle membrane. (GO cellular_component)

intent: neuronal dense core vesicle organization - A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a neuronal dense core vesicle. (GO biological_process)

intent: degradation of host chromosome by virus - The catabolic breakdown of the DNA of a host chromosome by a virus. This occurs during infection of bacteria by some phages. It frees up a large pool of nucleoside 5'-triphophates for use in viral DNA synthesis. (GO biological_process)
name: degradation of host chromosome by virus

intent: symbiont-mediated evasion of DNA end degradation by host - A process by which a symbiont evades and ends degradation of its DNA when free DNA ends are exposed. [synonyms: DNA end degradation evasion by virus; evasion of DNA end degradation by host; evasion by virus of DNA end degradation] (GO biological_process)
name: symbiont-mediated evasion of DNA end degradation by host

intent: maintenance of protein localization at cell tip - Any process in which localization of a protein is maintained at the cell tip. [synonyms: maintenance of protein location at cell tip] (GO biological_process)
name: maintenance of protein localization at cell tip

Some viruses encode their own methyltransferase in order to protect their genome from host restriction enzymes. Others directly inhibit restriction enzymes while some use unusual bases in their genome to avoid restriction. [synonyms: evasion of host restriction-modification system; restriction-modification system evasion by virus; evasion by virus of host restriction-modification system] (GO biological_process)
name: symbiont-mediated evasion of host restriction-modification system

intent: maintenance of protein localization at growing cell tip - Any process in which localization of a protein is maintained at the growing cell tip. [synonyms: maintenance of protein location at growing cell tip] (GO biological_process)

intent: RQC complex - A multiprotein complex that forms a stable complex with large ribosomal subunits (60S in eukaryotes and 50S in prokaryotes) containing stalled polypeptides and triggers their degradation (ribosomal quality control). intent: DiaA complex - A homotetrameric protein complex consisting of a symmetrical pair of DiaA homodimers. Facilitates DnaA binding to the origin of replication during replication initiation. [synonyms: DiaA homotetramer] (GO cellular_component)
name: DiaA complex

intent: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to osmotic stress by p53 class mediator - The series of molecular signals in which an intracellular signal is conveyed to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. name: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to osmotic stress by p53 class mediator

intent: GATOR1 complex - A GTPase-activating protein (GAP) complex that regulates TORC1 signaling by interacting with the Rag GTPase. [synonyms: molybdopterin converting factor complex; MPT synthase complex; molybdopterin cofactor (Moco) biosynthesis sulfurtransferase complex] (GO cellular_component)

[synonyms: CoA-SPC; coenzyme A-synthesizing protein complex] (GO cellular_component)
name: CoA-synthesizing protein complex

intent: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to hypoxia - The series of molecular signals in which an intracellular signal is conveyed to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway is induced in response to hypoxia (lowered oxygen tension). The pathway ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered. (GO biological_process)

[synonyms: DnaB-DnaG primosome complex] (GO cellular_component)

intent: stress response to copper ion - Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a disturbance in organismal or cellular homeostasis caused by a copper ion stimulus. intent: HU-DNA complex - A protein-DNA complex that consists of HU heterodimers (an alpha and a beta chain) assembled into octamers along DNA. intent: protein localization to actomyosin contractile ring - A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, the actomyosin contractile ring. [synonyms: protein localisation to actomyosin contractile ring] (GO biological_process)
name: protein localization to actomyosin contractile ring

intent: mitochondrial tRNA 3'-end processing - The process in which the 3' end of a pre-tRNA molecule is converted to that of a mature tRNA in the mitochondrion. [synonyms: tRNA 3' processing in mitochondria; tRNA 3' processing in mitochondrion; tRNA 3'-end processing in mitochondria] (GO biological_process)
name: mitochondrial tRNA 3'-end processing

intent: exosomal secretion - The process whereby a membrane-bounded vesicle is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. [synonyms: exosomal secretory pathway; extracellular vesicular exosome secretion; multi-vesicular body fusion with plasma membrane; secretion of exosome; exosomal protein secretion] (GO biological_process)

intent: lymphatic vascular process in circulatory system - A circulatory process that occurs at the level of the lymphatic vasculature. (GO biological_process)

intent: protein-N-terminal-glutamate acetyltransferase activity - Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + N-terminal L-glutamate in peptide = CoA + N-acetyl-L-glutamate-peptide. name: protein-N-terminal-glutamate acetyltransferase activity

intent: cobalamin transport complex - Protein complex facilitating ATP-dependent cobalamin (vitamin B12) transport through inner cell membrane (periplasm to cytoplasm) in Gram-negative bacteria.
